sources/algorithms/transport_ext_id_v1_valid.scxml new — §4.4 per-control-message extension FULL_ID allowlist. 2-param (t_mid, ext_header) → bool. Fragment (§4.2) extensions out of scope (extension_v1_dispatch R19 covers).

Round 292.decision_summary: R292 lifts the R277/R278/R284 run_demo teardown ordering invariant from doc-only to compile-time enforcement via a six-state typestate sequence wrapper in the new `crate::teardown` module.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/teardown.rs (new, 196 lines) — six typestates (TeardownInitial -> TasksJoined -> TokenDropped -> CloseEmitted -> ActionsDropped -> WriterDrained) with consume-self transitions encode the canonical chain. Per-step doc-comments anchor each transition to its originating round: TeardownInitial::abort_sweep_join_tasks owns R264 sweep_task.abort + R121e 200ms publisher/query/declare task join; TasksJoined::drop_liveliness_token owns R277 token_rx receive + RAII drop that enqueues Declare(UndeclToken) on the writer channel; TokenDropped::emit_close_if_cancelled owns R284 graceful Close(Generic) emit gated on was_cancelled; CloseEmitted::drop_actions owns Arc<SessionLinkActions> drop so the writer-task mpsc sender clones drain; ActionsDropped::drain_writer owns the 50ms writer_handle drain. Reaching WriterDrained is the compile-time witness that all seven steps ran in order.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs — pre-R292 inline Step 2-7 body (sweep_task.abort + 3x 200ms task join + token_rx receive+drop + outcome.is_none() Close emit + drop(actions) + 50ms writer_handle drain, ~80 lines of doc-comment-anchored R264/R277/R284 invariants) replaced by the fluent typestate chain. The R292 call-site binding `let _: teardown::WriterDrained = TeardownInitial { ... }.abort_sweep_join_tasks().await.drop_liveliness_token().await.emit_close_if_cancelled().drop_actions().drain_writer().await;` makes the canonical-order witness explicit. run_demo's outer doc-comment redirects readers to crate::teardown for per-step rationale; module-level doc-comment updated to advertise R292 invariant promotion.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs — `mod teardown;` added so the new sibling module enters the crate root (slot 6 of the seven sibling modules now in wz-ap-demo per R285-R287 decomposition + R292 addition).
Net diff: +257 / -102 across 3 files; the runner.rs side shrinks by ~80 lines as the inline R264/R277/R284 doc-comment block migrates to per-typestate doc-comments in teardown.rs.

The typestate chain compiles to identical machine code as the previous inline form (each consume-self transition is a struct move + field unpack; LLVM optimises to the same instruction sequence as the pre-R292 inline body).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — SessionLinkActions struct: `last_inbound_keepalive_at` + `established_at` retyped from `Mutex<Option<Instant>>` to `Mutex<Option<u64>>` (storage is now u64 ms since the shared monotonic epoch); new `pub clock: TokioTime` field carries the shared epoch. `SessionLinkActions::new` signature gains a `clock: TokioTime` parameter so production callers (runner.rs) thread the same `TokioTime` value to actions + drive_session for R263 single-shared-epoch invariant. Doc-comments rewritten across both fields + the new field.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — `check_lease_deadline` signature: `now: Instant` -> `now_ms: u64`. Body rewritten as pure u64 arithmetic: `lease_ms` is the `lease` field times 1000 when `lease_in_seconds`, otherwise as-is; baseline is `max(established_ms, keepalive_ms)`; comparator is `now_ms.saturating_sub(stamp_ms) >= lease_ms`. The `Duration::from_secs/from_millis` calls retired.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — `drive_session_until_terminal` body: `lease_ms` + `lease_deadline_ms: Option<u64>` (`stamp_ms.map(|s| s.saturating_add(lease_ms))`), `remaining_ms = deadline_ms.saturating_sub(now_ms)` for the `clock.sleep(remaining_ms)` race arm, and the lease-branch `check_lease_deadline(actions, engine, clock.now_monotonic_ms())` call. The R260 doc-comment paragraph that flagged the storage migration as a `future round` carry is updated to record the R294 closure.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs imports: `std::time::{Duration, Instant}` retired (the file no longer references either); `crate::runtime_impl::TokioTime` added for the new struct field type.

The pre-existing `session_clock = TokioTime::new()` value at run_demo scope is threaded into the actions ctor so the actions' clock matches the drive_session_until_terminal `clock` param + the sweep_task / spawn_background_tasks clones. R294 textbook: one TokioTime per session, shared by every consumer.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs tests + 10 test files in crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/ + 2 layer3 integration tests in crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/ — 33 `SessionLinkActions::new` call sites get a `TokioTime::new()` 3rd argument via a single perl regex (balanced-parens aware: `s/SessionLinkActions::new\(([^()]*(?:\([^()]*\)[^()]*)*)\)/SessionLinkActions::new($1, TokioTime::new())/g`). Round 296.decision_summary: R296 closes R293-carry (b) two-side $* matcher — lead/trail anchor pair is exact (zenoh-pico intersects-mode equivalent), not an over-approximation; +8 verify tests + chunk_intersects doc-comment correction.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::chunk_intersects — the (true, true) branch's doc-comment and the surrounding `keyexpr_intersect_patterns` doc are rewritten. The previous text labelled the lead/trail anchor pair check as `R293 over-approximation for two-side `$*`` and pointed at zenoh-pico's `_z_chunk_intersect_left_with_right_substar_substar` as the carry refinement. R296 closure: the lead/trail anchor pair is the exact necessary-and-sufficient condition. Middle `$*`-separated sub-parts on both sides always admit a common chunk literal via alternating interleaving (any two ordered sub-part sequences `[A1..AN]` and `[B1..BM]` are realised by `A1 B1 A2 B2 …`, with each side independently `$*`-floating its own sub-parts). zenoh-pico's `chunk_special_intersects` reaches the same answer through the `right contains $*` over-approximation branch (line 156 of `keyexpr_match_template.h`); every (true, true) input lands there because by precondition both chunks carry at least one `$*`. So wz's algorithm and zenoh-pico's intersects-mode chunk matcher agree on every (true, true) input under canonical wire form.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::tests — 8 new verification tests pinning the exact algorithm boundary: `intersect_dsl_both_sides_lead_anchor_mismatch_rejects` (byte-distinct lead anchors `A` vs `B`), `..._trail_anchor_mismatch_rejects` (byte-distinct trail anchors), `..._lead_prefix_compatible_accepts` (lead `A` is a prefix of `AB`), `..._trail_suffix_compatible_accepts` (trail `C` is a suffix of `BC`), `..._middle_sub_parts_always_fit` ([A,B] vs [B,A] interleave in `BABA`), `..._distinct_middles_accept` (`$*ABC$*` ∩ `$*XYZ$*` shares `ABCXYZ`), `..._lead_prefix_with_trail_suffix_overlap` (combined prefix + suffix anchor checks), `..._byte_overlap_lead_rejects` (`AB` vs `AX` share first byte but diverge — neither is a prefix). The pre-existing `intersect_dsl_both_sides_over_approx_documented` is renamed to `intersect_dsl_both_sides_lead_trail_anchor` and its body retained as the trivial `pre$*` ∩ `$*post` case; net wz-runtime-tokio lib test growth 562 → 570 (+8).

changes_bullets: crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h + build.rs — expose `_z_keyexpr_canonize(char *start, size_t *len)` and the `zp_keyexpr_canon_status_t` enum. The symbol is declared in `vendor/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/session/keyexpr.h:69`; the enum lives in `api/constants.h` and is already transitively included via `zenoh-pico.h`. Bindgen allowlist gains the function + the status enum; the wrapper header adds an explicit `#include <stddef.h>` + `#include "zenoh-pico/session/keyexpr.h"` to keep the keyexpr-domain FFI surface visible at one site (R297 intersect symbol lives next to it).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_keyexpr_canon.rs — new Layer 3 fixture (~330 lines). 9 tests: `canon_identity_on_already_canonical_input`, `canon_singleify_collapses_dollar_star_runs_in_dsl_chunks`, `canon_lone_dollar_star_alone`, `canon_drops_double_star_after_double_star`, `canon_rejects_invalid_grammar_single_violation` (agreed-subspace cross-validation), `canon_known_pico_anomaly_star_after_double_star`, `canon_known_pico_anomaly_dsl_rewrite_chunk_walk_overrun`, `canon_known_pico_anomaly_double_star_literal_star_aborts` (divergence pin), `keyexpr_canon_wz_pico_property` (proptest 512-case constrained generator). The status-code 1:1 map (wz `KeyexprCanonError` ↔ pico `zp_keyexpr_canon_status_t`) lives at `wz_error_to_pico_status` per the wz module doc-comment line 64-65.

Three wz/pico canon divergences discovered + documented in the fixture module doc-comment (lines 25-66): (1) `**` followed by `*`-shape chunk — pico's case-1 unconditional write + deferred `in_big_wild` produces `*/**/...` instead of `**/...`; (2) initial `$*` rewrite + any later chunk with `*` — pico's main-canonize char-walk uses `c < end` (should be `c < chunk_end`) so the per-chunk validation reads past the boundary and trips STARS_IN_CHUNK on a later chunk's `*`; (3) `**` + literal + `*` — pico's `__zp_canon_prefix` case-1 else-continue path skips `in_big_wild = false` reset, so a subsequent `*` returns SINGLE_STAR_AFTER_DOUBLE_STAR with `*len` pointing at the `/` between literal and `*`, then main canonize fails its `chunk_end - reader == 2` precondition and triggers `assert(false)` at `keyexpr.c:340` (process aborts via SIGABRT — wz peer sending such a keyexpr could DoS a pico client). Wz handles all three cleanly per spec.

Property generator constrained to AGREED subspace — R298-style canonical chunk strategy (alphabet [a,b,c], 1..=4 chunks, literal / `*` / `**` / flanked-DSL) with an in-generator post-process that drops every `*`-shape or `$*`-prefixed chunk appearing AFTER any `**` chunk in the sequence (avoids pico bugs #1 and #3 deterministically; #2 is avoided because dsl_chunk_strategy emits only flanked DSL chunks that stay in case-1/case-2 of the chunk handler, never falling through to the buggy char-walk). The constructive filter keeps shrinking on canonical inputs.

Pico bug discoveries reproducibly trigger — bug #1 (`**/*` → `*/**`) and bug #2 (`$*/a/*` → STARS_IN_CHUNK) pinned by `canon_known_pico_anomaly_star_after_double_star` and `_dsl_rewrite_chunk_walk_overrun` respectively; bug #3 SIGABRT path verified by hand (`**/c/*` aborts the process via assert(false) at keyexpr.c:340) and is intentionally NOT runtime-asserted (would kill the test binary) — the `_double_star_literal_star_aborts` test instead locks wz's identity output on these inputs and documents the pico abort analytically.
carry_forward_bullets: R299 surfaced THREE wz/zenoh-pico canon divergences — wire-interop hazards that affect any wz ↔ pico session where keyexprs containing `**`, `$*`, or specific chunk-shape combinations are exchanged. R300+ candidate (architectural): decide between (a) wz tracks pico's buggy output (lossy but interop-safe), (b) wz adds an inbound-side normalization shim that fixes pico's output before storage, or (c) wz upstreams patches to zenoh-pico (best long-term, requires merge cycle). User confirmation needed — architectural decision with cross-repo coordination if option (c).

Bug #3 (`**` + literal + `*` SIGABRT path) is a DoS risk: a malicious or buggy wz peer sending such a keyexpr to a pico client triggers a process abort. wz-side mitigation: caller MUST canonize_keyexpr() before sending Declare(DeclKexpr) so the post-canon string can never trip pico's assert. Add a pre-send canonize-or-reject gate in wz's send-declare path as R300+ candidate.

Three wz/pico canon divergences discovered + documented in the fixture module doc-comment (lines 25-66): (1) `**` followed by `*`-shape chunk — pico's case-1 unconditional write + deferred `in_big_wild` produces `*/**/...` instead of `**/...`; (2) initial `$*` rewrite + any later chunk with `*` — pico's main-canonize char-walk uses `c < end` (should be `c < chunk_end`) so the per-chunk validation reads past the boundary and trips STARS_IN_CHUNK on a later chunk's `*`; (3) `**` + literal + `*` — pico's `__zp_canon_prefix` case-1 else-continue path skips `in_big_wild = false` reset, so a subsequent `*` returns SINGLE_STAR_AFTER_DOUBLE_STAR with `*len` pointing at the `/` between literal and `*`, then main canonize fails its `chunk_end - reader == 2` precondition and triggers `assert(false)` at `keyexpr.c:340` (process aborts via SIGABRT — wz peer sending such a keyexpr could DoS a pico client). Wz handles all three cleanly per spec.

Property generator constrained to AGREED subspace — R298-style canonical chunk strategy (alphabet [a,b,c], 1..=4 chunks, literal / `*` / `**` / flanked-DSL) with an in-generator post-process that drops every `*`-shape or `$*`-prefixed chunk appearing AFTER any `**` chunk in the sequence (avoids pico bugs #1 and #3 deterministically; #2 is avoided because dsl_chunk_strategy emits only flanked DSL chunks that stay in case-1/case-2 of the chunk handler, never falling through to the buggy char-walk). The constructive filter keeps shrinking on canonical inputs.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/keyexpr_canon.rs — adds `OutboundKeyexprError` enum (NotCanonical(KeyexprCanonError) + PicoBugThreeFamily { keyexpr, offending_chunk }) and `check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe(input: &str) -> Result<(), OutboundKeyexprError>`. The gate first runs canonize_keyexpr for structural validity, then walks chunks with a 2-flag state machine (seen_double_star + seen_literal_after_double_star, reset on every fresh `**` chunk). Reject fires when both flags are set and the current chunk's canonical form is `*`-shape (single `*`, `**`, or any `$*`-only run via `chunk_canonizes_to_star_shape` private helper). Conservative scope: also rejects trailing `**` after a literal-after-`**` segment (`**/a/**` etc.) — R299 fixture empirically pins SIGABRT only for trailing `*`/`$*` (cannot cross-validate `**` trailing without process abort), but the underlying `in_big_wild` stale-state mechanism does not distinguish the closer's exact star-shape. False-positive zone documented; narrowing pending empirical fork-based pico abort probe.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/tasks.rs — declare_task and publisher_task callsites for send_declare_subscriber/queryable/keyexpr + session.declare_token now `if let Err(e) = ...` → log::warn + eprintln + early return (CLI bad-input path, no panic). Mirrors the argv-eager path so library API users still get the same gate at the runtime layer.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/r300_outbound_keyexpr_gate.rs — new Layer E fixture (4 tests, all #[ignore = "binary-dep e2e ..."]). Pins exit-code 2 + stderr diagnostic for the 3 R299 bug #3 family inputs via --declare-subscriber, plus uniform gate firing across --declare-queryable / --declare-token, plus structural reject path (empty chunk). Uses --connect 127.0.0.1:1 (unreachable target) so the argv-eager gate fires before any connect attempt — fast + peer-independent.
publishable_verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace — 589 lib tests pass / 0 fail (was 579 pre-R300; +10 = 9 SessionLinkActions gate tests + 1 reconstruct shape table test). 23 keyexpr_canon tests pass (was 15 pre-R300; +8 R300-specific). Layer E `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test r300_outbound_keyexpr_gate -- --ignored` — 4 pass / 0 fail in <1s (no peer dependency).

cargo build --workspace --tests — clean across wz-runtime-tokio, wz-runtime-tokio-test-support, wz-ap-demo, wz-integration-tests. Cascade scope: 13 declare_token + 23 send_declare_keyexpr test callsites + 4 wz-ap-demo prod callsites, all updated to handle Result.

validate_workspace baseline preserved — docs=12/12, T1 orphan total=0 (ledger=1 R193 known-stale unchanged), round-trip mandatory=12/12, T3 warn=855 / T4 info=427 unchanged, atomic ledger entries=298/sections=215/sync. R300 commit pre-commit hook passed.

Gate semantic correctness — R299 fixture 3 bug #3 cases (`**/c/*`, `**/foo/*`, `**/a/b/*`) reject; bug #1 cases (`**/*`, `home/**/*/temp`, `**/$*/temp`) pass (no false positive; wz canon converts these to safe wire form internally per R221, separate wire-drift handling deferred to R301+). Cross-boundary case verified: prefix `**` registered via send_declare_keyexpr, suffix `/c/*` via send_declare_subscriber → gate reports reconstructed full keyexpr `**/c/*` in the error (a suffix-only check would have missed this — the gate's raison d'etre).

No regression on R299 layer3_keyexpr_canon fixture (the 8 documented divergence pins + proptest 512-case property continue to pass — R300 added a separate safety layer above canonize_keyexpr without touching canonize_keyexpr itself, preserving R221 spec-mirror contract intact).
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R299 carry #1 (DoS mitigation gate) — CLOSED by R300.

R299 carry #2 (other wz/pico equivalence inventory) — still open; recommend R301 to grep wz-runtime-tokio for `mirror` / `equivalent` / `zenoh-pico's` doc-comments and inventory each module's empirical re-verification need. R299 retrospect lesson: every 'functionally equivalent' claim deserves an R299-style cross-validation fixture.

R299 carry #3 (wz↔pico canon divergence handling — bug #1 wire-interop drift) — still open; R300 narrowed scope to SIGABRT-only, leaving bug #1 family allowed. Decision among (a) wz traces pico bug / (b) wz inbound normalization shim / (c) zenoh-pico upstream patch still requires user input.

R300 conservative-reject false-positive zone (`**/a/**`-shape inputs are semantically valid zenoh keyexpr — 'a appears somewhere' — but the gate rejects them defensively). Empirical SIGABRT verification via a fork()/wait()-based pico subprocess probe would let R301+ narrow the gate to the literal-trailing-* subset. Currently conservative.

wz-ap-demo eager argv gate is DECLARE-side only. R301 could evaluate whether --key / --queryable / --query / --liveliness-subscribe (receive-side keyexprs) should also be argv-validated for grammar correctness (not pico-safety — they never leave wz) so CLI users get the same UX as DECLARE flags. Likely a low-effort UX tweak, not a correctness concern.

changes_bullets: crates/wz/ new top-level facade crate. Cargo.toml ~600 lines with [features] table holding 144 atomic + 19 domain-aggregate + 6 preset = 169 entries (plus default=[]). lib.rs minimal facade with #![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)] so preset-mcu-* (no_std) flows through. No [dependencies] yet — features compile to no-op labels at R302a; downstream gating lands R302b+ as modules move into the facade.
144 atomic features named <domain>-<capability> kebab-case per R301 inventory. Identical id set, zero renames. Source of truth = inventory entries; Cargo.toml is the mechanical projection.

19 domain-aggregate features `domain-<name>` = union of each domain's atomic set. Granularity layer between hand-picking atomic and pick-a-preset. Used as `cargo add wz --features domain-pubsub` for whole-domain opt-in.

6 preset features as EXPLICIT per-preset atomic lists; no preset-extends-preset. Rationale: v0.1.0 is a frozen semver contract — atomic catalog growth cannot silently shift preset membership. Counts: preset-mcu-minimal=36 / preset-mcu-extended=59 / preset-ap-client=67 / preset-ap-router=80 / preset-ap-full=131 / preset-zenoh-cpp=118.

Implication edges encoded only where inventory reason field says 'requires X' / 'builds on X': attachment-encoding-aware→attachment-bytes; declare-keyexpr→keyexpr-mapping; pubsub-attachment→attachment-bytes; pubsub-priority→session-extqos; query-attachment→attachment-bytes; liveliness-get→query-get; liveliness-historical-samples→liveliness-history; codec-fragment→transport-fragmentation; codec-join→session-multicast; link-fragment→transport-fragmentation; locator-{quic,serial,tls,unixsock,vsock,ws}→transport-link-{same}; runtime-tokio-uring→runtime-tokio; scouting-gossip→routing-router; scouting-multicast→transport-link-udp; transport-link-tls→transport-link-tcp; access-extauth-{jwt,pubkey,usrpwd}→session-extauth; session-extcompression→transport-compression; session-extshm→transport-shm; routing-{failover,routes,static-routes}→routing-router; storage-{history,replication}→storage-backend.

default=[] (no-default). Composable-framework contract: user explicitly opts into a preset or hand-rolls atomic combos. Differs from batteries-included crates like tokio. Matches kconfig / NixOS USE / Buildroot semantics where the user authors the config.

Mutually-exclusive groups (platform-{bare-metal,linux,macos,windows,qnx,freertos,zephyr} / runtime-{tokio,lwip,no-std,async-std} / transport-fragmentation vs transport-lowlatency) NOT encoded as Cargo edges — Cargo features are monotone-additive. Round 304.decision_summary: R304 retires Layer E test harness strict-UTF-8 decode: `read_captured` switches `read_to_string+expect` → `read_to_end + String::from_utf8_lossy`, removing the sporadic flake source.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: `pub fn read_captured(file: &mut File) -> String` rewritten. Old shape: `file.read_to_string(&mut s).expect("read captured output")` — panics on first non-UTF-8 byte the child wrote, surfacing the panic IN PLACE OF the captured content (caller sees the harness error, not the test's actual fail mode). New shape: `file.read_to_end(&mut bytes).expect("read captured bytes") + String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()` — non-UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD markers and the caller still sees the full captured snapshot.

Doc-comment expanded with the failure-mode background — child panic backtrace under tokio's worker-thread pool can interleave with a libc-side `abort(3)` message at byte granularity, producing mid-codepoint truncation. The strict-decode path masked this as a separate panic; lossy decode surfaces it as inline U+FFFD markers in the diagnostic output so the caller can see what the child actually wrote.
No source-level changes to wz-runtime-tokio / wz-codecs / wz-ap-demo — the flake was purely a test harness defect (R215 strict-decode legacy).
verification_bullets: Reproduction context — R302b push to origin/main triggered pre-push hook → scripts/run-ci.sh Layer E → `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor --release -- --ignored` failed once with `read captured output: Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }`. Manual retry passed. User flagged: flaky-1-occurrence-is-still-flaky — retry-pass is NOT diagnosis exemption.

Root cause analysis — grepped `wait_for_substring` in src/lib.rs, found `read_captured` at line 151 using `.read_to_string(...).expect(...)`. Rust std `read_to_string` returns `io::Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }` on first invalid byte. Exact match for the observed panic. Mechanism: child stderr captured to tempfile via Stdio::from; child panic + abort interleave can write byte-granular non-UTF-8; harness reads + decodes strict → panic.
Fix applied: read_to_string → read_to_end + from_utf8_lossy.

Empirical confirmation: 30 consecutive iterations of `cargo test ... --ignored` post-fix. Result: pass=30 fail=0. With pre-fix flake rate observable in 1 of 2 push attempts (~50% per-push, lower per-iteration), 30 consecutive passes carries >99% confidence that root cause is mechanically removed — not chance.

Side-channel verification: /tmp/wz-flaky-1.log (one of 30 captured passes) contains 0 U+FFFD replacement characters. So in this measurement window the child stderr was actually valid UTF-8 — the pre-fix flake was driven by a child output mode that fires rarely; the lossy-decode fix protects against future occurrences regardless of frequency.
cargo check -p wz-integration-tests --tests → pass 1.63s. Build clean.

Root cause is concurrent stderr writes from eprintln! (LIVELINESS SAMPLE log lines etc.) racing with env_logger output — both go to stderr but their stream-level locking is not coordinated. Mechanical fix: route the demo eprintln! lines through log::info! so env_logger handles serialization, OR wrap eprintln! calls in std::io::stderr().lock() for the duration of the line. Either approach is wz-ap-demo-side, R307-orthogonal. Estimated 1-2R.

Estimated 1-2R.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: wz-ap-demo stderr-interleaving e2e flake (~5% per trial across both baseline and R307; 3 different tests observed flaking: wz_queryable_round_trip / wz_initiator_round_trip / wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip). Root cause is concurrent stderr writes from eprintln! (LIVELINESS SAMPLE log lines etc.) racing with env_logger output — both go to stderr but their stream-level locking is not coordinated. Round 308.decision_summary: R308 converts wz-ap-demo eprintln! → log::info! across runner.rs + tasks.rs to unify stderr writes through env_logger lock, closing the 5% Layer E e2e flake measured at R307.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: 11 eprintln! sites converted to log::info!. Observer-callback closures (REMOTE SUBSCRIBER / QUERYABLE / TOKEN DECLARED + UNDECLARED, REPLY RECEIVED, FINAL RECEIVED, SUBSCRIBER FIRED, LIVELINESS SAMPLE, QUERYABLE FIRED) all route through env_logger's BufferWriter + io::stderr().lock() path. Pre-R308 the mixed eprintln! / log::info! writes serialised in theory (both acquire the same io::stderr() Mutex) but the empirical 30-trial measurement showed ~3-5% byte-interleave at the LIVELINESS SAMPLE callback fire site. Routing every callback line through env_logger collapses the writers onto a single Mutex<BufferWriter> + write_all(buf) discipline.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/tasks.rs: 5 eprintln! sites converted. declare_task / publisher_task previously had a dup-write pattern on the error path (log::warn! + eprintln! emitting the same message) plus eprintln! on the success-emission lines (DECLARED SUBSCRIBER / QUERYABLE / TOKEN, QUERY EMITTED, PUBLISHER DECLARED, PUBLISHER EMITTED). R308 drops the duplicate eprintln! on error paths (log::warn! already covers them) and converts the success eprintln! to log::info!. Net: 5 eprintln! removed; 5 log::info! added (3 of those replace removed-eprintln on success paths; 0 net-add).

Integration test substring matching preserved by design — env_logger renders each record as `[<ts> <LEVEL> <module>] <message>` and `<message>` carries the pre-R308 line verbatim. Test fixtures (e.g. wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs's wait_for_substring(`LIVELINESS SAMPLE PUT`)) match the substring inside the env_logger-prefixed line without modification.

The R310 shape called the getter twice across the two cfg branches (once binding to `peer_table`, once binding to `_peer_table`) purely to suppress the unused-variable lint when every consumer arm is gated off.

Round 310.5c.decision_summary: R310.5c restores Publisher/Querier/aliased get_matching_status signatures to always-visible; body branches on declare-* feature and returns matching:false default when off (zenoh-cpp parity).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Querier::get_matching_status (line 1945) loses its method-level `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")]`. The signature is now always visible whenever `Querier` exists (i.e. whenever `feature = "query-get"` is enabled — the `impl Querier` block-level gate). The body branches: `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")] let matching = { ... obs.remote_queryables.has_matching(&self.keyexpr) };` and `#[cfg(not(feature = "declare-queryable"))] let matching = false;`. The rustdoc records the R310.5c rationale (zenoh-cpp API parity, conservative-false default).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:QuerierAliased::get_matching_status (line 2082) loses its method-level cfg. The `UnknownMapping(id)` validation (resolve_outbound_mapping + ok_or) still always fires — callers see the declare-before-query invariant regardless of feature subset. Only the registry consult is gated; on the success path the method returns `Ok(MatchingStatus{matching:false})` when declare-queryable is off. The composed `_effective_keyexpr` binding takes a leading underscore so the unused-warning is silenced when the registry consult branch is elided.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Publisher::get_matching_status (line 2195) loses its `#[cfg(feature = "declare-subscriber")]`. Same shape: signature always visible (Publisher itself has no cfg gate), body branches on declare-subscriber, conservative false-default when off. The rustdoc records the same R310.5c parity rationale.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:PublisherAliased::get_matching_status (line 2287) loses its method-level cfg. UnknownMapping validation always fires; registry consult body-gated on declare-subscriber; `_effective_keyexpr` underscore-prefix for the elided-branch warning suppression.

Net effect: under `--no-default-features` (no declare-queryable, no declare-subscriber), `Publisher::get_matching_status` and `PublisherAliased::get_matching_status` are now callable (always returning `matching:false`); Querier/QuerierAliased::get_matching_status are callable iff `query-get` is enabled. This matches the zenoh-cpp shape where every Publisher / Publisher_alias / Querier / Querier_alias instance has a `get_matching_status()` method that always answers — whether the runtime actually tracks matching is a build-time question, not an API-surface question.

5 typestate (TeardownInitial, TasksJoined, TokenDropped, CloseEmitted, ActionsDropped) 모두에 `clock: TokioTime` 필드 추가. 각 typestate transition (.abort_sweep_join_tasks / .drop_liveliness_token / .emit_close_if_cancelled / .drop_actions)에서 다음 state로 clock forward.

tokio::time::timeout 5 사이트 모두 `self.clock.timeout(ms, fut).await` 형태로 전환 — abort_sweep_join_tasks 의 publisher / query / declare handle 3 timeouts (각 200ms), drop_liveliness_token 의 token_rx timeout (200ms), drain_writer 의 writer_handle timeout (50ms). 타이멃 예산 값 동일, tokio::time::timeout 직접 호출 0.

wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs L732 TeardownInitial 구조체 생성자에 `clock: session_clock` 필드 추가 — 기존 R263 session_clock (single TokioTime instance 이미 존재) 그대로 forward. session_clock은 declare_task / query_task / sweep_task 에서 이미 참조하는 공유 clock; teardown이 동일 인스턴스를 보면 monotonic epoch 일관성 유지.

doc-comment에 R311ad 명시 — TeardownInitial.clock 필드의 doc은 'Concrete TokioTime here because the ap-demo binary is AP-only; the Session<T: TimeSource> reparam round will generalise this to T: TimeSource' 명시.

carry_forward_bullets: **Layer E first-run flake 알림** — R311ad cargo fmt rebuild 직후 첫 run-ci.sh 에서 Layer E (wz_publisher_round_trip_against_zenoh_pico_z_sub) FAIL 1회, 재실행 PASS. [[feedback_no_flaky_ever]] 명시: retry pass = 진단 면제 X. R311ae 명시적 작업으로 root cause mechanical 제거 필요. 가설: cargo fmt 후 wz-ap-demo binary rebuild 직후 첫 실행은 page cache cold + .so loading + tokio scheduler cold 누적. 해결책 후보: scripts/run-ci.sh 가 Layer E 전에 wz-ap-demo warm-up 1회 생성 수행 또는 e2e test의 timeout 느슨.

R311ae — ap-demo runner.rs 의 남은 §5.P sites cascade. tokio::spawn 5 (146 writer_task / 430 publisher_task / 441 query_task / 455 declare_task / 665 sweep_task), tokio::task::JoinHandle 2 (runner.rs 45 / teardown.rs 38) — 모두 Runtime trait method / GAT 적용 대상. 하지만 R: Runtime generic 도입이 필요 — Session¬ 는 아직 R:Runtime 안 받고 SessionLinkActions도 R 안 받음. 몇몇 site는 wz-ap-demo 내부에서 R: Runtime + T: TimeSource pair를 명시적 generic param으로 처리 가능 — ap-demo binary main에서 TokioRuntime + TokioTime 단일 instance 주입.

Session reparam 다른 경로: 현재 소감된 sites 는 모두 논리적 leaf (teardown). 다음은 ap-demo 내부의 spawn cluster (writer/publisher/query/declare/sweep task spawn 동시 처리). 이 sites는 wz upper layer가 제공하지 않는 binary-side concerns; ap-demo 자체가 R: Runtime generic을 쓰는 구조로 재구성 가능.

TimeSource::timeout 계약 시점 (R311ac 단계)에서 API가 owning future만 지원. ap-demo teardown의 5 sites 모두 owned future (JoinHandle, oneshot::Receiver) 이므로 R311ad에서 API mismatch 없이 cascade 완료 — lifetime-borrowed timeout은 여전히 future round carry.

wz facade cross-compile PASS: `cargo build -p wz --target thumbv7em-none-eabihf --no-default-features` 통과. wz/src/lib.rs line 30 `#![cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = "runtime-tokio")), no_std)]` 자동 no_std 토글 입증; R302a "empty facade" 스킠낛이지만 future feature-gate (예: runtime-lwip namespace lands) 마다 이 게이트가 silent regression 막아줌.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/runtime.rs: Runtime trait에 `type Mutex<T>: Send + Sync + 'static where T: Send + 'static` + `type RwLock<T>: Send + Sync + 'static where T: Send + Sync + 'static` GAT associated type 2개 추가. 기존 `## Why no Mutex / RwLock here` 섹션 (R251 deferral)을 `## R311ar — Mutex / RwLock land` 섹션으로 교체; R311w 결정 인용 + per-runtime alias rationale + Session<R,T> reparam HKT-ergonomics objection sidestep 명시. crates/wz-runtime-core/src/lib.rs: 모듈 doc `## What is NOT here (Phase W carry)` 의 Mutex/RwLock 항목을 R311ar lands 반영으로 교체. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs compile_time_assertions mod: `tokio_runtime_mutex_rwlock_bounds_compile` 함수 추가 — `<TokioRuntime as Runtime>::Mutex<u32>` / `Mutex<String>` / `RwLock<u32>` / `RwLock<String>` 4건 Send+Sync+'static bound 검증. `runtime_and_time_compose_in_generic_code` 함수 끝에 `_generic_mutex_bound_holds<R, T>` + `_generic_rwlock_bound_holds<R, T>` 헬퍼 추가 (RwLock은 T: Send+Sync 추가 bound 별도 명문화); R, u32 / R, String 4건 호출로 generic-context에서 `Arc<R::Mutex<...>>` / `Arc<R::RwLock<...>>` 패턴이 mechanical compose됨을 컴파일 타임 증명 (Session<R,T> reparam 사전 검증).

compile fallback 적용: 초기 RwLock 바운드를 `T: Send + 'static`으로 두면 `std::sync::RwLock<T>: Sync requires T: Send + Sync` E0277 컴파일 에러 발생 (shared-read access semantic — `&T` cross-threads 가능, T 자체가 Sync여야). 메모리 fallback 분기 적용해 trait bound를 `T: Send + Sync + 'static`으로 강화; Mutex는 `&mut T`만 cross-thread (exclusive access), T: Send으로 충분.

Hidden-bug pattern guard for future deploy/* crates: (a) build.rs MUST emit `cargo:rustc-link-arg=-T<linker.x>` directly — never rely solely on `.cargo/config.toml::rustflags` because cargo's config lookup is CWD-based and scripts that build from the repo root will silently produce empty ELFs; (b) for embedded ClockSource impls, prefer architectural-standard surfaces (SysTick, generic timer) over implementation-defined ones (DWT CYCCNT on ARMv7-M) because QEMU + many silicon implementations stub the latter to 0; (c) when picking a QEMU `-machine`, cross-check `qemu-system-arm -machine help` for the machine's required CPU family — mps2-an385/386/505 each pin a distinct cortex-mN core and reject -kernel boot on a CPU mismatch.

changes_bullets: deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs SystickClock: TICKINT bit added (SYST_CSR_TICKINT = 1<<1) + RELOAD changed from 0xFFFFFF (~671ms wrap) to 24999 (1ms reload @ 25 MHz). `wraps` field now represents milliseconds since boot, incremented exclusively from the `SysTick` exception handler; `last_cvr` field + COUNTFLAG accumulation path removed (ISR is the single writer). `now_us` rewritten to a double-snap pattern (load wraps -> read CVR -> load wraps -> retry on mismatch) using Acquire ordering pairs with the handler's Release fetch_add — standard ISR-vs-thread lock-free read for an interrupt-incremented counter + an independently-decrementing hardware counter.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs new #[exception] handler: `#[exception] fn SysTick() { GLOBAL_CLOCK.wraps.fetch_add(1, Release); }` — sole side effect is the wraps increment so the ISR stays minimal (no allocation, no locks, no re-entrant work). cortex-m-rt 0.7's `exception` attribute is imported alongside `entry`.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs main loop: `cortex_m::asm::nop()` -> `cortex_m::asm::wfi()` + comment rewrite documenting the IRQ-driven idle pattern (textbook MCU: cycles only burn during work + tick ISR handling, not in a tight nop spin). R311be's contrary comment ('We deliberately do NOT call wfi() here — QEMU mps2-an386 has no SysTick configured') retired; R311bf's SystickClock was the prerequisite that makes wfi() safe (a SysTick wake source now exists).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs hprintln + PAYLOAD strings: 'R311bf' -> 'R311bi' (echo identity payload bytes change but the round-trip identity test is invariant of payload content; PAYLOAD const is still 29 bytes either side).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs header doc: 'Why SysTick poll mode' section replaced with 'Why SysTick IRQ-driven ClockSource + wfi() main loop' — documents the R311bi reload-value choice (1 ms tick = one ISR per LwipTime::sleep iteration), the wfi() power-down semantics, and the double-snap lock-free read pattern.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: add `hashbrown = "0.15"` and `portable-atomic = "1"` to [dependencies]. Both crates resolve under default features — hashbrown ships foldhash + inline-more + allocator-api2 (match std::collections::HashMap behaviour on AP), portable-atomic forwards to core::sync::atomic when native u64 atomics exist (this crate, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and falls back via critical-section on MCU profiles (wz-runtime-lwip already pulls the same dep per R311bb). The version surface is the same one wz-session-core (R311di proper) will inherit when session_glue.rs / session.rs extract — pulling here first means the extraction is a file-move, not a dep-graph rewrite.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: lines 53-55 import surface lift. `use std::collections::HashMap;` → `use hashbrown::HashMap;` (hashbrown::HashMap is the upstream implementation of std::collections::HashMap — std re-exports it via the alloc crate's collections, so the API surface is byte-identical at the call sites: new() / insert() / remove() / get() / iter() / Entry API). `use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` → `use portable_atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` (portable_atomic::AtomicU64 mirrors core::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 method-for-method; load() / store() / fetch_add() / Ordering enum identical). `use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};` retained for this round — Mutex<T> field types on SessionState route through Session<R>::Mutex<T> GAT at R311di proper (the GAT is already declared on the Runtime trait via R311ar, but the construction-side `Mutex::new(...)` calls on SessionState fields need a `Runtime::new_mutex<T>(t: T) -> Self::Mutex<T>` helper which is a separate ratify) and Arc is a zero-cost relabel (std::sync::Arc and alloc::sync::Arc are the same type) deferred to the same round.

Source-side effect: the 4 SessionState AtomicU64 fields (outbound_frame_sn, next_outbound_request_id, next_outbound_token_id, next_outbound_interest_id at session_glue.rs:865 / 900 / 924 / 949) and 1 HashMap field (outbound_mappings: Mutex<HashMap<u64, String>> at session_glue.rs:882) now hold portable_atomic / hashbrown types respectively. AP semantic unchanged — portable_atomic on x86_64 std forwards to native atomics and hashbrown is the same implementation std re-exports.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/runtime.rs: trait Runtime gains two construction-side methods. `fn new_mutex<T>(value: T) -> Self::Mutex<T> where T: Send + 'static` (complement of with_mutex_mut — generic-R code cannot invoke inherent methods on the GAT type Self::Mutex<T> since the trait declares the type as opaque; the trait method takes ownership and returns the GAT-typed value). `fn new_rwlock<T>(value: T) -> Self::RwLock<T> where T: Send + Sync + 'static` (one tighter bound than new_mutex because shared-read access lets &T cross threads, matching the type-level Self::RwLock bound). Doc comments record the per-profile binding discipline and the rationale for not exposing inherent methods on the GAT type.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs: TokioRuntime impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { crate::sync::Mutex::new(value) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { crate::sync::RwLock::new(value) }`. Both forward to the std primitive's `new` constructor (the crate::sync alias resolves to std::sync::Mutex / std::sync::RwLock). No poison state is materialised at construction time — std::sync::Mutex poisoning is a runtime side-effect, not a construction-time choice.

crates/wz-runtime-lwip/src/runtime_impl.rs: LwipRuntime<C: ClockSource> impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }`. RwLock collapses to the same critical_section::Mutex<RefCell<T>> shape per the single-core IRQ-safe model (see crate::sync module doc). Both constructors are infallible — critical_section::Mutex::new + RefCell::new are pure value-wrapping with no allocator or syscall dependency.

Round 311di-pre-f7.decision_summary: R311di-pre-f7 — decision-only round: 4 AtomicU64 fields keep `portable_atomic::AtomicU64` raw across profiles (option b ratified); Runtime trait stays at Mutex + RwLock abstractions only; portable_atomic IS the portable abstraction (option a R::Atomic GAT rejected as over-engineering).
changes_bullets: No source changes — decision-only round per the R311bp pattern (decision_summary records the ratification + atomic store ledger entry; no .rs file mutation). Mirrors the R311di-pre-f6 carry_forward question evaluation: option (a) Runtime trait extension with R::Atomic<u64> GAT + new_atomic + atomic_fetch_add* + atomic_load* methods (cleaner trait surface) vs (b) keep portable_atomic::AtomicU64 raw across profiles (zero added abstraction).

Ratification rationale: portable_atomic IS already the portable abstraction this problem domain needs. AP profile resolves to std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 (hardware atomic instructions on x86/ARM64); MCU profile via the unstable-portable-atomic-critical-section feature resolves to a critical_section-emulated atomic that gives correct semantics on single-core MCUs without hardware atomic ops. Wrapping it inside Runtime adds 4+ trait methods without expressivity gain — every binding would call back to portable_atomic verbatim. The Mutex abstraction earned its trait surface because std::sync::Mutex + critical_section::Mutex have genuinely different APIs (lock + PoisonError vs borrow + RefCell); atomic ops do not have that gap.

New `wz-session-core::source_info_ext` (alloc, no codec gate): `encode_source_info_ext_body` + the shared `pub(crate)` VLE primitive lifted out of the `codec-response`-gated `response_build` module so the `codec-push` body-extension path (`build_body_extensions`) reaches the encoder; `response_build`'s responder encoder re-imports the VLE helper.

Round 311er.decision_summary: R311er adds wz-session-core::locator parse_locator: the mode-agnostic seam turning active-discovered + static-synth locator strings into a typed ParsedLocator{Proto, SocketAddr} via core::net (MCU + AP).
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new locator module — Proto{Tcp,Udp} + ParsedLocator{proto, addr: core::net::SocketAddr} + parse_locator(&str) -> Result<ParsedLocator, LocatorParseError{MissingProtoSeparator|UnknownProto(s)|BadAddress(s)}>.

The mode-agnostic seam: active mode's ScoutOutcome::Discovered(String) and static mode's synth_static_locators(..)->Vec<String> both produce zenoh locator strings; parse_locator turns either into the typed endpoint a link dial consumes, enforcing "a discovered locator is a discovered locator regardless of mode" in one runtime-agnostic place.

Pure core::net + alloc (no std, no socket, no FSM) so it cross-compiles on the MCU static-deploy profile; distinct from wz-codecs::locator (the wire codec). MVP scope = numeric tcp/udp SocketAddr (IPv4/IPv6); DNS / metadata-suffix / other transports surface as parse errors (deferred, not silently mis-parsed).
8 unit tests (tcp/udp ipv4, ipv6 bracketed, missing-separator, unknown-proto, DNS-as-BadAddress, metadata-as-BadAddress, out-of-range-port).
verification_bullets: wz-session-core builds clean; 8 locator unit tests pass under Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace, wz-session-core default alloc gates the module + tests).
full scripts/run-ci.sh 0/A/A2/B/C0/C1/C1b..C1i/C2/C3/C4/C4b/D/E EXIT 0.

Layer G MCU 7-target cross-compile pass — core::net::SocketAddr is no_std (Rust 1.77+, MSRV 1.81), so wz-session-core (and the facade that re-exports it) cross-compile on every Phase W target (G.2 facade + G.5 runtime-lwip OK on all triples).
carry_forward_bullets: parse_locator is the parse half of scouting -> session-open; the dial half (ParsedLocator -> connected TcpDriver/UdpDriver) + the drive-to-Established orchestration are the next step. They are AP-bound (TcpStream::connect / split read+write halves) and reuse the existing drive_session_until_terminal; lifting the demo runner.rs open path into a reusable connect_and_open_session lib API is the bigger follow-on (user-scoped: this round was parser-only).
DNS hostname resolution + locator metadata suffix (#iface=..) parsing are deferred (AP std concern / config tail), surfaced as BadAddress for now.
non-tcp/udp transports (serial/ws/quic/unixsock) extend Proto as those link drivers land.

changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: TcpDriver::connect(addr) -> io::Result<Self> — TcpStream::connect then from_stream; the Initiator-side counterpart to the acceptor-side from_stream, fulfilling the standing open() doc note ('outbound dial flow lands when the Initiator path is wired').

wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: UdpDriver::connect(peer) -> io::Result<Self> — bind an ephemeral local socket (bind address family mirrors peer so an IPv6 locator binds an IPv6 socket) targeting peer for unicast send; distinct from bind_multicast_v4 which joins a scouting group.

Round 311fd.decision_summary: R311fd keyexpr-canon composability fix: keyexpr_canon re-export made unconditional so keyexpr-canon-OFF coherent subsets build (carry #3); feature reclassified foundational always-on (R311o ungated its types).
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: the `pub use wz_session_core::keyexpr_canon` re-export is now UNCONDITIONAL (removed R311cf's `#[cfg(feature = "keyexpr-canon")]`). Root cause: R311o's type-ungating made OutboundKeyexprError foundational (wrapped by the unconditional LivelinessAliasError::InvalidKeyexpr and imported unconditionally in session.rs:134), and the wz-session-core/alloc dep is unconditional, so the module + its consumers are always present — the gate was a phantom that broke every keyexpr-canon-OFF build.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml + wz/Cargo.toml: keyexpr-canon documented as FOUNDATIONAL (always-on), retained as a no-op compatibility marker so presets / domain-keyexpr rollup / facade forwards keep resolving; toggling it changes nothing. Genuine exclusion is blocked by the signature-stability principle (cannot gate OutboundKeyexprError / LivelinessAliasError::InvalidKeyexpr).

Empirical gap: a coherent subset (full declare/query/pubsub/session over TCP, udp OFF, keyexpr-canon OFF) failed with 2 keyexpr_canon errors (session.rs:134 OutboundKeyexprError + session_glue.rs:206 check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe) before the fix and builds clean after.

Acceptor + literal-keyexpr Put burst + drive-until-terminal/SIGTERM + minimal teardown, using ONLY the public facade pub/sub surface so it compiles under the subset with zero #[cfg]. Textbook single-responsibility — the alternative (cfg-gating the wz-ap-demo monolith for subset builds) is a ~70-site cfg-soup the project rejects. Registered as a workspace member in crates/Cargo.toml.

crates/wz-integration-tests: new wz_e2e_pubsub_to_zsub.rs e2e test (mirrors wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs but drives the subset binary against zenoh-pico z_sub) + wz_e2e_pubsub_binary() locator in the common lib.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer E2 (facade-subset behavioural e2e) drives the wz-e2e-* subset-pinned binaries vs zenoh-pico — the behavioural counterpart of the C4b facade BUILD subset matrix. Layer E now runs `--ignored --skip wz_e2e_` so the subset family runs ONLY in E2 (no test runs twice); header layer-list + run_layer dispatch updated.
.github/workflows/release.yml: build wz-e2e-pubsub (Layer E2 dep) + run Layer E2 steps added after the existing Layer E flow.
verification_bullets: Layer E2 e2e PASS 10/10 consecutive (no-flaky-ever sweep): the wz-e2e-pubsub acceptor's literal-keyexpr Put burst reaches zenoh-pico z_sub's subscriber callback (witnessed by ">> [Subscriber] Received" + the keyexpr + the value substrings).

FINDING — transport-batching is load-bearing for FOREIGN interop: with it off the pubsub subset BUILDS (C4b passes) and two wz peers interoperate (both force batch_size 65535) but zenoh-pico's z_sub rejects the InitAck (FSM closes SentInitAck -> Closed; z_sub logs "Unable to open session!"). Adding transport-batching to the pinned subset fixed the handshake. Only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces this; the build guard (C4b) and the in-process behavioural guard (C1j) both pass without it.
wz-e2e-pubsub builds clean (0 warnings under deny-warnings) under its isolated, feature-unification-free pinned subset (cargo build -p wz-e2e-pubsub).

full run-ci EXIT 0: all required lanes pass, including Layer E (full preset-ap-client demo suite, now run with --skip wz_e2e_) and the new Layer E2 (facade-subset e2e). fmt + clippy clean (the new crate + test; an earlier draft's fmt drift + a doc_lazy_continuation in the test doc were fixed before this run).
carry_forward_bullets: First facade-subset behavioural e2e guard lands (pubsub). Sibling subset binaries (wz-e2e-queryable / wz-e2e-liveliness) follow the same single-purpose-crate shape when their planes need foreign-interop coverage; each pins its own foreign-interop-coherent subset and adds a wz_e2e_* test that Layer E2 picks up.

FINDING generalisation: the foreign-interop-coherent subset is strictly larger than the build-coherent one (pubsub needs transport-batching for the zenoh-pico handshake). The other C4b/C4c/C1j build-coherent subsets may carry latent foreign-interop gaps that only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces — worth auditing as the wz-e2e-* family grows.

FOLLOW-UP (uncaught latent): an isolated `cargo clippy -p wz-e2e-pubsub` (the clippy analog of C3 for subset binaries) surfaces clippy::needless_return at session.rs:1181/1331/1433 — the signature-stability query-get methods whose `cfg(not(query-get))` arm's `return Err(FeatureDisabled)` becomes the function tail under the subset. No current CI lane clips wz-runtime-tokio under query-get OFF, so this is pre-existing + latent, not an R311fg regression. Adding a subset-isolated clippy guard requires resolving these per feedback_signature_stability (prefer cfg over #[allow]) first — coupled follow-up.

Open decision: whether C4b's pubsub-only BUILD subset should also list transport-batching for catalog consistency (build-coherent without it, interop-coherent only with it). Left as-is pending a ruling on whether C4b models build- or interop-coherence; the e2e binary pins the interop-coherent superset regardless.

Round 311fh.decision_summary: R311fh wz-e2e-queryable: second facade-subset e2e binary pins the queryable-only interop subset vs zenoh-pico z_get; codec-response-final surfaced as load-bearing for z_get's terminating Final.
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-queryable (Cargo.toml + src/main.rs): single-purpose queryable-only facade-subset e2e binary (acceptor + queryable, ZERO #[cfg]); sibling of wz-e2e-pubsub. Registered as a workspace member in crates/Cargo.toml.

Pinned interop-coherent subset = the shared handshake core (transport-unicast/link-tcp/keepalive/batching + session open/accept + the init/open/close/keepalive/frame codec quintet + keyexpr-literal/-canon) PLUS query-queryable (implies codec-request + codec-response) PLUS codec-response-final; query-reply-err omitted because this binary emits only the Put-form reply.
crates/wz-integration-tests: new tests/wz_e2e_queryable_to_zget.rs e2e (wz queryable acceptor vs zenoh-pico z_get) + wz_e2e_queryable_binary() locator in src/lib.rs::common.

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer E2 extended: prereq guards now require z_sub + z_get and both subset binaries, and the lane runs both wz_e2e_pubsub_to_zsub + wz_e2e_queryable_to_zget; header doc updated. .github/workflows/release.yml adds a Build wz-e2e-queryable step before Layer E2.

The new test gates ONLY on z_get's ">> Received" witness, not its earlier "Opening session" line: z_get's main thread + reply-callback thread race on the shared non-O_APPEND tempfile offset and clobber the EARLIEST captured lines; the late witness lines survive. The two value/keyexpr substring asserts run on the full capture so line reordering is tolerated.
verification_bullets: e2e PASS: z_get logs ">> Received PUT ('demo/test': 'hello-from-wz-queryable-subset')" + ">> Received query final notification"; wz logs "QUERYABLE FIRED ... rid=1 keyexpr='demo/test'" — full inbound-Request(Query) -> QueryableRegistry -> Reply + ResponseFinal round-trip under the queryable-only subset against a foreign peer.

FINDING (queryable-plane analog of R311fg transport-batching): codec-response-final is load-bearing for FOREIGN interop. query-queryable implies only codec-request + codec-response (the Reply emit), so the C4b 'queryable-only' BUILD subset omits codec-response-final; without it the reply still arrives but z_get gets no terminating Final and falls back to its query timeout. The foreign-interop-coherent subset is strictly larger than the build-coherent one.

no-flaky-ever: 50/50 consecutive PASS after the capture-race fix. Mechanical root cause = z_get concurrent-thread tempfile-offset corruption of the earliest lines (1/30 reproduced, 'Opening session...' clobbered while '>> Received' survived); removed by gating on the corruption-resistant witness rather than the redundant early line.
cargo build -p wz-e2e-queryable clean (0 warnings under deny-warnings) in its isolated, feature-unification-free pinned subset.

full scripts/run-ci.sh EXIT 0: all required lanes pass incl. C0 ignore-discipline, clippy --workspace (default features), C1h/C1j/C4b/C4c subset matrices, Layer E (--skip wz_e2e_) and Layer E2 (both subset binaries). Layer G 7-MCU cross-compile OK (G.6 riscv SKIP env-only).
carry_forward_bullets: FOLLOW-UP (now confirmed on a 2nd plane): `cargo clippy -p wz-e2e-queryable` surfaces clippy::needless_return at session.rs:1181/1331/1433 — the signature-stability query-get methods whose cfg(not(query-get)) arm's `return Err(QueryAliasError::FeatureDisabled)` becomes the fn tail under any query-get-OFF subset. Pre-existing + latent (R311fg carry #3); full clippy --workspace runs with query-get ON (wz-ap-demo feature unification) so CI stays green. A subset-isolated clippy guard needs these resolved first per feedback_signature_stability (cfg tail-expr, not #[allow]); the blocker now gates BOTH the pubsub and queryable subset-clippy.

Next sibling: wz-e2e-liveliness (declare / liveliness plane) follows the same single-purpose-crate shape vs zenoh-pico's z_liveliness_* examples when that plane needs foreign-interop coverage; pins its own interop-coherent subset + a wz_e2e_* test Layer E2 picks up.

Open decision (R311fg, unchanged): whether the C4b BUILD subsets should list their interop-only deltas (transport-batching for pubsub, codec-response-final for queryable) for catalog consistency, or stay build-coherent with the e2e binaries pinning the interop superset. Two such deltas now recorded — worth a ruling on what C4b models.

FINDING generalisation holds: each consumer plane's foreign-interop-coherent subset can exceed its build-coherent one by a different feature; only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces which. Audit remaining build-coherent subsets as the wz-e2e-* family grows.

Round 311fj.decision_summary: R311fj wz-e2e-liveliness: 3rd facade-subset e2e (liveliness-subscriber-only, deliberately wz=subscriber vs zenoh-pico z_liveliness; declarer lacks Interest-response R283) + new liveliness-sub-only SSOT subset completing the runtime-crate C4c/C1j/C4d triad coverage.
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-liveliness (Cargo.toml + src/main.rs): single-purpose liveliness-subscriber-only e2e binary (acceptor + declare_liveliness_subscriber, ZERO #[cfg]); third sibling of wz-e2e-pubsub / wz-e2e-queryable. Workspace member. Pinned subset = the shared handshake core (incl transport-batching) + liveliness-subscriber + declare-interest + codec-declare.

DIRECTION: deliberately wz=SUBSCRIBER (sink), zenoh-pico z_liveliness=client token DECLARER — unlike pubsub/queryable where wz is the data SOURCE. Structural reason: wz's liveliness DECLARER (declare_task) emits Declare(DeclareToken) proactively with NO peer-side Interest-response path (R283 carry), so a wz=declarer / foreign=subscriber topology would be fragile (a foreign subscriber connecting after wz's proactive declare can miss the token). wz's subscriber side is the wz<->wz-proven mature path; zenoh-pico is a robust reference declarer.
scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh: z_liveliness added to TARGETS (+ header doc updated).

crates/wz-integration-tests: new tests/wz_e2e_liveliness_to_zliveliness.rs (witness is on the WZ env_logger stderr — a single-writer stream, structurally immune to the multi-thread foreign-stdout capture race that R311fh's queryable test had to gate around) + wz_e2e_liveliness_binary() locator in src/lib.rs::common.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new declare/local_token.rs LocalTokenRegistry — the DECLARER-side registry of wz's own held LivelinessTokens (register/unregister + respond_to_interest). wz-runtime-tokio: SessionLinkActions impls ResponseSink::send_declare (the inherent send_declare encodes via encode_frame_with_declare + send_blocking on the reliable channel). The interest_id-tagged response is the exact shape zenoh-pico's _z_liveliness_pending_query_reply / _z_liveliness_process_declare_final expect (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/liveliness.c:218-256). DETERMINISTIC foreign proof: wz-e2e-liveliness-token vs zenoh-pico z_get_liveliness — z_get_liveliness's one-shot CURRENT liveliness query (NO future subscription) logs ">> Alive token ('group1/zenoh-pico')". Round 311fl.decision_summary: R311fl review-driven textbook cleanup (no behaviour change): extract wz-e2e-harness lib (4 e2e binaries 977->379 lines, boilerplate dedup, subset-pinning preserved) + centralise inner declaration MIDs in the wz_codecs::wire_const SSOT (byte-identical wire output).
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-harness: shared acceptor scaffolding for the wz-e2e-* family — run_main (env_logger + multi-thread tokio runtime + block_on + ExitCode wrapper), run_acceptor_e2e (bind/accept/open/drive/teardown), OpenedE2e (the {session, clock} surface a setup registers into), AbortOnDrop (publish-task stop), session_init_params, shutdown_signal. Each binary now carries ONLY its CLI parse + a plane-specific setup closure (publish burst / declare_queryable / declare_liveliness_subscriber / declare_token). The 4 binaries' main.rs shrank 977 -> 379 lines (+239 harness); session_init_params + shutdown_signal had been byte-identical 4x.

Subset-pinning preserved: the harness pins ONLY the handshake-core intersection of all four binaries' subsets, so Cargo feature unification resolves each binary's wz to (core ∪ that binary's plane) — the harness adds nothing a binary did not already pin, and its source uses only core APIs so it compiles under the core alone. Each binary still builds + is clippy-clean (deny-warnings) under its isolated pinned subset.

Teardown ordering preserved in the harness: the setup's returned hold is dropped FIRST (RAII unregister / LivelinessToken Drop's UndeclToken emit / pubsub AbortOnDrop) before the action senders close the writer channel — so the R283 liveliness-token UndeclToken-before-writer-close and the pubsub burst-abort semantics are unchanged. The declarer's declare-before-drive-loop determinism is now a structural property of run_acceptor_e2e (setup runs before the loop).

wire_const SSOT: the inner declaration-body MIDs are centralised in wz_codecs::wire_const (gated codec-declare): D_MID_KEXPR/SUBSCRIBER/QUERYABLE/TOKEN (0x00/02/04/06), D_MID_UNDECL_* (01/03/05/07), D_MID_FINAL (0x1A), FLAG_D_N (inline-suffix N), FLAG_N_DECLARE_I (outer Declare interest_id-present I). The 12 session_glue build_declare_* / build_undeclare_* literals and the R283 wz-session-core::declare::local_token builders now reference them.

The context-dependent 0x20 N-flag COMPUTATIONS (wireexpr-N vs declare-N vs interest-C all share the bit) deliberately stay local — DRY applies to the disjoint MID enum, not to a coincidentally-shared bit; forcing them to one const would conflate distinct flags.

Builder unification (#3 of the review) deliberately NOT done: after the wire_const SSOT the proactive build_declare_token and the interest-response build_decl_token_reply share the constants; the two are legitimately different shapes (mapping-id + WireexprNonlocal sibling + interest_id None vs literal-only + interest_id Some), and collapsing them into one over-parameterised cross-crate function would be the wrong abstraction.
verification_bullets: Pure refactor, no wire / behaviour change. The layer3_declare (1) + layer3_inbound_declare (3) wire-byte tests — which pin exact declare bytes — pass, proving the wz_codecs::wire_const consts produce BYTE-IDENTICAL declare output vs the prior per-site literals. The 7 wz-session-core local_token unit tests pass.

All four wz-e2e-* e2e tests pass via the harness (Layer E2). Flake sweeps after the refactor: 20 x 2 on the trickiest two (liveliness-token determinism + pubsub teardown) and 10 x 4 on all four = 0 failures — the harness's hold-dropped-first teardown and setup-before-drive-loop ordering preserve the determinism and the UndeclToken-before-writer-close semantics.
Each of the four binaries builds + is clippy-clean (deny-warnings) under its own isolated pinned subset; the harness builds under the handshake-core subset alone (no plane features).

Teardown ordering preserved in the harness: the setup's returned hold is dropped FIRST (RAII unregister / LivelinessToken Drop's UndeclToken emit / pubsub AbortOnDrop) before the action senders close the writer channel — so the R283 liveliness-token UndeclToken-before-writer-close and the pubsub burst-abort semantics are unchanged. The declarer's declare-before-drive-loop determinism is now a structural property of run_acceptor_e2e (setup runs before the loop).

wire_const SSOT: the inner declaration-body MIDs are centralised in wz_codecs::wire_const (gated codec-declare): D_MID_KEXPR/SUBSCRIBER/QUERYABLE/TOKEN (0x00/02/04/06), D_MID_UNDECL_* (01/03/05/07), D_MID_FINAL (0x1A), FLAG_D_N (inline-suffix N), FLAG_N_DECLARE_I (outer Declare interest_id-present I). The 12 session_glue build_declare_* / build_undeclare_* literals and the R283 wz-session-core::declare::local_token builders now reference them.

The context-dependent 0x20 N-flag COMPUTATIONS (wireexpr-N vs declare-N vs interest-C all share the bit) deliberately stay local — DRY applies to the disjoint MID enum, not to a coincidentally-shared bit; forcing them to one const would conflate distinct flags.

Builder unification (#3 of the review) deliberately NOT done: after the wire_const SSOT the proactive build_declare_token and the interest-response build_decl_token_reply share the constants; the two are legitimately different shapes (mapping-id + WireexprNonlocal sibling + interest_id None vs literal-only + interest_id Some), and collapsing them into one over-parameterised cross-crate function would be the wrong abstraction.

Round 311fq.decision_summary: R311fq decouples query-get from query-queryable: the forced feature edge that welded the requester (z_get client) plane onto the queryable (responder) plane is removed, the in-process loopback fan is cfg-gated on query-queryable, and the SSOT zget-reply-only subset becomes a genuine pure getter — closing a north-star arbitrary-composition smell and a SSOT-truthfulness defect the audit-on-pattern carry surfaced.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — query-get edge changed from ["query-reply","query-queryable","codec-request"] to ["query-reply","codec-request"]. The R307 baseline welded query-get->query-queryable so the loopback fan always compiled, but that fused two ORTHOGONAL consumer planes (issue gets vs answer queries) into one forced edge and made the SSOT zget-reply-only composability subset a misnomer (it silently pulled the queryable responder in). Comment rewritten to document the emergent-capability model.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the in-process queryable loopback fan in Session::query (observer.queryables.local_query -> QueryReply -> InboundReply) and Session::query_aliased is now wrapped in cfg(feature = query-queryable); the synthetic loopback Final (deliver_local_final) stays OUTSIDE that gate under query-get, so a wire-only getter (query-queryable OFF) finalises a SessionLocal/Any get immediately with zero local replies (semantically correct: no queryable capability => no local queryable to answer). query_aliased gains a cfg(not(query-queryable)) let _ = loopback_keyexpr since the wire branch routes by (mapping_id, inline_suffix).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the bare use wz_codecs::query::Query and use crate::query::QueryReply imports moved from cfg(query-get) to cfg(all(query-get, query-queryable)) to match their sole call site (the now-gated loopback fan).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — new unit test query_session_local_with_no_queryable_finalises_inline_with_zero_replies guards the invariant the decouple relies on (synthetic Final fires for a SessionLocal get with no matching queryable; deliver_local_final outside the query-queryable cfg). The query-queryable-OFF behavioural twin is the now-genuinely-isolated wz-e2e-zget binary (Layer E2).

No preset change required: every wz facade preset that lists query-get already lists query-queryable explicitly (paired in wz/Cargo.toml), so dropping the implication only changes the arbitrary-subset zget-reply-only case — confirming the edge was redundant for presets and load-bearing only for the composability gap.
verification_bullets: Build isolation (true composability proof): cargo build -p wz-runtime-tokio under the SSOT zget-reply-only subset (codec-response,codec-response-final,query-get,query-reply, no query-queryable) with RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings — compiles clean, 0 dead-code surfaced. cargo tree --edges normal confirms 0 query-queryable nodes (was >=1 before, via the dropped edge).

Real interop (behaviour proof): wz-e2e-zget binary now resolves 0 query-queryable nodes (genuinely isolated wire-only getter); built clean -D warnings, and wz_e2e_zget_round_trip_against_zenoh_pico_z_queryable PASS 3/3 against a real zenoh-pico z_queryable — the isolated getter receives replies from a foreign REMOTE queryable with no local queryable plane compiled in.

Round 311gp.decision_summary: R311gp gc-3a: switchboard static generator foundation -- wz-switchboard-schema + wz-switchboard-codegen pure lib (forge-ast.v1 ingress events -> closed no-heap match, build-validated).
changes_bullets: New crate wz-switchboard-schema: no_std+alloc serde model of wz-switchboard.yaml (SwitchboardSpec{machine, bindings:[Binding{keyexpr,event}]}) -- the single shape both the AP dynamic SwitchboardRegistry loader and the MCU static generator bind to. Leaf data crate, no format backend pinned (YAML/JSON chosen at each consumer's I/O boundary), deny_unknown_fields.

New crate wz-switchboard-codegen: PURE transformation lib (no process/IO) -- generate(SwitchboardSpec, MachineFacts) -> Rust source for a closed no-heap dispatch_switchboard match; parse_machine_facts deserializes only the forge-ast.v1 statechart subset (v / kind / name / external_ingress_events) per docs/SCE_FORGE_AST.md + apis/forge-ast.v1.schema.json. Logic in a pure lib (not a build.rs) so validation + emission are unit+golden testable.

Validation = W3C SCXML 3.12.1 event-descriptor matching of each Binding.event against the machine's external_ingress_events (SCE's documented event-injection contract, drift-proof: SCE owns the reserved-family filter). Build errors: UnknownEvent, MachineMismatch, non-canonical Keyexpr, NotStatechart, UnsupportedAstVersion -- never a silent runtime no-op.

Emission reuses wz-session-core SSOT: canonize_keyexpr at build time (strict-reject where the runtime registry merely warns) + keyexpr_match::keyexpr_pattern_matches (no-alloc, BoundedVec-backed) over &'static str chunk literals. Mirrors SwitchboardRegistry::dispatch (every matching row fires in declaration order; signal path injects empty _event.data). No canonicalization/matching reimplemented.

Both crates added to crates/Cargo.toml workspace members (grouped with wz-statechart-bridge in the statechart domain). build.rs orchestration (shell-out sce-codegen --emit-ast + OUT_DIR include) and a real example machine deferred to gc-3c; the pure-lib boundary means that wiring -- and any future SCE in-process statechart API -- only changes the thin I/O layer, not the validated logic.
verification_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: 11 unit+golden tests pass -- parse_machine_facts (v1/kind/empty-ingress), W3C 3.12.1 descriptor matching (exact / token-boundary prefix / trailing .* / non-match / reverse), generate happy-path byte-exact golden, plus UnknownEvent / MachineMismatch / non-canonical-keyexpr rejects, prefix-descriptor accept, empty-switchboard constant-zero emit.
wz-switchboard-schema: 3 tests pass (serde round-trip, deny_unknown_fields reject of a typo'd key, keyexpr/event field-name contract).
cargo clippy --all-targets on both crates clean under workspace deny(warnings); cargo build --workspace green -- no regression to the existing 22 crates (purely additive members).

Empirically confirmed sce-codegen --emit-ast on a real statechart (sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml) emits ast.document.external_ingress_events as an 18-event closed set with error.* filtered -- the generator's input contract is verified against SCE, not assumed.
validate_workspace: §5.20 caveat added; sections 257 unchanged, T1 orphan=0 (new=+0), round-trip 13/13, T3 warn 862 unchanged, GENERATED.md=sync.
carry_forward_bullets: gc-3b (next): value path -- extend wz-switchboard-schema with an optional payload-decode field + wz-switchboard-codegen to emit a typed EventSchema decode -> _event.data (forge-ast.v1 imported_event_schemas). This is the serialization SSOT deferred from gc-2; deserves its own round of design care.

gc-3c: wire the generator into a consumer build.rs (mcu-qemu-demo / wz-ap-demo) -- shell-out sce-codegen --emit-ast + OUT_DIR include -- against a real example SCXML application machine; this flips the §5.20 "MCU static match not yet generated" caveat.
A future AP dynamic loader (wz-runtime-tokio, std) deserializes wz-switchboard.yaml via wz-switchboard-schema to populate SwitchboardRegistry -- the schema crate is the shared SSOT, ready for it.

Long-term-ideal surfaced (non-blocking, SCE-owner decision): SCE exposing the statechart codegen+forge-ast pipeline in-process would remove the build.rs shell-out; the pure-lib boundary is designed so that change would touch only the I/O layer.
Track2 no-alloc (24-module bounded backing flip) remains a separate follow-up.

Round 311gq.decision_summary: R311gq gc-3b: switchboard generator value path -- typed raise_<event> via generated <Machine>Inject; typed_inject_events gate + EventSchema/codec multi-doc join + codec-superset cross-check; pin c16811a9b.
changes_bullets: wz-switchboard-schema: Binding gains an optional `codec` field -- None = signal binding (empty _event.data, gc-3a behaviour); Some(name) = value binding naming the wire forge codec. skip_serializing_if so existing signal-only sidecars stay byte-stable. Value round-trip test added.

wz-switchboard-codegen: MachineFacts + parse_machine_facts gain `typed_inject_events` (forge-ast.v1 pin c16811a9b) -- the eligibility SSOT. A value binding gates on event-in-set rather than re-deriving SCE's native-lowering rule (primitive-only schema + guard-read); the absent-event case is a build error (EventNotTypedInject).

wz-switchboard-codegen: new EventSchemaFacts + CodecFacts + parse_event_schema_facts / parse_codec_facts -- the multi-doc join the consumer feeds (each imported EventSchema doc + each codec doc forge-ast). Fields parsed as id + SceType (primitive string vs non-primitive opaque). forge-ast does NOT carry imported_event_schemas (serde-skip), so the join is wz-side.

wz-switchboard-codegen: generate() reworked to take GenInput {spec, facts, schemas, codecs, machine_module}. Branches signal-only (gc-3a `&mut dyn EventInjector` shape, byte-identical sans marker) vs value-bearing (`&mut Engine<{Machine}Policy>` + `use {Machine}Inject;`). Value row: decode payload via `SceCursor::new` + `{codec}::decode`, field-map into `{Machine}{Variant}Payload`, call `engine.raise_<event>(payload)`. wz-owned codec-fields-superset-of-schema cross-check (SchemaFieldNotInCodec) so the wire format and the _event.data view cannot drift.

wz-switchboard-codegen: SCE naming filters to_pascal_case / to_snake_case mirrored (forge-ast stays language-neutral; the two published filters are the contract, loud-fail-backstopped, unit-pinned). 4 new CodegenError variants (EventNotTypedInject / MissingEventSchema / CodecNotFound / SchemaFieldNotInCodec). Crate module doc updated (gc-3a/gc-3b, signal+value).

Round 311gs.decision_summary: R311gs: AP dynamic switchboard value path -- registry value rows route to a generated per-machine injector via a defaulted EventInjector::inject_value; one guard semantics across AP+MCU.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core `switchboard::EventInjector` gains a defaulted `inject_value(event_name, payload) -> bool` (the value shape of the same cohesive, SCE-free ingress port -- not a second port: a value injector necessarily owns the one `&mut Engine` borrow the signal path needs, so the borrow checker forbids splitting them). Signal-only impls inherit the `false` default, so the bridge `EngineInjector` and every gc-2c consumer ripple zero.

`SwitchboardEntry` gains a value/signal routing kind; `register_value()` mirrors a yaml `Binding` carrying a `codec`; `dispatch` routes value rows to `injector.inject_value(name, sample.payload())` (counting only on a successful decode -- byte-for-byte the static arm's `if let Ok(decoded)` semantics) and signal rows to `inject(name, "")`.

wz-switchboard-codegen refactors the value-arm decode+raise into a generated per-event `inject_<event>` helper (one decode body, deduped across keyexprs targeting the same event) shared by BOTH the static `dispatch_switchboard` arms (MCU) and a NEW generated `{Machine}Injector` newtype that impls `EventInjector` (signal via `raise_external_by_name`, `inject_value` matching `event_name` -> helper). The codec/payload-union mangling stays encapsulated in the generated injector (ACL); the static arm collapses to `if match && inject_<event>(payload, engine)`.

wz-switchboard-example enables `wz-session-core/switchboard` and adds 4 AP-dynamic smoke tests that drive the SAME machine through a runtime-populated `SwitchboardRegistry` + the generated `SensorMonitorInjector`, asserting state outcomes identical to the static `dispatch_switchboard` tests.

Structure note: the registry stays type-erased + non-generic (no `StatePolicy` leak into the SCE-free session-core tier); genericity over the machine lives behind the port in the generated injector. This refines R311gr's carry premise (which framed the registry itself decoding) -- the textbook split keeps the ACL/DIP boundary intact while the value path still reaches `raise_external_typed`.

Round 311gt.decision_summary: R311gt: switchboard value path handles scalar string/bytes payload fields -- the generated dispatch deep-copies the codec's borrowed &str/&[u8] view into the owned String/Vec<u8> payload struct via .into().
changes_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: new `owned_field_move(sce_type, expr)` threads `.into()` for a scalar string/bytes schema field. SCE decodes a scalar string/bytes codec field as a borrowed view (`&'a str` / `&'a [u8]`, lifetime tied to the wire buffer) but the native-lowered `<Machine><Variant>Payload` struct holds it owned (`String` / `Vec<u8>`, no lifetime -- it derives Clone+Default and outlives the buffer once queued). `.into()` bridges the two with the target inferred from the struct field's known type, so no alloc/std path is named and the one shared helper compiles on both the AP (std) and MCU (no_std+alloc) tiers. A primitive (Copy) field moves verbatim, keeping the primitive-only golden byte-identical.

wz-switchboard-codegen: the typed_inject_events MachineFacts doc corrected -- the native-lowerable schema rule is "non-enum" (primitive plus scalar string/bytes fields), not "primitive-only" (verified against SCE schema_is_native_payload_eligible, which rejects only SceType::Enum).

wz-switchboard-example: the temp_update EventSchema + temp_payload codec gain a scalar string field (sensor_id: length-prefixed UTF-8 = sensor_id_len VLE u64 + sensor_id string length-ref, the zenoh-pico _z_string_encode wire shape); the codec is now a borrowed view (TempPayload<'a> { sensor_id: &'a str }).

wz-switchboard-example: sensor_monitor adds a native string guard (hot --temp_update[_event.data.sensor_id === 'kitchen']--> alarm) + an alarm state, so the decoded value is observed semantically -- proving the borrowed-view -> owned field-move delivered the right value, not just that it compiled.

wz-switchboard-example tests: temp_bytes -> temp_wire (encodes via the codec's own encode_to_vec, a real publisher encode -> wire -> decode round-trip); new alarm test (static dispatch + AP registry) asserts only the kitchen sensor escalates hot -> alarm, livingroom stays hot.

changes_bullets: wz-codecs/Cargo.toml — `codec-push = []` feature added + appended to the `default` list so wz-codecs standalone consumers (no forwarding wz-runtime-tokio dep) keep the previous full-catalog default. Caveat block at the per-feature comment documents catalog truthfulness: codec-push gates the SCXML codegen + `pub mod push` + the wz-runtime-tokio session_glue.rs Push wire emit / parse / 8 build_push_* / encode_frame_with_push / 6 send_push_* methods / `NetworkMessage::Push` variant.
