wz-codecs/build.rs — `push` arm added to `is_codec_enabled` (CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_PUSH env-var check) + `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_PUSH` so the SCXML codegen invalidates correctly when the feature toggles.

wz-codecs/src/lib.rs — `pub mod push { include!... }` gated `#[cfg(feature = \"codec-push\")]`. The `push.rs` codegen artifact still emits under any codec-push-on build (the gate elides only the lib.rs include); without the include the `wz_codecs::push::Push` / `PushVariant` symbols disappear from the wz-codecs public surface.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — `codec-push = [\"codec-frame\"]` declares the body-codec-implies-envelope edge (codec-frame OFF → codec-push must also be OFF; the first body-codec handshake-only-deploy contract slot per the R311g..R311k cascade plan). The wz-codecs Cargo dep gains `\"codec-push\"` in its features list (alongside `\"alloc\"`) so `pubsub.rs`'s unconditional `wz_codecs::push::{Push, PushVariant}` import always resolves — the R311h scope reduction trades full catalog elision at the wz-codecs level for an architecturally cleaner R311m consumer-module cascade. `codec-push` appended to the wz-runtime-tokio default feature list.

wz/Cargo.toml — `codec-push = [\"wz-runtime-tokio?/codec-push\"]` facade forward replaces the previous R311a-recanon `codec-push = []` placeholder. Caveat block documents R311h scope: feature-off = `session_glue.rs` Push surface (parse arm + outbound encode + 8 build helpers + 6 send_push_*) elides; the consumer module (`pubsub.rs` SubscriberRegistry / dispatch_push / Subscriber RAII / Session::declare_subscriber{_aliased} / Session::publish*) stays compiled — R311m round will gate the consumer surface.

session_glue.rs — `use wz_codecs::push::{Push, PushVariant};` cfg-gated on `codec-push`. `N_MID_PUSH` const cfg-gated on `codec-push` (sole callers `parse_frame_payload` `N_MID_PUSH` arm + outbound `encode_frame_with_push` both gated). `NetworkMessage::Push(Box<Push>)` variant cfg-gated. `Debug` impl arm `Self::Push(_) => f.write_str(\"Push(..)\")` cfg-gated. `parse_frame_payload` `wire_const::N_MID_PUSH` match arm cfg-gated. 8 `pub fn build_push_*` helpers cfg-gated (principled exemption from signature-stability sweep — return type is the gated `Push`; same exemption rationale as `encode_init_with_role` per `feedback_signature_stability` MEMORY note). 1 `pub fn encode_frame_with_push` cfg-gated (same principled exemption). 5 private helpers (`build_body_extensions` / `apply_chain_z_bits` / `build_push_outer_extensions` / `build_msg_put_with_meta` / `build_msg_del_with_meta`) cfg-gated (dead-code under minus-codec-push).

session_glue.rs — 8 send_push_* SessionLinkActions methods retrofit to signature-stable + body-cfg shape per `feedback_signature_stability`: `send_push_literal` / `send_push_aliased` / `send_push_del_literal` / `send_push_del_aliased` / `send_push_with_meta_literal` / `send_push_with_meta_aliased` / `send_push_del_with_meta_literal` / `send_push_del_with_meta_aliased`. All `()` returning so the no-feature body is a silent no-op (`let _ = (args)` to suppress unused-variable warnings on minus-codec-push). Consumers (wz-ap-demo tasks.rs publish loops) call these unconditionally regardless of feature mix.

pubsub.rs — dispatch_push method cfg-gated (consumer of the cfg-gated `NetworkMessage::Push` variant). `NetworkMessage::Push(push) => self.dispatch_push(...)` match arm cfg-gated. `use wz_codecs::push::{Push, PushVariant};` cfg-gated (only `dispatch_push` references these types directly; the rest of pubsub.rs uses Sample/Reliability from `crate::sample` which stays unconditional). `dispatch(_reliability: Reliability)` param renamed to `_reliability` with a cfg-gated rebind to `reliability` so the variable is consumed exactly where the codec-push arm uses it. Sample imports split: `Reliability` + `Sample` stay unconditional; `extract_attachment` / `extract_qos` / `extract_source_info` / `EncodingHint` / `SampleKind` / `TimestampHint` cfg-gated (only the dispatch_push body uses them).

Architectural deferral — R311m round will gate the pub/sub CONSUMER MODULE surface (pubsub.rs SubscriberRegistry as a whole + session.rs Session::declare_subscriber{_aliased} + Session::publish{,_aliased,_aliased_auto} + Session::set_own_zid + Session::clear_own_zid + Subscriber struct + impl + Drop + SubscribeOptions + SubscribeAliasError + observer.rs `subscribers: SubscriberRegistry` field) on `codec-push` (or a new `pubsub-runtime` feature). The cascade depth (~30+ .subscribers references in session.rs alone, including loopback publish paths and self-echo dedup) warrants its own round for atomic test footprint per `feedback_signature_stability` MEMORY note's architectural deferral carve-out. R311i..R311k mirror this pattern: each body-codec cascade has wire-layer (this round) + consumer-module-layer (deferred to R311m or a per-domain follow-up).

Implication chain established at the wz-runtime-tokio Cargo features layer: `codec-push = [\"codec-frame\"]` is the first edge of the eventual handshake-only-deploy contract (codec-frame OFF will require every body codec OFF once R311i..R311k complete their codec-declare / codec-request / codec-response edges). R311g's interim codec-frame-OFF asymmetry (inbound parse gated, outbound encode unguarded) shrinks one step closer to coherent.

Round 311ha.decision_summary: R311ha: gc-3 carry #2 CLOSED -- live switchboard value-path e2e: a real zenoh-pico z_put to demo/sensor/temp drives the demo's app machine idle->hot through the production session + observer + switchboard.
changes_bullets: New Layer E e2e test wz-integration-tests/tests/ap_demo_switchboard_inbound.rs: a REAL foreign peer (zenoh-pico z_put CLI) publishes a temperature sample to the demo's switchboard value keyexpr (demo/sensor/temp), and the demo's session inbound -> ApplicationLayerObserver switchboard fan-out -> generated SensorMonitorInjector decodes the wire payload into the typed _event.data and drives the application machine idle -> hot. Asserts the demo stderr line `APP SWITCHBOARD FIRED ... app_state=Hot`. Mirrors the ap_demo_round_trip harness (spawn demo --listen, wait "listening on", z_put -e tcp client, wait the marker, SIGTERM).

Test data note: zenoh-pico z_put -v takes a STRING value, so the wire payload is the literal ASCII bytes; temp_payload decodes a big-endian uint16 from the first two bytes, and every printable ASCII byte is >= 0x20, so any two-character value decodes to celsius_centi >= 8224 -- over the 3000 guard. The value "OK" (0x4F4B = 20299) therefore reaches Hot. SUB-threshold discrimination (a cold sample that must STAY idle) needs arbitrary wire bytes the CLI cannot express, so it stays covered by the in-process fan-out test (R311gz); this e2e owns the live-wire plumbing proof.

Layer-classification: named ap_demo_* (full preset-ap-client wz-ap-demo, Layer E) rather than wz_e2e_* (the facade-subset family Layer E2 drives against wz-e2e-* binaries). The #[ignore] + the non-wz_e2e_ test-fn name make run-ci Layer E (`--ignored --skip wz_e2e_`) pick it up automatically with no script edit.
verification_bullets: ap_demo_switchboard_inbound::switchboard_value_path_against_zenoh_pico_z_put passes: captured demo stderr shows the full live path -- "listening on" -> "accepted peer" -> "session Established" -> "switchboard registered" -> "APP SWITCHBOARD FIRED fired=1 app_state=Hot" -> "session ended: Terminated".

Full host run-ci (WZ_RUN_LAYER_G=1) all required layers pass incl Layer G MCU no_std cross-compile (thumbv7m + riscv32imac) and Layer E, which now runs BOTH binary-dep e2e tests (ap_demo_round_trip + the new switchboard inbound) against the live wz-ap-demo + zenoh-pico CLI.

Round 311j.decision_summary: R311j codec-request wire-layer cascade — request envelope + Query inner body gated; query-* implies codec-request; send_request_query body-cfg.
changes_bullets: wz-codecs/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = []` feature added + appended to default. Caveat scopes the gate: SCXML codegen for request envelope + Query inner body + matching `pub mod` blocks; downstream wz-runtime-tokio session_glue.rs Request wire surface + 6 build_request_query_* + encode_frame_with_request + RequestQueryBuilder + NetworkMessage::Request variant + parse arm.

wz-codecs/build.rs — `request` and `query` stems routed to `CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_REQUEST` env-var check + matching `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed` line. Single match arm via `|` pattern covers both stems.
wz-codecs/src/lib.rs — `pub mod query` and `pub mod request` blocks gated `#[cfg(feature = \"codec-request\")]`. Query is the Request body inner type so they share the codec-request gate.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = [\"codec-frame\"]` declares the third body-codec-implies-envelope edge (after R311h codec-push and R311i codec-declare). wz-codecs Cargo dep features gain `\"codec-request\"` so the consumer module (query.rs / reply.rs / session.rs Query/Queryable/Reply APIs) always have the request/query types available. `codec-request` appended to the default feature list.

verification_bullets: multicast_glue 7 tests (admit-by-src + Close-evict-by-src + own-zid filter + encode/decode) + multicast_dispatch 16 tests (addr-keyed; same-zid-distinct-src = 2 peers) pass; 9 session_fsm tests pass (RxFrame migration preserved behaviour).

clippy wz-session-core (session-multicast) + wz-runtime-tokio (transport-multicast) clean; G.12 thumbv6m no_std OK (dispatcher uses core::net::SocketAddr); G.11-style lwip cross OK (session_drive RxFrame::new).
Full host run-ci all required layers pass (exit 0). CLI validate-workspace healthy on schema v11 (the MCP store tools are dead on v11; §3.2 caveats added via CLI).
carry_forward_bullets: Next layer (separate effort): the multicast DATA plane - delivering a Frame's PAYLOAD to the subscriber/observer registries (pub/sub over multicast), which sits above this transport-level peer attribution.

Tracked: graceful multicast.stop (a shutdown signal into the select loop); slim multicast buffer pool (M0 variant); richer JOIN options (sn_res/batch_size negotiation for full zenoh interop); Layer M real-socket multicast e2e + the §3.4 client-whatami-refuses-multicast guard (Round D).

Round 311jl.decision_summary: R311jl decision-only: zenoh-pico parity assessed (~90% client TCP/UDP, ~70-75% default build, ~50% all-optional); next-work priority = unicast robustness before multicast data plane.
changes_bullets: No code change. Assessed watching-zenoh vs zenoh-pico from zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_* (37 flags, config.h.in) + wire MIDs (transport.h) + wz actual code/tests (2 Explore surveys + direct reads).

Parity result: client-over-TCP/UDP ~90% (pub/sub, query/queryable, declare/undeclare, liveliness token+subscriber, scouting, keyexpr all wire-byte-compatible vs zenoh-pico per layer3_* + wz-e2e-* vs zenohd); zenoh-pico DEFAULT-feature build ~70-75%; everything incl default-OFF optional ~50-55%.
NOTE: the wz catalog active=63/143 (~46%) is a DIFFERENT denominator - it includes non-pico MS3+ atoms (router/storage/SHM/QUIC), so it is NOT the zenoh-pico parity number.

Corrected a stale survey claim: the multicast cluster (Rounds A-H, pushed 340b591) is DONE - session FSM + per-peer FSM (addr-keyed, zenoh-pico _z_find_peer_entry parity) + Join beacon + RX classify + lease sweep; transport-multicast is ACTIVE. NOT 'stub/absent'.

Confirmed remaining gaps by direct grep: batching (only batch_size MTU negotiation, no real msg-grouping), auto-reconnect (comments only), fragmentation (codec+dispatcher present, AP drive-loop + e2e incomplete), multicast DATA plane (transport done, Frame-payload->subscriber delivery NOT wired), liveliness-get + query-source-info-rx (stubs).
verification_bullets: Evidence base: ~/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/config.h.in (37 Z_FEATURE_* flags) + protocol/definitions/transport.h (MIDs) + src/transport/multicast/rx.c (_z_find_peer_entry by addr); wz layer3_*.rs wire-byte-compare tests + crates/wz-e2e-* round-trips vs zenohd; claudedocs/composability-audit-2026-06-05.md.
Full host run-ci was green at 340b591 (this entry is assessment-only, no code change).
carry_forward_bullets: NEXT-WORK PRIORITY (ratified) - finish UNICAST robustness FIRST (client-over-TCP/UDP is the common deployment, ~90%->100%): (A2) fragmentation completion = wire the reassembly dispatcher into the AP drive loop + a >1-MTU payload e2e; (A3) batching = collect N network messages into one transport frame + flush; (A4) auto-reconnect = re-dial + re-handshake on link loss.

THEN (A1) multicast DATA plane = decode multicast Frame PAYLOAD and deliver to the subscriber/queryable registries (pub/sub over multicast) - the layer above the transport peer-attribution Rounds A-H added.
SMALL wins: liveliness-get (CURRENT token snapshot); query-source-info RX (codec exists, add the receive arm); matching-listener callback.
THEN (B, optional - pico default-OFF too): TLS/serial/WS/BT links, advanced publisher/subscriber, admin space, RX cache, multicast declarations.
NOT zenoh-pico parity (pico itself lacks): router/routing, storage, full access-control, SHM, gossip scouting, QUIC/vsock/unixsock - these are wz north-star MS3+ only.
Multicast cluster A-H pushed origin/main=340b591; 6 commits 9625953..340b591. Tool: CLI is R422, store schema v11, MCP store tools dead on v11 - use CLI.

Round 311jv.decision_summary: A1a/b multicast DATA plane RX: sn.rs half-window SSOT + per-peer SN gate (init_rx_seq from JOIN next_sn) + glue Frame arm fans FramePayload to the observer registries via new on_event param; JOIN gains §3.2 validation; transport-multicast selects codec-frame.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core `sn.rs` NEW: zenoh-pico `transport/utils.c` mirror (`mask_from_res` / `half` / `precedes` / `decrement` / `increment`), pure no_std unconditional; half-window SN ordering SSOT (first consumer = multicast data plane).

`multicast_dispatch.rs`: `PeerSlot` gains `sn_mask` + per-channel `rx_sn_reliable`/`rx_sn_best_effort`; `ingest_join` signature gains `JoinSnBaseline` (sn_res + next_sn pair) and seeds baselines via decrement (the §3.2 `init_rx_seq` effect point, realised; re-seeds on refresh JOIN per pico `_sn_rx_sns` copy); NEW `ingest_frame_by_src(src, reliable, sn, now)` -> `FrameIngest` (Admitted / OutOfOrder / UnknownPeer / SessionNotRunning) applying the half-window gate per channel; OutOfOrder still refreshes lease (pico sets `_received = true` BEFORE its SN gate - liveness independent of data validity).

`multicast_glue.rs` (wz-runtime-tokio): `decode_join` full-body decode (decode_join_zid now a thin projection); NEW `validate_join` (§3.2 rejection rules: version + sn_res compat, absent sn_res = own default); JOIN RX arm validates before `ingest_join`; `T_MID_FRAME` arm now decodes via `parse_inbound`, admits via `ingest_frame_by_src`, parses payload via `parse_frame_payload`, and fans `IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload)` through the NEW `on_event: FnMut(IterationEvent)` parameter of `drive_multicast_session` (the unicast `drive_session_until_terminal` observer-fan mirror - one `ApplicationLayerObserver` serves both transports); malformed/unknown-peer/stale frames dropped without touching the session FSM.
`MulticastParams` gains `seq_num_res` (own 2-bit resolution; multicast has no negotiation, mismatched JOINs are ignored).
wz-runtime-tokio Cargo: `transport-multicast` forward gains `codec-frame` (kconfig select - the data plane is the point of a transport; consumer arms stay per-feature like unicast).
verification_bullets: wz-session-core 141 tests PASS (`--features session-multicast`): 23 multicast_dispatch (7 new frame-admission: unknown-peer / not-running / first-frame-at-next_sn / channel independence / lease-on-out-of-order / lease-on-admit / half-window + re-JOIN re-seed) + 5 sn (pico mask vectors, wrap-around, decrement seed).

changes_bullets: `SessionLinkActions` gains `transport_available: R::Mutex<bool>` (initial true): `false` at `release_link` (FSM Closing/Closed entry) + `reset_for_reopen` (supervisor re-dial window), `true` at `record_established_at` (Established (re-)entry, right before the supervisor replay).

Handshake INIT/OPEN/CLOSE + KeepAlive transport messages bypass the chokepoint and stay ungated.

Round 311ka.decision_summary: R311ka session-review fixes: F-1 multicast_put_literal reliable=true (pico Z_RELIABILITY_DEFAULT falsified the best-effort claim), F-2 finalized-staging loss window closed (same-lock-window drain contract + debug_assert; false comment rewritten), F-3 GaveUp-resume e2e pin, F-4 multicast-declarations RX-half caveat.
changes_bullets: F-1 (parity falsified): `multicast_put_literal` defaulted best-effort with a doc claiming "the zenoh multicast default" — pico's put default is RELIABLE (`Z_RELIABILITY_DEFAULT = Z_RELIABILITY_RELIABLE`, api/constants.h:203, multicast included). Now `reliable: true` + honest doc (the flag selects the SN ring + R flag, not a delivery guarantee — neither impl retransmits); unit test asserts the R flag + reliable-ring JOIN advance.

F-2 (false comment + loss window): the F3 `finalized` staging overflow comments claimed a dropped marker "only delays the prune" — FALSE: this drain is a get entry's ONLY prune, a dropped marker is a permanent replay-leak. Closed the window structurally: every staging site now drains within its own lock window (dispatch -> flush_pending same call; sweep -> caller drain — the wz-ap-demo ticker drains `take_finalized` -> prune right after `sweep_timed_out` under the same observer lock), making one staged batch provably <= the pending table; `debug_assert` pins the invariant; comments rewritten to the airtight contract.

F-2 enabler: `prune_liveliness_get_interest` moved to an INHERENT method on `SessionLinkActions` (the `send_response` inherent-twin shape); the `ResponseSink` trait method delegates — sweep callers holding the actions handle need no trait import.

F-3 (doc claim unpinned): NEW e2e `gave_up_supervisor_resumes_on_re_drive` pins the F6 GaveUp-resume contract (endpoint dies -> drive #1 GaveUp{attempts:2} -> post-GaveUp send rejects SendDeclareError::TransportUnavailable (F2) -> endpoint rebinds same addr -> drive #2 re-handshakes + replays verbatim + reconnects()==1).
F-6 (doc drift): `response_sink` module intro now describes the full drain-effect set (reply emits + declarer interest-responses + the F3 cache prune), not just "wire emit".

Reply-before-Final restructure: the dispatch SSOT (dispatch_iteration_event_with) stages each matched request's ResponseFinal as a deferred-fire JOB contiguous with the handler jobs (same observer lock window) instead of flushing finals under the lock — a drainer executes a taken batch sequentially, so per-rid ordering is structural and drainer-identity-independent (an auxiliary query/publish-tail or sweep drainer stealing the batch preserves it); observer grows flush_pending_replies + take_pending_final_rids, the combined flush_pending stays the raw-registry / MCU drain

Final trigger fix (live gap, pico parity): QueryableRegistry::dispatch_messages keys the Final on the MATCH count (fire_matching_queryables/dispatch_request/local_query now return it), not the staged-reply delta — a matched-but-silent inline handler previously sent NO Final and starved the querier until timeout (zenoh-pico emits the reply Final on query-object drop regardless of reply count); non-Query bodies and un-resolvable keyexprs still owe nothing

QueryView grows is_local (default false; BorrowedQuery field) — the pico _z_query_t._is_local parity the deferred job routes replies by; QueryResponder::new public constructor for the job-local responder

query/query_aliased local sequencing: the loopback Final is delivered AFTER the tail drain ran every deferred local handler (then a second drain fires on_final) — on_final after every local on_reply, the pico deliver-query-locally emit-final-at-tail ordering preserved across the deferred shape

Round 311lr.decision_summary: R311lr multicast declarer interest-response TX: MulticastReplySink impls DeclareReplySink, DeclareReply tx-item + loop arm, observer flush_declare_replies; mcast has no get-prune (connectionless).
changes_bullets: observer.rs: flush_declare_replies<S: DeclareReplySink> narrow drain added - the DeclareReplySink sibling of flush_query_replies, exposing the private drain_declare_replies. Demand-driven: a single-concern public drain exists only because a consumer (the multicast loop) needs it; the get-prune concern stays bundled in flush_pending (no narrow consumer).
multicast_glue.rs: MulticastResponseSink renamed MulticastReplySink - it now drains two concerns (query reply + declare interest-response), so the "Response" name was a misnomer.

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastReplySink impls DeclareReplySink (send_declare_token_reply / send_declare_final_reply build the owned Declare via build_token_reply / build_final_reply .try_into_owned() and enqueue MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply) - mirror of the unicast SessionLinkActions: DeclareReplySink.

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply { declare: DeclareOwned } variant (gated liveliness-token, the sole producer; it implies declare-token -> codec-declare) + loop TX arm (mint reliable SN -> encode_frame_with_declare -> multicast_frame_or_fragments, reliable).

MulticastReplySink intentionally does NOT impl LivelinessGetPrune: the get-prune concern is the session-reconnect declaration-cache prune, and the connectionless multicast transport (JOIN + lease, no re-dial) has no cache to prune. The loop drains via the narrow flush_query_replies + flush_declare_replies, not the 3-concern flush_pending - honoring the R311lq ISP split rather than stubbing an empty LivelinessGetPrune.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core multicast_params.rs: MulticastDriveConfig (R311ls, was tokio-local) + a new MulticastOutcome are hoisted here as the shared SSOT both transport profiles' drive loops consume. lib.rs re-exports wz_codecs::wire_const so loop crates reach the transport-MID constants through the session SSOT rather than taking a direct wz-codecs dep.

wz-runtime-tokio multicast_glue.rs: drops its local MulticastDriveConfig + MulticastOutcome defs and re-exports them from session-core (existing multicast_glue::Multicast* import paths preserved). MulticastParams + LostCause imports moved into the test module - the lib no longer names either type after the hoist.

wz-session-lwip: new transport-multicast feature (forwards session-multicast + codec-join / codec-frame / codec-close) + a new multicast_drive.rs: run_multicast_session - the sync MCU poll-loop mirror of the AP drive_multicast_session - plus LwipMulticastDriver (the group-socket TX/RX wrapper, multicast mirror of LwipUdpDriver) and peer_key (the §3.2 src-address attribution helper).

The loop foundation owns JOIN emit + RX classify (Join / Frame / KeepAlive / Close attributed by source address) + lease sweep + the Frame->observer data plane (the same IterationEvent::Poll(FramePayload) fan the unicast run_session + the AP loop use). It reuses MulticastDispatcher + the JOIN/SN primitives unchanged; only the loop STRUCTURE is new (the run_session philosophy: structure over shared SSOT primitives).

session-lwip default + transport-multicast tests coexist in one binary (2 passed under transport-multicast): peer_key is lwIP-free, so it adds no second LwipLink::init alongside session_drive's existing one. The real-lwIP runtime integration test is CARRIED (init-once harness prerequisite - see carry).
carry_forward_bullets: MCU multicast runtime integration test (real-lwIP peer-admit over loopback) is BLOCKED on the init-once test harness: wz-session-lwip's session_drive test already calls LwipLink::init (NO_SYS process-global, not re-entrant), so a second lwIP-initing test needs the deferred wz-link-lwip-test-support init-once harness (the R71 / session_drive carry, now due). The foundation's peer_key unit test is lwIP-free and coexists; the loop's runtime LOGIC is delegated to the already-tested MulticastDispatcher + codec primitives + the byte-identical AP RX-classify, so the integration test is confidence-raising, not correctness-establishing - but it should land next.

MCU multicast TX publish seam (app z_put / queryable reply / liveliness declare over the group) is the next functional increment - the no-alloc MCU TX variant the carry deferred until the loop shaped it (it now has). This foundation emits only the JOIN beacon; the data/reply/declare TX paths the AP loop carries (MulticastTxItem + the per-channel mint) are unbuilt on MCU.

changes_bullets: Finding 1 (SSOT): the §3.1 multicast RxDispatch classify+dispatch (JOIN admit / Frame admit-and-fan / KeepAlive refresh) - duplicated across the AP multicast_glue and the MCU multicast_drive loops - extracted to a new wz_session_core::multicast_rx::dispatch_multicast_inbound (+ the MulticastRxNext enum). Round 311lw.decision_summary: R311lw Finding 2: run_session #[allow(too_many_arguments)] retired via a SessionDriveConfig param object (timeouts/role/max_iters), the unicast sibling of MulticastDriveConfig.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip session_drive.rs: introduce SessionDriveConfig { timeouts, role, max_iters } - the static parameterization of one run_session drive, separated from the loop's live collaborators (the runtime / link / driver / actions / clock handles + the on_event observer) via Introduce-Parameter-Object. run_session drops from 9 args to 7 (runtime, link, driver, actions, clock, config, on_event) and the #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] the prior signature carried is removed. The body destructures config into the local names at the top, mirroring how the two multicast loops handle MulticastDriveConfig.

All three fields are Copy (SessionTimeouts derives Copy, SessionRole is a Copy enum, max_iters is Option<usize>), so SessionDriveConfig owns them by value and carries no lifetime - unlike wz_session_core MulticastDriveConfig, which must borrow its non-Copy params (the Vec-bearing MulticastParams). The HandshakeDeadlineTracker::new(*timeouts) deref becomes a by-value pass.

SessionDriveConfig is defined LOCAL to wz-session-lwip (next to SessionRole + run_session), not hoisted into wz-session-core: run_session is the MCU-only unicast loop (the AP unicast drive_session_until_terminal has a different shape), so unlike MulticastDriveConfig it is not shared across both transport profiles. Exported via the wz_session_lwip lib pub use; it reaches the facade through the existing pub use wz_session_lwip as session_lwip.

Both run_session call sites rewired to pass SessionDriveConfig: the session_drive.rs mcu_session_shell test and wz-mcu-session-acceptor run_acceptor_e2e (lib.rs:360, shared verbatim by the host e2e + the deploy/mcu-session-acceptor QEMU bin). SessionDriveConfig added to the acceptor's wz::session_lwip import.

Round 311lx.decision_summary: R311lx Round A: multicast TX emit extracted to shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (MulticastTxItem + multicast_tx_emit, the TX twin of multicast_rx); AP loop de-duplicated to call it.
changes_bullets: New wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (the TX twin of R311lv's multicast_rx): MulticastTxItem (moved from wz-runtime-tokio) + MulticastTxFrames + multicast_tx_emit(item, &mut TxSn, &MulticastParams) -> MulticastTxFrames. The §3.1 TxData decision (item variant -> mint -> encode_frame_with_* -> multicast_frame_or_fragments) now has ONE home consumed by both transport profiles' loops, realising the engine-free contract for the egress half - it was inline-duplicated in the AP loop, the same smell R311lv removed for RX. Module gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc); the per-variant body codecs (codec-push/response/response-final/liveliness-token) gate the enum variants + emit arms; the emit fn is union-gated so it exists only when a body codec inhabits the item.

multicast_put_literal moved alongside MulticastTxItem (it composes the session-core build_push_literal SSOT, so it belongs with the shared item type). Both re-exported from wz_runtime_tokio::multicast_glue via pub use, so the AP loop's public TX API + its tests are unchanged by the move.

wz-runtime-tokio multicast_glue de-duplicated: the inline 4-arm outbound match (Push/Response/ResponseFinal/DeclareReply, ~110 LOC) replaced by a multicast_tx_emit call + a send loop, so the AP loop now owns only the IO (the mpsc recv + the async LinkDriver::send). The emit import + the outbound Some(item) arm are union-gated, with a not(union) `match item {}` arm preserving the uninhabited-item build (matching the prior per-codec import gating; no robustness regression). The encode_frame_with_* / multicast_frame_or_fragments / build_response_final / push_build imports retired from the loop (the SSOT owns them); build_token_reply / build_final_reply stay (the AP MulticastReplySink composes them before enqueuing).

ResponseFinal now routes through multicast_frame_or_fragments like the other three variants (one uniform egress path): byte-identical (a single tiny VLE rid never reaches the budget, so it returns its one frame with no follow-on mint) but it removes the special-case arm and keeps params + tx_sn used by every arm, so the union-gated emit fn has no unused-parameter edge in any single-codec config.

Round 311ly.decision_summary: R311ly Round B: MCU multicast TX seam - run_multicast_session next_tx pull-callback feeds the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT (z_put over the group); 8->7 args via clock-derivation, no #[allow].
changes_bullets: wz_session_lwip::multicast_drive::run_multicast_session gains the application TX publish seam (the R311lu/lv carry): a next_tx: FnMut() -> Option<MulticastTxItem> pull-callback, symmetric with the on_event push-callback - the MCU busy-poll mirror of the AP loop's tokio mpsc outbound receiver. Each iteration, right after the JOIN beacon and before the lwIP pump, the loop drains pending outbound items and frames each through the SAME shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx::multicast_tx_emit SSOT (R311lx) the AP loop calls, multicasting the datagrams via send_to_group so they ride that iteration's run_until_idle. The MCU multicast loop now emits app data, not only the JOIN beacon.

The TX emit + the mut tx_sn binding are gated on codec-push (wz-session-lwip's only forwarded TX body codec); a codec-free transport-multicast build leaves MulticastTxItem uninhabited, so the seam stays in the signature - next_tx is consumed by a not(codec-push) `if let Some(item) = next_tx() { match item {} }` - without an unused-parameter or unused-mut lint, so the RX-only multicast build is unchanged.

New wz-session-lwip `codec-push` feature forwards wz-session-core/codec-push (orthogonal to transport-multicast; a publishing multicast node enables both). build_push_literal needs only codec-push, so multicast_put_literal builds a literal-keyexpr Put with no extra pub/sub feature.

Adding next_tx took the loop to 8 args (clippy too_many_arguments 8/7). Resolved NOT with #[allow] (the hack R311lw just removed from run_session) but by dropping the redundant clock parameter: the multicast loop derives its monotonic clock from the runtime it already pumps (LwipTime::new(runtime)). Unlike the unicast run_session (R263 external clock to share the actions clock-clone epoch) or the AP loop (ambient tokio, no runtime param), the multicast loop has no actions bundle, so an external clock was a redundant re-derivation. 7 args, no #[allow].

Deterministic real-lwIP test run_multicast_session_publishes_a_put_over_loopback (codec-push): a queued Put is framed + multicast, echoed by multicast loopback, admitted at our own source via a pre-injected distinct-zid JOIN (the §3.2 source-keyed peer entry), and observed by on_event as a Push - a true TX -> loopback -> RX round trip, frozen-clock deterministic.

Round 311lz.decision_summary: R311lz: MCU multicast TX seam variant-complete - next_tx gate codec-push-only -> TX-codec union, so Response/ResponseFinal/DeclareReply route through multicast_tx_emit SSOT like Push.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip's multicast TX seam (run_multicast_session's next_tx pull) is now variant-complete: the loop's TX gate - the multicast_tx_emit import, the `mut tx_sn` binding, and the drain while-loop - generalised from `#[cfg(feature = "codec-push")]` to the `any(codec-push, codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token)` union, the SAME gate the shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx::multicast_tx_emit SSOT and the AP wz-runtime-tokio::multicast_glue loop already carry. A queued queryable Response / ResponseFinal or a liveliness DeclareReply now routes through the one SSOT exactly as Push did (R311ly); the drain stays variant-agnostic (the item carries which arm). The not(union) RX-only branch (the `match item {}` on the then-uninhabited item) widened in step so a no-TX-codec build still compiles unchanged.

Three new wz-session-lwip features forward the matching wz-session-core TX body codecs: codec-response + codec-response-final (the queryable reply chain - a reply payload + its terminating ResponseFinal, forwarded together because a reply needs both) and liveliness-token (the declarer-side interest-response; transitively pulls codec-declare so the loop can frame a held-token Declare reply over the group). Each is orthogonal to transport-multicast; a publishing node enables the variant(s) it emits. The application produces these reply items today (it builds + queues them on next_tx); the observer-staging auto-producer is the follow-on.

New deterministic real-lwIP test run_multicast_session_publishes_a_declare_reply_over_loopback (liveliness-token, NO codec-push): a DeclFinal reply (build_final_reply(9).try_into_owned()) queued on next_tx is framed by multicast_tx_emit, multicast to the group, echoed by loopback, admitted at our own pre-injected distinct-zid source, and observed by on_event as a Declare carrying interest id 9 - a true non-Push TX -> loopback -> RX round trip, frozen-clock deterministic. It exercises the union gate WITHOUT codec-push (the case the old codec-push-only gating mis-compiled to `match item {}` on an inhabited type). The variant-body check (DeclFinal vs DeclToken) is omitted: it needs wz-codecs, not an MCU-crate dep, and interest_id is the querier's correlation key while the only Declare emitted is the DeclFinal, so it suffices.

Module + param docs updated: the TX publish seam moved out of the stale "Not yet here" block (R311ly already landed Push; R311lz completes the variants) into a "TX publish seam (R311ly Push; R311lz variant-complete)" section; the remaining "Not yet here" is the MCU observer staging (the no_std MulticastReplySink mirror that auto-PRODUCES reply items from inbound Query / Interest frames - the seam already EMITS them) + Fragment RX/TX + LinkLost.

Round 311mb.decision_summary: R311mb: MCU queryable observer staging - MulticastReplyQueue impls ResponseSink (query-queryable + wz-codecs dep); box large MulticastTxItem variants to fix large_enum_variant + shrink MCU queue.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip's MulticastReplyQueue (R311ma) now also implements ResponseSink (the queryable reply chain), completing the MCU observer-staging mirror of the AP MulticastReplySink: the observer drains its staged query replies (flush_query_replies -> Response + terminating ResponseFinal, reply-before-final) into the queue, the loop's next_tx seam drains them out. So a registered queryable on the MCU now auto-replies to an inbound Query over the group, as the liveliness declarer (R311ma) does for an Interest. The type's gate widened from liveliness-token to the reply-variant union any(codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token); each producer-trait impl stays gated by its own codec family (ResponseSink any(codec-response, codec-response-final); DeclareReplySink liveliness-token).

New wz-session-lwip query-queryable feature forwards wz-session-core/query-queryable (the QueryableRegistry + codec-request for inbound Query decode + codec-response). codec-response now ALSO forwards wz-codecs/codec-response, and a wz-codecs direct dep (default-features=false, alloc) is added SOLELY so the ResponseSink::send_response signature can name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned (the one wz_codecs type this MCU crate references; the declare / push arms use inferred owned types). Mirrors how wz-runtime-tokio deps wz-codecs for the AP reply path.

New integration test run_multicast_session_stages_observer_query_replies_into_next_tx (all(query-queryable, codec-response, codec-response-final)): an inbound Query (rid 7, at the JOIN-advertised SN 0) for a registered queryable is dispatched to the observer, whose handler stages a Response; flush_query_replies drains it + its terminating ResponseFinal through the queue's ResponseSink into the shared queue, and next_tx drains exactly one Response + one ResponseFinal. Asserts on the drained items (the injected Query at SN 0 advances the shared peer entry past our reply mints, so a loopback echo would SN-stale-drop - the same artifact the liveliness sibling avoids).

Boxed the large MulticastTxItem variants (R311mb): Push -> Box<PushOwned>, Response -> Box<ResponseOwned>, DeclareReply -> Box<DeclareOwned> (the small ResponseFinal, a bare rid, stays inline), mirroring NetworkMessage's own Box<PushOwned> / Box<ResponseOwned> / Box<DeclareOwned> in the same crate. This bounds the enum to a pointer (the owned payloads already heap-allocate, so the extra Box is marginal), shrinks the MCU MulticastReplyQueue's VecDeque slots from 700+ bytes to pointer-sized, AND fixes clippy large_enum_variant which the new codec-response/final-only run-ci clippy combo surfaced (the lint compares largest vs second-largest variant; without codec-push / liveliness-token, Response 784 bytes vs ResponseFinal 8 bytes tripped it). multicast_tx_emit derefs the Box per arm; the AP + MCU construction sites Box::new. The `use alloc::boxed::Box` import is gated on the boxed-variant union (codec-push / codec-response / liveliness-token; NOT codec-response-final, which stays inline), so a no-data-codec or ResponseFinal-only build does not import an unused Box under -D warnings.

run-ci G.11 (the facade session-lwip cross-real lane) gains two facade builds proving the forwards cfg-in the MCU multicast loop THROUGH the facade on real MCU targets. changes_bullets: New wz-session-core module multicast_reply_sink (gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc) - the multicast_tx gate): a generic MulticastReplySink<Q> + a MulticastReplyEnqueue trait. The "given a ResponseSink / DeclareReplySink call, which MulticastTxItem does it become" construction (the build_*_reply + try_into_owned + Box::new + variant choice) lives here ONCE - the TX-staging twin of the multicast_rx (RX dispatch) and multicast_tx (TX emit) SSOTs. ResponseSink (codec-response / codec-response-final) + DeclareReplySink (liveliness-token) are impl'd once for MulticastReplySink<Q: MulticastReplyEnqueue>; Q decides only HOW each constructed item is queued for the loop.

Before R311md the AP MulticastReplySink (wz-runtime-tokio) and the MCU MulticastReplyQueue (wz-session-lwip) duplicated those four trait methods byte-for-byte except the enqueue line (tx.send vs queue.push_back). Both collapse to a MulticastReplyEnqueue backing: AP TokioReplyBacking (wraps UnboundedSender, enqueue = send) + pub type MulticastReplySink = MulticastReplySink<TokioReplyBacking> (the public name is preserved); MCU MulticastReplyQueue becomes the Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>> backing (enqueue = push_back, keeps pop() for next_tx). The observer drains MulticastReplySink::new(backing.clone()); the loop pops the backing.

wz-session-lwip's wz-codecs DIRECT DEP (added R311mb only to name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned in its duplicated send_response signature) is REMOVED, and its codec-response feature no longer forwards wz-codecs/codec-response: the ResponseOwned-named send_response now lives in wz-session-core (which already deps wz-codecs), and the backing's enqueue takes the already-constructed MulticastTxItem. So the dep was a pure symptom of the duplication - folding the impl removed both. The MCU backing crate names no codec type.

changes_bullets: lib.rs: the deferred_fire module #[cfg] collapses from all(feature="alloc", any(deferred-fire, session-matching, declare-subscriber, declare-queryable, liveliness-token, liveliness-subscriber, query-reply)) to feature="deferred-fire" alone (the feature implies alloc). The pre-R311lh plane arms were dead weight: no wz-session-core code instantiates a deferred type under them (only doc-links in decl_sink.rs / declare/matching.rs), and the only real consumer, AP wz-runtime-tokio, enables deferred-fire unconditionally on its wz-session-core dependency - so the module still compiles for the tier that uses it.

Root cause closed: liveliness-token in the gate forced `use alloc::sync::Arc;` (deferred_fire.rs:101) to compile on the MCU multicast profile; thumbv6m (ARMv6-M) has no target_has_atomic="ptr", so the otherwise-unused module failed to build (E0432 unresolved import alloc::sync). The MCU multicast liveliness / queryable reply is staged inline through the Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>>-backed MulticastReplyQueue (wz-session-lwip multicast_drive.rs), never the deferred seam - so dropping the module from that profile IS the inline-fire path the R311mc/md carry asked for, not a behaviour change.

Round 311mf.decision_summary: R311mf: MCU multicast Fragment RX/TX - the AP R311kn/ko arms ported to run_multicast_session: reassembly RX wiring + a transport-fragmentation feature that splits TX via the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-lwip/src/multicast_drive.rs: run_multicast_session now wires the reassembly-divergent RX tail through the shared wz-session-core SSOT, the MCU twin of the AP loop's R311kn arm. Under `reassembly` a per-(slot,channel) Router (mcu_reassembly = ReassemblyDispatcher<4,4096>, the same run_session owns) is built before the loop; the FrameOutOfOrder arm aborts the channel's in-progress chain (reasm.abort_channel via peer_index_by_src), the Fragment arm parses the inbound T_MID_FRAGMENT (parse_inbound -> InboundFrame::Fragment) and reassembles via ingest_multicast_fragment (per-peer SN gate -> chain -> the completed message fans as the SAME FramePayload Poll a whole Frame does), and the Close arm aborts the departing peer's chains before close_by_src. The sweep arm becomes sweep_with(now, abort_peer_chains) + sweep_reporting under `reassembly`, the bare sweep otherwise. Without the feature the arms keep the prior drop-Fragment behaviour (pico fragmentation-off).

crates/wz-session-lwip/Cargo.toml: a new `transport-fragmentation` feature = [reassembly, wz-session-core/transport-fragmentation] forwards the core umbrella (reassembly + codec-fragment + alloc) and re-uses this crate's reassembly forward for the wz-runtime-lwip Router. No drive-loop code change for TX: run_multicast_session already frames its next_tx seam through the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT, which splits an oversize payload via multicast_frame_or_fragments once the feature is on - exactly as the AP loop. The MCU TX port was a feature forward; the fragmentation SSOT was already shared (R311ko).

Test run_multicast_session_reassembles_a_fragmented_put_over_loopback (gated transport-fragmentation,codec-push): the real-lwIP fragment leg. A 200-byte z_put at batch_size 64 is proven to fragment (>1 datagram via a direct multicast_tx_emit probe), multicast to the group, echoed back, and reassembled by the Fragment RX arm into one observed Push (no ReassemblyDropped). The pre-admitted peer JOIN advertises batch_size 64 to match self: validate_join admits only when the JOIN's batch_size equals the receiver's params, else the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop.

scripts/run-ci.sh: C1m gains a transport-multicast,reassembly arm (the reassembly RX path composing WITHOUT fragmentation) + a transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push arm (the round-trip), test + clippy each. G.11 cross-real adds a wz-session-lwip transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push build on every non-riscv target - the reassembly Router + TX splitter cross-compile on thumbv6m (Vec-backed, no Arc), the M0 fragment reach.
verification_bullets: Full host run-ci + Layer G (WZ_RUN_LAYER_G=1): RUNCI_EXIT=0 (read from the trailing exit-code line, not a pipe/tee-masked tail). "run-ci: all required layers pass", no FAIL lines.

Layer C1m pass: the new transport-multicast,reassembly + transport-multicast,transport-fragmentation,codec-push arms (test + clippy each) pass alongside the existing multicast lanes; the fragment round-trip test passes (5 tests in the fragmentation build).

Root cause found during bring-up + recorded: the first round-trip failed silently (saw_push false, no drop event) because validate_join (multicast_join.rs) rejects a JOIN whose batch_size != the receiver's params; the pre-admitted peer was on the default 2_048 while self ran 64, so the peer was never admitted and the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop. A direct-drive diagnostic (admit + feed the 5 probe fragments through dispatch + ingest) confirmed the SSOT completes (completed=1, dropped=0) once batch_size matches; the fix set the peer JOIN's batch_size to 64.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-mcu-multicast-e2e: new no_std SSOT crate (#![cfg(lwip_real_build)]). run_multicast_e2e<C>(&LwipLink, clock) -> MulticastE2eReport drives the FULL MCU multicast feature profile (session-lwip + transport-multicast + transport-fragmentation + codec-push) end to end via wz_session_lwip::run_multicast_session: a crafted peer JOIN (distinct zid, batch_size=64 matching self so validate_join admits it) admitted into the §3.2 table + an oversize 200-byte Put split into a T_MID_FRAGMENT chain by multicast_tx_emit + reassembled by the R311mf Fragment RX arm into one Push. Mirrors the wz-mcu-session-acceptor lib-owns-the-scenario / bin-stays-thin split; composes via the wz facade (the R311mg composition-surface lesson). The caller supplies &LwipLink so the host test injects a multicast-routed lwip_test_link link and the bin a plain LwipLink::init(). Re-exports ClockSource + LwipLink + MulticastOutcome (single-dep boundary). Registered in crates/Cargo.toml members.

crates/wz-mcu-multicast-e2e/tests/host_multicast_e2e.rs: the RUNTIME PROOF the footprint bin cannot give via QEMU. Uses wz_link_lwip::lwip_test_link (the sanctioned host-only LWIP_LOOPIF_MULTICAST + LWIP_TESTMODE loopback-multicast affordance) to observe the full round trip (asserts join_ok + outcome=IterationLimit + tx_fragmented + peer_admitted + saw_push + !saw_drop). The multicast-loopback runtime proof's correct home is the host: dragging the test-only lwIP flags into a deploy port + the bin would be a test fiction masquerading as a deploy AND contradict the ratified cross/deploy-port policy ("LWIP_LOOPIF_MULTICAST is host-only - real deploys join on their ethernet netif, not loopback").

deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e: new standalone-workspace cortex-m bin (SysTick clock + 256 KB heap + sys_now + verdict map). Cross-compiles the full multicast profile to a final-linked ELF so it is footprint-measurable (Layer G.11 builds only -p wz, a lib that cannot be sized). main calls run_multicast_e2e (a genuine call site, not a black_box footprint-retention trick); join_ok=false on a QEMU loopback env -> SKIP exit (the bin is build + footprint only; it is a real multicast deploy that boots on hardware with a real IGMP netif). mps2-class only: the 32x1536 multicast rx pool (~49 KB, slim-toggle-independent) does not fit nrf51's 16 KB SRAM, so there is no microbit fork.

scripts/check-footprint.sh: extended with a second optional `artifact` arg (qemu-demo default | multicast-e2e) selecting the binary + baseline table via bash namerefs, preserving the original single-arg Q.3 behaviour byte-for-byte. New BASELINE_MC_{TEXT,DATA,BSS} table anchored to THIS entry (not §6.7, which anchors the cortex-m4-default / mcu-qemu-demo artifact): thumbv7m-none-eabi text=50680, thumbv7em-none-eabihf text=50484, data=4, bss=270100 INFO (ROM axes ±256 B hard-gated; bss HEAP_SIZE-dominated INFO per R311bj caveat (c)).

Round 311mk.decision_summary: R311mk: structurally decouple the catalog-atomic transport-multicast from transport-unicast at the wz-runtime-tokio + facade level - gate the previously-unconditional session_glue (unicast handshake driver) + the Session handle on transport-unicast, relocate the shared reassembly-pool wiring to crate::reassembly and BoxedLinkDriver to its wz_session_core::link SSOT home (out of the unicast tier), and add codec-close to transport-multicast (the multicast_rx Close/abort SSOT it consumes) - so a multicast-only build composes WITHOUT transport-unicast (closing the R311lv facade carry); the cheap transport-multicast=>transport-unicast implication was rejected as an atom-welding smell that mis-states the protocol (zenoh-pico builds multicast-only); guarded by new Layer C4e, Q.5 multicast footprint +0 unchanged.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/reassembly.rs: NEW transport-agnostic shared module. Relocated TokioReassembly (the AP reassembly Router type alias) + reassembly_config() + the REASSEMBLY_SLOTS / REASSEMBLY_SLOT_SIZE consts out of session_glue.rs (the unicast handshake driver) into a neutral SSOT gated on the `reassembly` feature only. Both the unicast steady-state drive loop and the multicast drive loop (multicast_glue) run their own pool instance over the SAME SCE-sourced AP dims/knobs (one buffer-pool policy SSOT, two transports). Keeping them in session_glue made a transport-multicast-only build (no session_glue) unable to reach the pool config - the root of the facade composability gap.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: `pub mod session_glue` + `pub mod session` are now `#[cfg(feature = "transport-unicast")]`. session_glue names the SessionFsmUnicast{Policy,Event} types and drives session_actions / session_timeouts / drive (all session-unicast-gated in wz-session-core); the Session handle owns a session_glue::SessionLinkActions bundle (the unicast action machinery) - so both are the unicast-session API surface. A transport-multicast-only build drives multicast through multicast_glue::drive_multicast_session over the shared ApplicationLayerObserver, not a Session handle. Added `#[cfg(feature = "reassembly")] pub mod reassembly`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/{udp_pipeline,link_pipeline}.rs: import BoxedLinkDriver from its SSOT home wz_session_core::link (the shared link tier) instead of via the crate::session_glue re-export hop. The link pipeline is transport-agnostic (a multicast deploy binds a UDP multicast socket too), so it must not depend on the now-transport-unicast-gated session_glue. This also closed the pre-existing transport-link-udp / transport-link-tcp WITHOUT transport-unicast arbitrary-composition gaps as a bonus (the realistic transport-multicast,transport-link-udp deploy shape now builds).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multicast_glue.rs: the multicast reassembly Router is constructed from crate::reassembly (was crate::session_glue); the tx_sn TX-mint state carries a `#[cfg_attr(not(any(codec-push, codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token)), allow(unused_mut))]` because a JOIN-only multicast build (transport-multicast with no data-plane body codecs, now reachable since the unicast decouple) reads tx_sn for the beacon (encode_join) but never mints (multicast_tx_emit is gated on those codecs).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: transport-multicast += codec-close. The shared multicast RX classify/dispatch SSOT wz_session_core::multicast_rx (consumed by multicast_glue) is gated on codec-close because it decodes T_MID_CLOSE and aborts the leaving peer's reassembly chains via dispatcher.close_by_src (multicast_rx.rs:147,209). A select edge in the same class as the existing codec-join / codec-frame - a multicast transport that cannot process a peer's Close is incomplete, not optional. Previously masked by the default codec set; the facade composability build (no default) exposed the unresolved multicast_rx import.

crates/wz/Cargo.toml: facade transport-multicast does NOT re-list codec-close - the crate forward self-selects it (wz-runtime-tokio/transport-multicast += codec-close; wz-session-lwip/transport-multicast already pulls wz-session-core/codec-close), mirroring how the facade does not re-list codec-join / codec-frame. An explicit facade codec-close forward would be redundant AND would perturb wz-runtime-lwip's feature set for the MCU multicast footprint bin (Q.5) for zero benefit, so it was deliberately omitted; a one-line comment records this.

scripts/run-ci.sh: NEW Layer C4e (transport-axis matrix). The consumer-plane matrices C4b/C4c/C1j/C4d vary the consumer plane on a transport-unicast base and cannot express the orthogonal transport axis; C4e builds the wz facade (the reported-gap shape) + clippy-checks the wz-runtime-tokio crate in isolation (deny-warnings) under 3 multicast-WITHOUT-unicast subsets (multicast-join-only, multicast-data, multicast-udp-deploy) so the decouple cannot silently regress. No cargo-test twin: a multicast-only crate has no unicast-handshake tests and the multicast behaviour is already covered with unicast on by C1p/C1q + the MCU e2e by C1r. The stale "transport-unicast is FOUNDATIONAL / transport-multicast reserved with no consumer" rationale in _wz_runtime_tokio_coherent_subsets was corrected (transport-multicast is now an independently-composable atom).

Decision rationale (why the structural decouple, not an implication edge): the cheap alternative transport-multicast => transport-unicast was rejected as a smell - it would weld two catalog atoms (violating the atomic-features north star), encode a wz implementation artifact as a protocol-level dependency that is FALSE (zenoh-pico builds multicast-only), and leave the real mis-placement (SessionLinkActions / reassembly / BoxedLinkDriver sitting in the unicast tier) unaddressed. The structural decouple is the SSOT-correct fix: each module in its correct tier, the catalog-atomic transport-multicast composes alone.

Both the unicast steady-state drive loop and the multicast drive loop (multicast_glue) run their own pool instance over the SAME SCE-sourced AP dims/knobs (one buffer-pool policy SSOT, two transports). Keeping them in session_glue made a transport-multicast-only build (no session_glue) unable to reach the pool config - the root of the facade composability gap.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: `pub mod session_glue` + `pub mod session` are now `#[cfg(feature = "transport-unicast")]`. session_glue names the SessionFsmUnicast{Policy,Event} types and drives session_actions / session_timeouts / drive (all session-unicast-gated in wz-session-core); the Session handle owns a session_glue::SessionLinkActions bundle (the unicast action machinery) - so both are the unicast-session API surface. Round 311mr.decision_summary: B5b-1 (Level B): the transport-dispatch send seam. Add Session::send_network_message (the _z_send_n_msg analogue) routing a built NetworkMessage to the owned transport send path; B5b-1 inhabits the multicast arm (Push-only, gated not(transport-unicast)) and migrates the multicast publish remote leg through it. The unicast arm + gate-drop + actions() dismantling is B5b-2.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: added Session::send_network_message (gated all(transport-multicast, not(transport-unicast), codec-push)) - the wz analogue of zenoh-pico _z_send_n_msg (src/transport/transport.c:29 switch over the transport tag, called by every put/get/declare primitive in src/net/primitives.c). Takes a built NetworkMessage (the transport-agnostic outbound currency = pico _z_network_message_t) and routes Push -> MulticastTxItem::Push -> the drive-loop TX channel. A non-Push reaching it (unreachable: a multicast Session originates only Push) returns SendWireError::FeatureDisabled, never a panic. The application API stays transport-agnostic; the transport split lives in the seam (pico shape), not a fallible actions() exposed at every call site (the Option-A design I rejected).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: migrated the multicast Session::publish remote leg through the seam - builds NetworkMessage::Push via build_push_literal then send_network_message, replacing the inline multicast_put_literal enqueue. Return type Result<(), CodecError> -> Result<usize, SendWireError>. SendWireError is the SAME error the unicast dispatch_* family returns, so B5b-2's unicast arm needs no error unification; it lives ungated in wz_session_core::send_wire_error, reachable in a multicast-only build that the transport-unicast-gated session_glue re-export is not.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio-multicast-tests/: added the seam-direct test (send_network_message routes a built Push to the channel) alongside the B3 enqueue / B4 loopback / B5a wire-RX tests.

carry_forward_bullets: B5b-1 lands the send seam's multicast arm + NetworkMessage as the outbound send currency; the multicast publish now sends through it. Remaining B5b: the UNICAST arm (route a NetworkMessage to the SessionLinkActions dispatch_* family - those take a closure-encoded body via dispatch_network_message, not a NetworkMessage value, so the arm matches the variant and calls the matching dispatch_*), then drop the not(transport-unicast) gate so a both-transports build runtime-matches the transport - which forces actions() (33 call sites, all in transport-unicast-gated methods) to become transport-aware = the actions() dismantling.
The seam's error type (SendWireError) is already transport-uniform, so the unicast arm needs no error unification.
Multicast Session origination stays Push-only until a multicast query/declare API exists (a new-feature follow-on); the reply messages are emitted by the drive-loop MulticastReplySink, not this seam.
The unicast publish still sends via send_push_with_meta_literal (not yet migrated to the seam); it migrates when the unicast arm lands (B5b-2).

Design note: Option A (fallible actions() exposed at every call site) was rejected for the send-seam structure after reading zenoh-pico (transport.c:29 + primitives.c all route through _z_send_n_msg); the application API must stay transport-agnostic with the split hidden in the seam.

Round 311my.decision_summary: Session-review follow-up (R311mw/mx): add the send-seam gate-skew regression guard to run-ci. R311mw shipped a real compile bug (the seam Declare arm was codec-declare-gated while dispatch_declare is declare-*-union-gated -> absent dispatch in a codec-declare-without-Declare-origination build), and run-ci passed it because every codec-declare lane in the C1h matrix either pins a 6-union origination member (masking the skew) or omits session-unicast (so it never compiles the SessionLinkActions seam). R311mx fixed the bug but added no regression guard. This round adds a clippy -D warnings lane to layer_c1h_arbitrary_subset_matrix: wz-session-core --features alloc,session-unicast,declare-interest,codec-frame - the only lane that compiles the seam (session-unicast) with codec-declare on (via declare-interest) but no Declare-origination feature, so a future seam arm whose gate outruns its dispatch_* helper, or a dropped catch-arm param discard, fails mechanically. Realizes the stale run-ci.sh:846 codec-declare-bare comment intent. No source change.

This is the send-seam gate-skew guard: session-unicast compiles the SessionLinkActions seam (gated all(alloc, session-unicast)); declare-interest pulls codec-declare + the Interest arm but no 6-union Declare-origination feature, so the seam's Declare arm is cfg'd out. The prior C1h codec-declare lanes (alloc,codec-declare ... Round 311mz.decision_summary: Session-review follow-up: fix the declare_token_aliased liveliness-token registration asymmetry (a confirmed correctness bug, pico-divergent). The literal Session::declare_token registered the held token in the declarer-side LocalTokenRegistry (so an inbound non-final liveliness Interest replays it to peers that subscribe LATER), but Session::declare_token_aliased silently skipped that register - so an aliased-declared token was invisible to late subscribers, diverging from zenoh-pico (_z_declare_liveliness_token always inserts into _local_tokens, net/liveliness.c:77, regardless of literal/alias form). Fixed unrepresentably (not test-guarded) per feedback_unrepresentable_over_test: the LocalTokenRegistry registration moved into LivelinessToken::new_held, the now-SOLE constructor, and the struct fields made private - so neither declare path can build a held token without registering. Behaviour change: aliased tokens now replay to late subscribers (the fix); literal path byte-identical.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/liveliness.rs: made the LivelinessToken fields private (was pub(super)) and added LivelinessToken::new_held - the SOLE constructor - which registers the token in the declarer-side LocalTokenRegistry (observer.local_tokens.register, the R283 late-subscriber replay state) then builds the handle. With the fields sealed, a held token cannot be constructed without that registration, so the literal and aliased declare paths register identically by construction (the asymmetry is unrepresentable, not merely tested - feedback_unrepresentable_over_test). Doc cites pico parity (net/liveliness.c:77) + the late-subscriber replay consequence.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: declare_token (literal) now calls LivelinessToken::new_held(self.clone(), token_id, keyexpr_string, options) instead of an inline observer.local_tokens.register + a direct struct literal - the register moved into the constructor (byte-identical effect). declare_token_aliased now ALSO calls new_held(self.clone(), token_id, resolved, options) - it previously constructed the handle WITHOUT registering, so this ADDS the missing registration of the RESOLVED literal (the bug fix). cache_token_declaration ordering unchanged (cache before register, both paths).
verification_bullets: Full host run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0, all required layers pass (0 FAIL): the liveliness behaviour + e2e lanes (Layer C/E) green - the literal declare_token path is byte-identical (register moved into new_held), the aliased path now registers. Default + liveliness-subset clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean (no test constructed LivelinessToken directly, so the private-field seal compiles cleanly); cargo fmt --all --check clean.

Bug confirmed by direct read before the fix: literal declare_token registered the held token (old mod.rs:2451-2455), aliased declare_token_aliased did NOT (old :2579-2586 constructed the handle directly with no register); the consumer observer.rs:647 local_tokens.keyexpr_for(token_id) returns None for an unregistered token -> no Declare(DeclToken) reply to an inbound non-final liveliness Interest -> an aliased token was invisible to a peer that subscribed LATER. zenoh-pico _z_declare_liveliness_token (net/liveliness.c:52-77) always inserts into _local_tokens with the resolved keyexpr, regardless of literal/alias form; wz's aliased omission diverged.

Unrepresentable-by-construction (feedback_unrepresentable_over_test): NO discipline test added - the private fields + the single registering constructor make a non-registered held token impossible to build, a stronger guard than a test asserting the register ran. The struct's existing accessors (id/keyexpr/options) + teardown stay in-module, so sealing the fields does not affect the public surface.
carry_forward_bullets: declare_token_aliased registration asymmetry FIXED (R311mz), unrepresentably: LivelinessToken::new_held is the sole constructor and registers in the LocalTokenRegistry; the struct fields are private. Aliased liveliness tokens now replay to late subscribers (pico parity restored, net/liveliness.c:77). The session-review's most material finding - a real correctness bug, not a structural smell - is closed.

Session-review residual #2 REVIEWED + CLOSED AS NON-DEFECT: the LivelinessToken/LivelinessSubscriber teardown `let _ = &self.session` discards are NOT a band-aid to fix. Gating the structs on liveliness-token/liveliness-subscriber (the reviewer's proposed root fix) would break the R311o signature-stability of declare_token / declare_liveliness_subscriber (their return types LivelinessToken<R,T> / LivelinessSubscriber<R,T> would vanish when the feature is off, breaking handshake-only builds); reverting the teardown to the signature-stable send_undeclare_token / send_interest_final wrappers would re-couple the to-be-retired wrappers (blocking session-review Finding 2) and break origination/retraction symmetry. The discard is the deliberate minimal cost of signature-stability + seam-routing. The initial recommendation to "gate the structs" was a too-quick acceptance of the reviewer's diff-only finding; verification against R311o reversed it.

Session-review residual #3 still open (lower value): SendWireError::UnsupportedVariant - the seam catch arm returns FeatureDisabled for reply-plane variants (Response/ResponseFinal/Oam) that structurally cannot originate through the Session-method seam, conflating feature-off with caller-bug; a distinct variant is the honest surface. Bundle candidate, not urgent.

Could mirror the new_held unrepresentable-constructor pattern to LivelinessSubscriber for consistency, but its two declare paths already register symmetrically in liveliness_subscribers (no bug) - YAGNI unless a future divergence appears.

Round 311n.decision_summary: R311n measurement automation — scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh + lib/feature_implies.py compute wz-facade implies-graph from cargo metadata; honest SKIP on compile-fail lanes.
changes_bullets: scripts/lib/feature_implies.py NEW — wz facade → wz-runtime-tokio implies-graph resolver. Reads `cargo metadata --format-version=1 --no-deps` JSON from stdin, computes wz-runtime-tokio transitive closure + wz facade activation map + invert to PULLERS-by-codec, emits shell-sourceable `PULLERS_codec_X="..."` assignments for every `codec-*` rt feature. Standalone module instead of inline heredoc because `cargo metadata | python3 - <<EOF` is ambiguous in bash (heredoc + pipe both target stdin).

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh — each minus-<codec> lane excludes the codec + its full transitive puller set (declare-* / query-* / liveliness-* / domain-* / presets). Pre-R311n the exclusion was the codec name only; cargo resolver silently re-enabled the codec via `declare-subscriber = [codec-declare]` etc. and the lane measured a fake near-zero delta. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs liveliness_get (Session-review Finding 1, the real defect): bind `let actions = self.actions()?` at the TOP of the method, BEFORE the `if !is_established()` gate, and reuse it for alloc_next_interest_id + cache_get_interest. On a multicast session, is_established() reads `false` (the R311nc is_established() -> unwrap_or(false) projection), so the establishment gate front-ran the transport check and returned LivelinessGetError::NotEstablished ("retry after the session re-establishes" - futile on multicast) instead of the honest RequiresUnicast the `actions()?` one line later would have produced. Round 311nf.decision_summary: R311nf: Session transport typestate — `Session<R,T,Tp>` replaces the `SessionTransport<R,T>` runtime enum; illegal cross-transport calls are now compile errors.
changes_bullets: session/transport.rs (REWRITTEN): sealed-trait typestate home. `sealed::Sealed` + `TransportState<R,T>` trait (associated `type Payload` + `fn send_network_message`). Unconditional `struct Unicast` / `struct Multicast` markers; `Sealed` impls cfg-gated per feature. Unicast payload = `Arc<SessionLinkActions<R,T>>`; Multicast payload = `MulticastPayload { #[cfg(codec-push)] tx }`. Deleted `SessionTransport<R,T>` enum + manual Clone.

session/mod.rs: `Session<R,T,Tp>` struct — `transport: <Tp as TransportState<R,T>>::Payload`; no `Tp` default (eagerly bound-checked at definition in multicast-only builds; aliases carry the default). Clone impl gated `where Tp::Payload: Clone`. `TokioSession = Session<_,_,Unicast>` + `TokioMulticastSession = Session<_,_,Multicast>` aliases. Three impl blocks: agnostic (`publish`, observer, clock, `declare_subscriber`, `send_network_message` forwarder), unicast-only (`new`, infallible `actions()`, `dispatch_iteration_event{,_with}`, `is_established`, `batch_*`, all alias/query/declare/liveliness surface), multicast-only (`new_multicast`, `dispatch_multicast_iteration_event`).

session/{subscriber,publisher,querier,queryable,liveliness,matching_listener,decl_listener}.rs: all `Session<R,T>` references updated to `Session<R,T,Unicast>` (or agnostic `Session<R,T,Tp>` for `deferred_sample_sink`). `Subscriber<R,T>` -> `Subscriber<R>` (dropped T; stores observer Arc, not Session clone — ISP). `SubscribeAliasError::RequiresUnicast` variant deleted (now a compile-time guarantee). All `.actions().map_err(|_| X::RequiresUnicast)?` chains flattened to `.actions()`. `matching_listener` + `decl_listener` gated `transport-unicast`. `dispatch_iteration_event_with` flattened: `flush_pending_replies(self.actions().as_ref())` runs unconditionally (was `if let Ok` silent skip on multicast).

wz-session-core/src/send_wire_error.rs: `UnsupportedVariant` doc narrowed — removed the retired `Session::actions()` fallible-projection meaning; sole remaining runtime meaning is non-Push `NetworkMessage` on the multicast send arm.

Consumer migration: `wz-e2e-harness` + `wz-ap-demo` (`tasks.rs`/`runner.rs`) bare `Session` -> `TokioSession`; all `let Ok(actions) = session.actions() else { warn; return; }` blocks flattened to `let actions = session.actions()`. `wz-runtime-tokio-multicast-tests` + `multicast_glue.rs` `both_build_multicast_session_is_live`: `Session::new_multicast` -> `TokioMulticastSession::new_multicast`; deleted `session.actions() == Err(UnsupportedVariant)` assertion (now a compile-time guarantee).

session/tests.rs: `Session` type annotations -> `TokioSession`; all `.actions().expect("unicast test session")` removed (45 sites; `actions()` is infallible); restored `obs.flush_pending(session.actions().as_ref())` in `queryable_staged_before_undeclare_suppressed_but_final_still_sent` (was silently deleted by bulk sed — root cause: entire call line matched the removal pattern).

Round 311nm.decision_summary: R311nm: wz->pico multicast JOIN+Push interop e2e 신규 — wz in-library mcast publisher의 JOIN+Push를 외부 pico z_sub -m peer가 admit+decode(byte-exact, 실 UDP). Layer M opt-in, Layer E 제외.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_publisher_to_pico_multicast_zsub.rs (NEW): wz in-library 멀티캐스트 publisher(ephemeral TX-only `UdpDriver::from_socket` + `drive_multicast_session` + `multicast_put_literal`; mc_params version 0x09 / batch 2048 / sn-req-res 0x02 = vendored pico config 정확히 일치)가 JOIN beacon + framed Push를 실 UDP group(224.0.0.224:7457)에 송신 → 외부 `z_sub -m peer -l udp/...#iface=<default-route-dev>`가 admit + decode → stdout `>> [Subscriber] Received ('demo/mc/interop': '...')` byte-exact. 방향=wz->pico (pico->wz는 wz `bind_multicast_v4`가 SO_REUSEADDR 미설정이라 동일 host 동일 group port co-bind 시 EADDRINUSE; carry). JOIN admission은 transitive 증명: pico rx.c:373-396이 version/seq_num_res/req_id_res/batch_size 불일치 peer의 Frame을 admit 전 drop하므로 z_sub의 Received 발화 자체가 wz JOIN을 pico가 파싱·admit했다는 증거. JOIN-admission 윈도우 레이스는 100ms republish loop로 제거([[feedback-no-flaky-ever]]). default-route iface는 `ip route show default`로 런타임 발견(wz INADDR_ANY mcast egress가 고르는 그 iface) → 양 peer 동일 링크. stdbuf -oL로 z_sub stdout line-buffer.

changes_bullets: scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh: TARGETS에 z_pub 추가(주기 publish CLI). pico->wz 멀티캐스트 publisher로 필요 — z_put one-shot은 JOIN-admission 윈도우를 레이스하므로 주기 publisher(z_pub -n)가 no-flaky 전제. 동일 스크립트가 7 binaries 빌드(z_sub 체크가 z_pub 커버).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio: socket2를 optional 프로덕션 dep로 승격(version 0.6, features=["all"]로 set_reuse_port 잠금해제, dep:socket2 게이트=scouting-active/transport-multicast). UdpDriver::bind_multicast_v4를 socket2 경유 재작성 — SO_REUSEADDR+SO_REUSEPORT를 bind 전 설정(Socket->std UdpSocket->tokio from_std; tokio는 pre-bind setsockopt 훅 없음). zenoh-pico parity(udp_multicast_posix.c:180/185 무조건 REUSE, INADDR_ANY:port bind line196). lib.rs 주석의 'single-receiver, socket2 회피' 결정을 multi-listener pico-interop 요구로 supersede — 그 주석이 명시적으로 예고한 socket2 진입 지점.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_subscriber_from_pico_multicast.rs: 신규 e2e — 외부 pico z_pub -m peer 멀티캐스트 publisher의 JOIN beacon+framed Push를 wz in-library mcast subscriber가 group port co-bind + admit + byte-exact decode. dispatcher.active_peers()==1 직접 단언(R311nm transitive 증명과 대비 — wz가 in-process admitter). wz mc_params를 pico CONFIG(version 0x09/seq_num_res 0x02/batch 2048)에 핀해 ingest_join §3.2 admit. payload byte-exact는 pico [%4d]<value> 템플릿(z_pub.c) 재구성으로 full 단언(idx는 pico 내부 카운터라 비결정적).
scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer M(opt-in, env-dependent)에 4번째 sub-step(wz_subscriber_from_pico_multicast) 등록. 기존 z_sub 존재 체크가 z_pub도 graceful-SKIP 커버.
verification_bullets: Phase 0 falsify: z_pub 빌드(7 binaries) 후 pico z_pub -m peer -> pico z_sub -m peer 같은 host co-bind '>> Received' 5/5 — OS 멀티캐스트 라우팅 + REUSE co-bind 동작을 wz 프로덕션 변경 전 사전 확인. 멀티캐스트 listener는 양쪽 INADDR_ANY:port + REUSEADDR+REUSEPORT라 SO_REUSEPORT 필수(socket2 features=["all"]로 잠금해제).

Phase 1 회귀: REUSE 추가 후 기존 Layer M scouting_multicast_loopback 2/2 + multicast_pubsub_loopback 2/2 통과(단일 binder에 REUSE 무해). cargo check --features transport-multicast,scouting-active EXIT=0(socket2 path 컴파일).
Phase 2: 신규 pico->wz e2e 15/15 연속 no-flaky. Layer M 전체 4 sub-step EXIT=0. keyexpr matching + cross-impl JOIN admission(active_peers==1 직접) + Push byte-exact 실측 통과.

Phase 3: full host run-ci(WZ_RUN_LAYER_M=1) EXIT=0 'all required layers pass'(파이프 없는 exit code 직접 캡처; 컴파일 error[/panicked 0, 589 매치는 전부 '0 failed' 노이즈). atomic ledger entries 722->723, orphan delta=0(T1 new=+0 유지), T3 warn 4 불변. resolver=2가 socket2 dev-dep 누수를 C1 격리(default workspace 빌드 무영향).
carry_forward_bullets: R311no로 멀티캐스트 wz<->pico 양방향 interop 완성: wz->pico(R311nm) + pico->wz(R311no) 모두 실소켓 JOIN admit + Push byte-exact. wz가 admitter인 역방향은 active_peers()==1로 JOIN admission을 직접 관측(R311nm은 pico Frame-drop 정책으로 transitive 증명만 가능했음).

NEXT 후보: ① 멀티캐스트 큰메시지 >256B — wz MsgPut payload codec bound 256(msg_put.scxml:111) 확장 선결(별건; R311nl negative test가 unicast로 pin). ② breadth: serial 링크 / gossip scouting interop 실소켓. ③ 양방향 동시(wz+pico 동일 group 양쪽 publish)는 reachable하나 YAGNI.
설계 메모: socket2가 wz-runtime-tokio 프로덕션 dep로 진입(feature-gated). pico parity(멀티캐스트 group port=multi-listener, REUSE 무조건)가 근거 — 테스트 워크어라운드가 아니라 실 프로덕션 interop 갭 청산. lib.rs 주석이 예고한 진입 지점이었음.
UNPUSHED 누적: R311nm(b6572ca+e3c2e73) + R311nn(67c5ac3+5e79be9) + R311no(이 라운드) = origin/main(a95338c) 대비. push=사용자 명시 동의 대기.

Round 311np.decision_summary: R311np: R311no가 들인 테스트 SSOT 위반 청산 — GROUP/pico CONFIG(0x09/0x02/2048)/default_route_iface가 두 멀티캐스트 interop 테스트에 byte-identical 복제됐던 것을 wz-integration-tests::common 단일소스로. 빌더는 MulticastParams dev-dep 경계로 잔류.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs (common 모듈): 멀티캐스트 interop SSOT 추가 — ZENOH_MULTICAST_GROUP(224.0.0.224) + PICO_PROTO_VERSION/SN_RESOLUTION/BATCH_MULTICAST_SIZE(pico CONFIG 0x09/0x02/2048, vendored pin 참조 주석) + default_route_iface(). 두 멀티캐스트 interop 테스트가 byte-identical 복제하던 값/인프라의 단일 소스. pin bump 시 한 곳만 surfacing.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_publisher_to_pico_multicast_zsub.rs + wz_subscriber_from_pico_multicast.rs: GROUP을 common::ZENOH_MULTICAST_GROUP alias로, PICO_* 상수 + default_route_iface 로컬 정의 제거 → common import. wz_mc_params 빌더는 MulticastParams(wz-session-core dev-dep) 타입 경계로 각 테스트에 잔류하되 common::PICO_* 참조(값 drift 제거). wz-session-core를 lib dep로 승격하면 resolver-2 dev-dep 격리(R311nm/nl)를 위협하므로 회피 — 빌더 2-site는 dev-dep 경계상 정당.
verification_bullets: R311nn F1("publisher 하니스 SSOT 중복=FALSE POSITIVE, dev-dep cycle hazard")을 부분정정: sibling crate(wz-runtime-tokio-test-support) 추출은 cycle hazard 맞으나, 같은 크레이트 common 모듈(src/lib.rs) 추출은 cycle-free SSOT였음 — 그 옵션을 놓쳤음. MulticastParams가 dev-dep라 빌더만 잔류하는 부분 청산이 dev-dep 경계 존중하는 교과서 최선.

clippy -p wz-integration-tests --all-targets EXIT=0(unused import 0, fmt 자동정렬). 두 멀티캐스트 interop 테스트 각 10/10 no-flaky(동작 보존; 순수 값-SSOT 리팩터). full host run-ci(WZ_RUN_LAYER_M=1) EXIT=0 'all required layers pass'(컴파일 error[/panicked 0). atomic ledger entries 723->724, orphan delta=0(T1 new=+0 유지), T3 warn 4 불변.
multicast_pubsub_loopback.rs(wz-runtime-tokio crate)의 동일 값 복제는 cross-crate라 wz-integration-tests::common 사용 불가 — R311nn sibling-crate hazard 유효, 별개 유지(정직한 범위 한정).
carry_forward_bullets: R311no 도입 부채(테스트 헬퍼 SSOT 위반) 청산 완료 — 멀티캐스트 interop의 값(pico CONFIG)·인프라(default_route_iface)·group이 wz-integration-tests::common 단일 소스. R311nn F1("SSOT 중복=FALSE POSITIVE, dev-dep cycle hazard")을 부분정정: sibling crate 추출은 cycle hazard 맞으나 같은 크레이트 common 모듈 추출은 cycle-free였음(그 옵션을 놓쳤음).

잔여(의도된 구조): wz_mc_params 빌더 2-site는 MulticastParams=wz-session-core dev-dep 경계. multicast_pubsub_loopback의 동일 값(wz-runtime-tokio crate)은 cross-crate라 common 사용 불가(R311nn sibling-crate hazard 유효). 둘 다 dev-dep 경계상 구조적 정당.

NEXT(R311no carry 유지): ① 큰메시지>256B 멀티캐스트 — msg_put payload bound 256(msg_put.scxml:111) 확장은 비자명: SCE codegen max-size semantics(owned decode-reject vs MCU 고정버퍼) + MCU 메모리 trade-off + R311nl 257B negative test 의미변경 + query/ext_zbuf 256 일관성. ② breadth: serial 링크/gossip scouting 실소켓 interop.
UNPUSHED: R311np 청산 커밋. push=사용자 동의 대기.

SceBytes/SceString을 codec.rs newtype에서 공유 crate sce-portable-bytes로 unify; sce_rust_runtime::SceBytes(이전 type alias =Vec<u8>/heapless로 N을 erase)와 sce_forge_runtime::codec::SceBytes가 동일 N-preserving newtype 재export. from_slice가 자체 error CapacityExceeded 반환(범용 carrier가 codec CodecError 비의존; From<CapacityExceeded> for CodecError로 흡수). 5769510d8의 'Infallible' 오기 주석을 CapacityExceeded 타입으로 fallibility 명시.

crates/wz-session-core/src/codec_owned.rs: owned_bytes를 SceBytes::<N>::from_slice(b)? 로(CapacityExceeded->CodecError From 변환; SCE 생성 codec try_into_owned과 동일 패턴). SceString은 codec.rs 잔류라 owned_string 무변경.

crates/wz-switchboard-codegen/src/lib.rs: native event payload의 bytes 필드가 sce_rust_runtime::SceBytes<N>(이제 N-preserving newtype, 이전 alias=Vec). &[u8] 디코드뷰->owned 변환을 infallible .into()에서 fallible from_slice pre-conversion으로(let id=match from_slice{Ok=>v,Err=>return false}; decode-miss와 동일 graceful, 디코드가 max-size N 검증해 by-construction 성공이나 panic 금지). string은 SceString alias라 .into() 유지. owned_field_move bytes arm 제거 + field-init shorthand(redundant_field_names 회피). codegen 22 unit test 갱신(from_slice/return false/shorthand assert).
