Round 311sj.decision_summary: R311sj: c3c-3 B1b control-plane keyexpr alias resolution. forward_subscription / forward_unsubscription now resolve an aliased DeclareSubscriber keyexpr / UndeclareSubscriber ext_keyexpr against the inbound face's link-local table and re-flood NORMALIZED to a literal -- the symmetric control-plane twin of B1a's data-plane push resolution, so an aliased subscribe can be cleanly undone by an aliased unsubscribe (no interest leak). Extends declare_ext_keyexpr with resolve_ext_keyexpr (a VLE-inner-id resolver, the read_ext_keyexpr alias-capable superset). Completes B1: the linkstate-peer HAT resolves keyexpr aliases on both planes. wz still originates literals; the value is interop.
changes_bullets: session-core declare_ext_keyexpr.rs: add resolve_ext_keyexpr(exts, table) -- the resolve_wireexpr analogue for the UndeclareSubscriber ext_keyexpr form (id==0 = literal suffix verbatim, id!=0 = table[id]+suffix). Decodes the inner mapping-id VLE via a small decode_vle (no length cap; read_ext_keyexpr only handled the single-byte literal id 0x00). +3 units: literal-with-empty-table, aliased-composed-via-table, unknown-alias-is-None.

linkstate_forward.rs forward_subscription: resolves the DeclareSubscriber keyexpr against the inbound face's link-local table (resolve_wireexpr) inside the scoped faces borrow, registers the RESOLVED literal interest, and re-floods a carrier that is a clean literal sourced DeclareSubscriber when the inbound was aliased (build_declare_subscriber(0,0,literal)) or the cloned original when already literal (the literal path stays byte-unchanged). An unresolvable alias drops the declaration.

linkstate_forward.rs forward_unsubscription: the symmetric withdrawal -- resolves the ext_keyexpr via resolve_ext_keyexpr against the face table, withdraws the resolved literal interest, and re-floods a literal undeclare rebuilt (build_undeclare_subscriber_with_keyexpr) when aliased / cloned when literal. This is what lets an aliased subscribe be cleanly undone by an aliased unsubscribe -- a subscribe-only B1b would have leaked the interest (aliased sub registers, aliased unsub could not resolve to withdraw).

linkstate_forward.rs helpers: removed the now-dead literal-only declare_subscriber_keyexpr / undeclare_subscriber_keyexpr / literal_keyexpr; added keyexpr_is_aliased (id != 0 detector, decides whether a carrier must be normalized) + declare_subscriber_wireexpr (returns the raw Wireexpr for resolution). forwarded_keyexpr inlines the literal extraction (literal_keyexpr removed).

Tests: forwarded_declare_keyexpr + aliased_undeclare helpers + 2 integration units (an aliased subscription resolves and re-floods a literal; an aliased unsubscription resolves the ext alias and withdraws the interest -- the symmetry).

Completes B1: the linkstate-peer HAT resolves keyexpr aliases on BOTH the data plane (B1a push) and the control plane (B1b declare/undeclare), reusing the resolve_wireexpr / resolve_ext_keyexpr SSOTs and the per-face table. wz still originates only literals; the value is interop with external zenoh/pico peers that alias keyexprs.

Round 311sl.decision_summary: R311sl: c3c-3 D3 remove_detached_nodes. The linkstate-peer graph GC-prunes nodes no longer reachable from self over the advertisement graph (DFS over node.links), run at the ingest tail (process_linkstates) and inside remove_link (zenoh network.rs:786,948,990); the driver purges each pruned node's subscription interest (zenoh pubsub_remove_node). Corrects deregister to purge only the genuinely-detached set so a neighbour still reachable via another face keeps its interest, and the demo reports the PEAK node count (teardown's prune collapses the live graph). Tree accessors tolerate a node pruned in the coalesced-recompute window.
changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: remove_detached_nodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Zid> -- a DFS from self over each visited node's ADVERTISED links (node.links.keys(), not the petgraph edges: reachability is over what nodes claim to link to), removing every unvisited node. Keeps idx_by_zid (wz's zid->NodeIndex secondary index, which zenoh lacks) in lockstep -- every node dropped from the graph is dropped from the index too. Mirrors zenoh remove_detached_nodes (network.rs:990-1013), narrowed to return zids (zenoh returns (NodeIndex, Node) for gossip; wz needs only the zid to purge interest).

process_linkstates now runs the prune at its tail and retains `updated` to drop any pruned zid (zenoh network.rs:786-788 new_nodes/updated_nodes.retain); Changes gains `removed: Vec<Zid>` (zenoh Changes.removed_nodes parity, narrowed to zids). remove_link returns Vec<Zid> (the detached set) instead of Option<Link>, calling remove_detached_nodes after the self-edge drop -- zenoh remove_link (network.rs:936-988): self-side bookkeeping then the prune.

tree_children_of / next_hop now use graph.node_weight (not the panicking index op) so a child/hop pruned since the last compute_trees -- possible because the recompute is COALESCED onto a later tick (D2c) -- resolves to None and is skipped rather than panicking on a removed StableGraph index. The pruned node is unreachable, so it was never a valid forward target; the next recompute drops it for good.

linkstate_forward: the forward() OAM arm purges subs.remove_peer for every changes.removed node (zenoh pubsub_remove_node over handle_oam's changes.removed_nodes, hat/linkstate_peer/mod.rs:418-422). deregister REPLACES the former unconditional state.actions.peer_zid() purge with the detached-set purge from remove_link's return (zenoh undeclare_face mod.rs:378-387, pubsub_remove_node per removed node) -- a correctness fix: a neighbour still reachable via ANOTHER face is no longer in the detached set, so it KEEPS its interest (the old unconditional purge wrongly dropped a still-reachable subscriber); the departed neighbour is itself returned only when it had no other path.

wz-ap-demo runner: a peak_nodes high-water mark sampled each app-tick; the shutdown summary now reports `peak N node(s) in topology graph` (and the learned-topology witness `peak N node(s) in graph`) because teardown deregisters EVERY face and the D3 prune collapses the live graph toward self during shutdown -- the peak is the meaningful convergence witness ("this peer's graph held N peers once converged"), which the 4-peer selectivity e2e asserts on.

Tests: the 7 incrementally-built graph mechanics tests (mapping/sn-gate/edge-formation) now use consistent single-snapshot ingests via a `relay` helper (the link peer 0x07 relay-advertises the test nodes so they are reachable; a real flood is one consistent list, and a transiently-detached node is now correctly pruned). +3 graph prune tests (ingest-detach, remove_link transitive prune, stale-tree accessor tolerance) + 1 driver test (a multi-path peer KEEPS its interest on the direct face's deregister). deregister_recomputes_trees re-anchored on the recomputes() counter (the prune is inline; only the tree recompute is deferred). re-home test now asserts the multi-path node is NOT pruned.
verification_bullets: wz-routing-graph 31 PASS (incl 3 new prune tests + the relay-fixed mechanics tests). wz-runtime-tokio (routing-peer) lib 357 PASS (linkstate_forward module 61: +1 multi-path-keeps-interest, deregister_recomputes re-anchored on recomputes()). clippy(wz-routing-graph + wz-runtime-tokio + wz-ap-demo, --tests) clean. fmt --check clean. default (non-routing-peer) wz-ap-demo build clean (the shared runner.rs still compiles without the routing-peer forwarder path).

E6 e2e 8/8 across 3 consecutive runs, NO flake (wz_peer_mesh 1 + wz_peer_data_forward 3: forward 2-hop / withdraw 2-hop / 4-peer selectivity). The 4-peer test confirms peer-D converges to PEAK 4 nodes -- it is a fully-converged member, so its non-receipt is the subscription filter pruning it, not topological isolation.

Root cause caught + fixed: the 4-peer e2e first FAILED with D reporting "1 node(s) in topology graph" at shutdown. Diagnosed as a TEARDOWN ARTIFACT, not isolation: teardown deregisters D's accepted face to B, which now prunes B (and transitively A, C), collapsing the live graph to self. Proof it was steady-state-converged: C still received the forwarded data (the mesh ran), and D is structurally identical to C (a pure acceptor of B, whose accept-side add_link is proven by the two-hop forward). Fixed by reporting the peak node count, not the mid-teardown live count.

Grounding (direct read): zenoh remove_detached_nodes (network.rs:990-1013, DFS over self.graph[node].links.keys()); its two call sites -- link_states tail (:786, returns Changes.removed_nodes) and remove_link (:948). The existing-node update branch (:711-722) updates sn/links/locators but NOT whatami, so a node first seen as a placeholder keeps whatami None even after its own link-state arrives -- wz matches this (one mechanics test lists the node before the relay to insert it fresh). HAT consumers: pubsub_remove_node (pubsub.rs:622, purges any sub whose interested set contains the removed node) called per removed node in handle_oam (mod.rs:418-422) and undeclare_face (mod.rs:378-387).

Correctness fix: deregister now purges ONLY the genuinely-detached set returned by remove_link, so a neighbour still reachable via another face KEEPS its interest (the former unconditional peer_zid purge over-purged a still-reachable subscriber -- zenoh purges only remove_link's detached set, mod.rs:378-387). Validated by deregister_keeps_a_still_reachable_peers_interest (triangle S-A-C: drop the direct S-A face, A stays reachable via C, A's interest survives).

Honest divergences/notes: (a) the demo shutdown summary reports PEAK node count, not live, because teardown's deregister prune collapses the graph toward self -- the peak is the convergence witness the 4-peer e2e reads. (b) a placeholder node keeps whatami None even after its own link-state (wz matches zenoh network.rs:711-722, which updates sn/links not whatami; spanning-tree forwarding is whatami-agnostic, so harmless until gossip/autoconnect). (c) tree accessors tolerate a node pruned in the coalesced-recompute window (node_weight, not the panicking index).

Round 311sl.publishable_decision_summary: R311sl: c3c-3 D3 remove_detached_nodes. The linkstate-peer graph GC-prunes nodes no longer reachable from self over the advertisement graph (DFS over node.links), run at the ingest tail (process_linkstates) and inside remove_link (zenoh network.rs:786,948,990); the driver purges each pruned node's subscription interest (zenoh pubsub_remove_node). Corrects deregister to purge only the genuinely-detached set so a neighbour still reachable via another face keeps its interest, and the demo reports the PEAK node count (teardown's prune collapses the live graph). Tree accessors tolerate a node pruned in the coalesced-recompute window.
publishable_changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: remove_detached_nodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Zid> -- a DFS from self over each visited node's ADVERTISED links (node.links.keys(), not the petgraph edges: reachability is over what nodes claim to link to), removing every unvisited node. Keeps idx_by_zid (wz's zid->NodeIndex secondary index, which zenoh lacks) in lockstep -- every node dropped from the graph is dropped from the index too. Mirrors zenoh remove_detached_nodes (network.rs:990-1013), narrowed to return zids (zenoh returns (NodeIndex, Node) for gossip; wz needs only the zid to purge interest).

process_linkstates now runs the prune at its tail and retains `updated` to drop any pruned zid (zenoh network.rs:786-788 new_nodes/updated_nodes.retain); Changes gains `removed: Vec<Zid>` (zenoh Changes.removed_nodes parity, narrowed to zids). remove_link returns Vec<Zid> (the detached set) instead of Option<Link>, calling remove_detached_nodes after the self-edge drop -- zenoh remove_link (network.rs:936-988): self-side bookkeeping then the prune.

tree_children_of / next_hop now use graph.node_weight (not the panicking index op) so a child/hop pruned since the last compute_trees -- possible because the recompute is COALESCED onto a later tick (D2c) -- resolves to None and is skipped rather than panicking on a removed StableGraph index. The pruned node is unreachable, so it was never a valid forward target; the next recompute drops it for good.

linkstate_forward: the forward() OAM arm purges subs.remove_peer for every changes.removed node (zenoh pubsub_remove_node over handle_oam's changes.removed_nodes, hat/linkstate_peer/mod.rs:418-422). deregister REPLACES the former unconditional state.actions.peer_zid() purge with the detached-set purge from remove_link's return (zenoh undeclare_face mod.rs:378-387, pubsub_remove_node per removed node) -- a correctness fix: a neighbour still reachable via ANOTHER face is no longer in the detached set, so it KEEPS its interest (the old unconditional purge wrongly dropped a still-reachable subscriber); the departed neighbour is itself returned only when it had no other path.

wz-ap-demo runner: a peak_nodes high-water mark sampled each app-tick; the shutdown summary now reports `peak N node(s) in topology graph` (and the learned-topology witness `peak N node(s) in graph`) because teardown deregisters EVERY face and the D3 prune collapses the live graph toward self during shutdown -- the peak is the meaningful convergence witness ("this peer's graph held N peers once converged"), which the 4-peer selectivity e2e asserts on.

Tests: the 7 incrementally-built graph mechanics tests (mapping/sn-gate/edge-formation) now use consistent single-snapshot ingests via a `relay` helper (the link peer 0x07 relay-advertises the test nodes so they are reachable; a real flood is one consistent list, and a transiently-detached node is now correctly pruned). +3 graph prune tests (ingest-detach, remove_link transitive prune, stale-tree accessor tolerance) + 1 driver test (a multi-path peer KEEPS its interest on the direct face's deregister). deregister_recomputes_trees re-anchored on the recomputes() counter (the prune is inline; only the tree recompute is deferred). re-home test now asserts the multi-path node is NOT pruned.

Round 311sm.decision_summary: R311sm: c3c-3 D4 Details split. The linkstate re-flood (propagate) now honours zenoh's full-for-new / links-only-for-updated Details split (network.rs:645-678): a node seen for the first time with full state re-floods FULL (zid + links), an already-mapped re-advertiser re-floods LINKS-ONLY (no zid -- the receiver resolves the omitted zid from the psid it learned when the node was new). Changes splits into new/updated/removed; process_linkstates classifies by oldsn==0; make_link_state gains a links_only variant that clears the P flag and omits the zid (0 codec changes); build_linkstate_for becomes build_linkstate_split.
changes_bullets: make_link_state(idx, links_only): the wz LinkState codec already gates the zid on the P flag (linkstate.scxml options.P -> zid_len/zid present-if), so links_only=true clears P and omits zid_len/zid while keeping psid/sn/whatami/links/weights -- zenoh's Details{zid:false, links:true}. Mirrors zenoh make_link_state's per-Details field gating (network.rs:330-334). 0 codec changes (the wire shape was already representable).

Changes { new, updated, removed }: new = a node whose full state the receiver does not yet have, so the re-flood must carry its zid (a fresh insert, OR an existing node whose sn was still 0 = a placeholder = zenoh oldsn==0, network.rs:717); updated = an already-mapped re-advertiser (oldsn>0); removed = the D3 prune set. process_linkstates classifies each ingested entry into new/updated and retains BOTH minus the pruned zids.

build_linkstate_for(zids) -> build_linkstate_split(new, updated): builds new nodes FULL (make_link_state false) then updated nodes LINKS-ONLY (make_link_state true). New nodes are listed FIRST so a links-only entry that happens to reference a brand-new node still resolves within the single list. Mirrors zenoh make_msg over propagate_link_states' per-link out list (network.rs:645-678).

propagate (driver): per face (excluding the source face and the node whose own state it is), build_linkstate_split(new, updated) into ONE OAM so both halves arrive atomically -- zenoh network.rs:643-644 "send all states at once for each face to avoid premature node deletion on the other side". Early-returns when new and updated are both empty (overall and per face).

Correctness invariant: a face holds full state for every node either from its JOIN BOOTSTRAP (register -> flood_self floods the WHOLE graph FULL via build_linkstate_list, not just self) or from when the node was new (propagated full), so a later links-only update always resolves against a prior psid->zid mapping (convert_to_local_link_states' zid:None branch). Honest: locators still deferred; propagate keeps wz's tighter source-face exclusion for new nodes too (zenoh echoes new to the source and relies on sn-drop -- wz omits the redundant echo).

Round 311sn.decision_summary: R311sn: c3c-3 B2 wildcard keyexpr intersection. LinkstatepeerSubs lookups (interested / interested_remote) now match a published key against every registered subscription keyexpr by keyexpr INTERSECTION (keyexpr_intersect_patterns -- the SSOT the local SubscriberRegistry already uses, zenoh's Resource::get_matches route matching) instead of exact string equality, so a demo/** or demo/* subscription attracts a concrete demo/data Push. An EXTENSION of the flat by_key map's read path (a private matching_peers scan), NOT the resource-tree rewrite the roadmap feared; the prefix-tree fold for sublinear matching stays a tracked performance deferral. Contained in the lookup -- register/flood/data-route/codec unchanged.
changes_bullets: linkstate_subs.rs: new private matching_peers(target, exclude) -- splits the target (published key) and each registered subscription keyexpr on '/' and tests keyexpr INTERSECTION via keyexpr_intersect_patterns (the same SSOT + chunk-split idiom as declare.rs:110-113), deduping peers across all matching keys. interested(keyexpr) = matching_peers(keyexpr, None); interested_remote(keyexpr, self_zid) = matching_peers(keyexpr, Some(self_zid)). So a demo/** or demo/* subscription now attracts a concrete demo/data Push, while a literal subscription stays byte-exact (intersection of two literals = equality).

register / withdraw / remove_peer / subscriptions UNCHANGED: the keyexpr stored is the pattern as-declared; only the read-path lookup widened from exact get to intersection scan. The data route (forward_push / publish -> interested_remote -> directions_toward) and the control plane (forward_subscription register, re_advertise_subscriptions) are also UNCHANGED -- B2 is contained entirely in the lookup, so a wildcard subscription flows through register/flood as a literal pattern string and is matched at read time. 0 forwarder changes, 0 codec changes.

SCOPE: an EXTENSION of the existing flat by_key: HashMap<String, HashSet<Zid>> read path -- NOT the resource-tree rewrite the roadmap feared. The wildcard MATCHING is the feature (delivered here); zenoh additionally folds subscriptions into a prefix RESOURCE TREE for sublinear matching, which stays a tracked PERFORMANCE deferral (the O(subscriptions) scan is correct but linear; the tree is only needed for large subscription sets, not modelled).

Module + field docs rewritten: the exact-match MVP note is replaced with the intersection-matching contract (keyexpr_intersect_patterns SSOT, zenoh Resource::get_matches), the resource-tree fold named as the honest remaining deferral (performance, not correctness).

Tests (unit): a_literal_subscription_stays_exact (renamed from interest_is_keyed_exactly_not_by_prefix; a literal sub must still NOT answer a sibling or prefix key) + a_wildcard_subscription_attracts_a_concrete_publish (** spans extra depth, * is one chunk, other/** misses demo/data; interested_remote applies the same match then drops self) + a_peer_matching_via_two_patterns_appears_once (a peer matched by two covering keys is deduped).

Test (e2e): wz_peer_mesh_wildcard_subscription_attracts_a_concrete_publish -- the far subscriber C declares the PATTERN demo/**, the publisher A publishes the CONCRETE demo/mesh; C receives over real TCP, proving the pattern keyexpr survives the DeclareSubscriber wire, floods A-ward, and the data route intersects it against the concrete publish (exact-match-only would never route this). Auto-joins the already-wired E6 wz_peer_data_forward binary.

The graph crate is untouched -- B2 is a subscription-table read-path change, no topology change.

changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: `pub type Zid = Vec<u8>` becomes a Copy `struct Zid { bytes: [u8;16], len: u8 }` (the zenoh ZenohIdProto fixed-buffer-plus-size mirror) with from_slice (truncate to 16 + canonical zero-pad), as_slice (the trimmed wire bytes), len/is_empty, le16 (the 16-byte buffer the edge-jitter hashes), MAX_SIZE, a hex Debug, and From<&[u8]> / From<Vec<u8>>. zid_to_le_16 is now a one-line wrapper over le16 so the update_edge hash sites read unchanged.

The derived Ord/Eq/Hash are correct BECAUSE of the canonical invariant (bytes[len..]==0): a shorter zid that is a zero-extended prefix of a longer one compares equal on bytes then orders BEFORE it on len -- exactly as Vec<u8> orders a prefix before its extension (proved case-by-case: a differing real byte decides identically; an all-zero tail falls through to the len tie-break). So the deterministic cross-implementation edge-jitter tie-break with a zenohd peer (update_edge orders the pair by Ord, then hashes le16) is byte-for-byte unchanged by the representation switch.

LinkstateForwarder::new / with_trees_delay take `impl Into<Zid>` so the demo (Vec<u8> params.zid) and the tests (Zid) both compile unchanged.

Round 311sq.decision_summary: R311sq: 4-agent adversarial session review of sl..sp (D3/D4/B2/E2/E1) + remediation. The review found the self-assessment OVERCONFIDENT: a real correctness transient (tree-index reuse aliasing -- StableUnGraph reuses freed indices and D2c defers the recompute, so a stale tree entry could alias a reused index and misforward), a load-bearing untested claim (the Zid Ord == Vec<u8> cross-impl jitter tie-break), a convergent faithfulness gap (reintroduced placeholders not re-flooded), and convergent SSOT smells. All remediated: remove_detached_nodes scrubs freed indices from the cached trees; the Zid Ord equivalence is now tested; placeholders re-flood via changes.new; vestigial zid_to_le_16 deleted; purge_detached_interest + into_list extracted; matching_peers HashSet dedup; the demo drops a needless zid clone; + the D4 unmapped-psid drop test and doc-honesty fixes.
changes_bullets: F1 (CORRECTNESS, root-cause MAJOR): remove_detached_nodes now scrubs every freed NodeIndex from the cached spanning trees + distances (new scrub_trees). StableUnGraph REUSES a freed index on the next add_node, and the recompute is COALESCED (D2c), so a stale `trees` entry holding a freed index would, after a reuse, resolve via node_weight to a DIFFERENT live node and MISFORWARD a Push during the window (the node_weight guard only catches a still-absent index, not a reused one). Scrubbing keeps the invariant "the trees never reference a freed index": affected routes resolve to None (drop) until the tick rebuild, never an aliased misroute. +unit a_reused_node_index_does_not_alias_a_stale_tree_entry (prune frees C's idx, D reuses it, next_hop(self,D) must be None not C's old hop A).

F2 (CRITICAL coverage, quality): the load-bearing Zid Ord == Vec<u8> equivalence (the cross-impl jitter tie-break) was prose-only. +unit zid_ord_matches_vec_u8_ord_including_zero_extended_prefixes (a full table incl [1]/[1,0]/[1,5] prefix cases) + zid_eq_hash_truncation_and_from_are_canonical (HashSet dedup, >16 truncation, From<&[u8]>/From<Vec<u8>>).

F3 (faithfulness, architect+root-cause convergent): rebuild_edges now returns the placeholders it introduced; process_linkstates pushes them into changes.new (deduped) so a reintroduced node re-floods onward (zenoh new_nodes.push, network.rs:763) -- the prune retain drops it if it is itself unreachable. +unit a_reintroduced_placeholder_re_floods_as_new.
F4 (SSOT, architect+refactoring convergent): deleted the vestigial zid_to_le_16 free fn (body was `zid.le16()`); the 6 update_edge / test hash sites call .le16() directly.
F5 (SSOT, refactoring): the byte-identical "purge each removed node's interest" loop at the two prune sites (deregister + the ingest OAM arm) is extracted to one purge_detached_interest(&[Zid]).

F6 (SSOT, refactoring): build_linkstate_list / build_linkstate_split shared their LinkStateList assembly tail (triplicated num_link_states=len); a free `into_list(Vec<LinkstateOwned>)` derives the count once.

F7 (smell/perf, refactoring): matching_peers dedup was O(matches^2) via out.contains on the DATA path (interested_remote per Push); now a HashSet<Zid> accumulator (Zid is Copy+Hash). Doc names the per-message keyexpr-intersection cost.
F8 (smell, refactoring): the demo dropped an unnecessary params.zid.clone() -- LinkstateForwarder::new takes impl Into<Zid>, so it now passes &params.zid[..] (From<&[u8]>, no Vec clone).

Coverage + honesty: +unit a_links_only_entry_for_an_unmapped_psid_is_dropped (the D4 unsafe boundary -- a zid-less entry for an unmapped psid MUST drop; also path-covers the E2 unresolvable-psid log); edge_pruned test now asserts A/B SURVIVE (edge_count==0 is the edge prune, not a node prune -- it could have passed for the wrong reason). Doc honesty: the Zid Ord docstring now states the equivalence is vs the OLD Vec<u8> and that the vs-ZENOH property holds only for canonical wire zids (zenoh trims trailing zeros, so the prefix corner is unreachable); flood_self doc admits the D4 Details split is applied to propagate ONLY -- the self-event flood still sends FULL topology (a tracked follow-on); propagate doc labels the whole-source-face skip a deliberate divergence from zenoh's finer new-to-source rule.
verification_bullets: wz-routing-graph 38 PASS (+5: a_reused_node_index_does_not_alias (F1), zid_ord_matches_vec_u8 + zid_eq_hash_truncation_and_from (F2), a_reintroduced_placeholder_re_floods (F3), a_links_only_entry_for_an_unmapped_psid_is_dropped (D4 boundary)). wz-runtime-tokio (routing-peer) lib 360 PASS (the F5 purge extract + F7 HashSet dedup + the doc edits regress nothing). clippy(both --tests) clean. fmt --check clean (graph + runtime-tokio + ap-demo). default (non-routing-peer) wz-ap-demo + wz-runtime-tokio build clean.

E6 e2e 5/5 across 3 runs, NO flake (wz_peer_mesh 1 + wz_peer_data_forward 4: forward 2-hop / wildcard 2-hop / withdraw / 4-peer selectivity). The F1 tree scrub + F3 placeholder re-flood are behaviour changes on the prune / propagate paths, so the real-TCP multi-hop convergence + selectivity are the meaningful gate: they hold.

Round 311st.decision_summary: R311st: c3c-3 tracked (b) -- migrate the driver's peer-zid plumbing from Option<&[u8]>/&[u8] to the routing Option<Zid>/Zid. The session-layer peer_zid (Vec<u8>) is converted to Zid ONCE at the fan_out read boundary (and the 3 forward read sites), so resolve_source / is_tree_forward_target / is_child / the propagate keep all work in Zid terms (Copy, Eq) instead of re-deriving from raw bytes. Pure behavior-preserving refactor enabled by the sr Zid type; cleans the peer-zid seam F builds on.
changes_bullets: fan_out: the per-face builder callback is now FnMut(FaceId, Option<Zid>) (was Option<&[u8]>); fan_out converts state.actions.peer_zid() (Vec<u8>) -> Option<Zid> via Zid::from_slice at the SINGLE read boundary, so each builder gets a Copy Zid instead of a borrowed byte slice it must re-derive from.

resolve_source(inbound_zid: Option<Zid>, ..) (was Option<&[u8]>): node_id 0 returns inbound_zid? directly (no per-call Zid::from_slice). The 3 forward read sites (forward_push / forward_subscription declare + undeclare) convert peer_zid() -> Option<Zid> at the destructure and pass it (Copy) to BOTH resolve_source and is_tree_forward_target -- the inbound_zid.as_deref() calls are gone.

is_tree_forward_target(zid: Option<Zid>, inbound_zid: Option<Zid>, ..) and is_child(children: &[Zid], zid: Zid) -> children.contains(&zid) (was &[u8] + iter().any(|c| c.as_slice() == zid)). The propagate `keep` closure compares Option<Zid> directly (zid != Some(**z)) instead of via as_slice. is_child is by-value (Zid is Copy), so its three call sites (is_tree_forward_target + the two flood closures) need no textual change.

declare.rs declared_intersects (the SHARED consult behind subscriber + queryable has_matching AND the matching-watch re-evaluation): now splits the published target ONCE into a Vec, then declared.values().any(|c| keyexpr_intersects_target(c, &target_chunks)) -- replacing the inline per-candidate split + keyexpr_intersect_patterns. linkstate_subs.rs matching_peers (the remote linkstate-peer interest scan, called per Push via interested / interested_remote): same shape -- split the target once, scan by_key calling keyexpr_intersects_target per registered subscription, collect + HashSet-dedup the matching peers. The value delivered here is the SSOT SEAM: a future tree is ONE reimplementation site (keyexpr_intersects_target, or both callers swapping their HashMap scan at that one seam) rather than two divergent scans. So (c)'s "with the resource-tree" is intentionally split -- the extraction lands now, the tree stays a tracked PERF deferral.

Round 311sv.decision_summary: R311sv: 4-agent adversarial session review of sr/ss/st/su + remediation. The textbook/SSOT/north-star/cost-no-object question (recurring trigger) fired it; self-assessment was OVERCONFIDENT again. Found a real correctness+SSOT gap (all-zero handshake zid enters the graph unvalidated while the ingest validates -- the exact illegal-state sr targeted -- with the Vec->Zid conversion duplicated 6x), two load-bearing UNTESTED claims (the 2-entry add-delta's receiver-side cross-entry resolution; the candidate-bound branch), a zenoh-fidelity divergence (relink excludes by face-id not zid), stale module docs, and an unrepresentable smell (Details {false,false}). All remediated; M2/R5/m5/m2 declined with rationale.
changes_bullets: R1 (CORRECTNESS+SSOT, convergent 3/4 agents): peer_zid is captured verbatim from the peer INIT body (session_actions.rs:989,1018) -- UNTRUSTED wire data. sr validated the linkstate INGEST but the HANDSHAKE path still used the infallible from_slice, admitting an all-zero zid to the graph as a zero-identity node (the exact illegal-state sr set out to close). New driver SSOT peer_zid_routing(actions)->Option<Zid> via Zid::try_from (rejects empty/all-zero) replaces all 6 peer_zid().map(from_slice) sites (fan_out + 3 forward reads + register). An absent/rejected zid holds the face WITHOUT a routing identity (routes nothing), consistently. Session boundary unchanged (peer_zid() stays Vec<u8>; session-core stays routing-agnostic).

R2 (FIDELITY): flood_link_added now excludes EVERY face whose zid == neighbour from the existing-links delta (zenoh `link.zid != zid`, network.rs:864), not just the new face by id -- a relink to an already-held peer no longer sends that peer's other face a redundant self-links frame. +the b0-gets-nothing assertion.
R3 (UNREPRESENTABLE): Details struct{zid,links} -> enum {Full, LinksOnly, ZidOnly}; make_link_state matches via Details::fields(). The meaningless {false,false} combo is now unconstructible.

R4 (SSOT): graph build_self_links_delta() names the 1-entry [self links-only] delta once; both flood_link_added (relink branch) + flood_self_links_changed call it (was build_linkstate_split(&[],&[self]) twice).
R6 (HONESTY): the stale module doc (claimed "full link-state to every face" -- false since ss) rewritten to the D4 delta split; the runner.rs dead `flood_self` symbol reference reworded.

R7 (COVERAGE): build_link_added_delta_resolves_at_the_receiver feeds the 2-entry delta into a RECEIVER's ingest -- asserts it learns the neighbour AND resolves self's links-only A->C link (the cross-entry psid resolution that is the delta's whole point, previously only byte-shape-tested) + link_added_delta_resolves_regardless_of_entry_order (the docstring's two-pass tolerance claim).
R8 (COVERAGE): the candidate-bound cfg-split pair (intersects_target_candidate_over_depth_* no-alloc no-match / alloc grows), mirroring the existing over_depth_target_* pair.

DECLINED (with rationale): M2 store Zid in session-core remote_peer_zid -- couples session-core (no_std, routing-agnostic) to routing-graph, violating the layering the fidelity reviewer confirmed correct; R1 fixes the duplication driver-side. R5 from_slice debug_assert -- breaks truncation-using test setup (ingest_drops_entry_with_oversized_zid + the sq canonical test feed >16 to from_slice) and risks a demo-config panic; the footgun is contained (R1 routes all untrusted bytes through TryFrom). m5 split target inside the keyexpr helper -- regresses the scan's split-target-once for cosmetic symmetry, no one-off caller (YAGNI). m2 is_child &Zid -- Zid is Copy; by-value in a predicate is idiomatic.

TRACKED (pre-existing, review-surfaced, NOT in scope): the no-alloc wz-session-core build break at query_sink.rs:298 (untouched by these commits) leaves the no-alloc keyexpr_match tests dormant (the new candidate-bound no-alloc assert + the prior over_depth_target_no_alloc); C1o is alloc-only.

Round 311sw.decision_summary: R311sw: BUILD FIX for sr -- zid_hex (the router/peer face-log hex helper, cfg(any(routing-router, routing-peer))) imported the routing-peer-only linkstate_forward::Zid (sr's SSOT-via-Zid::Display), so the routing-ROUTER-only demo build (run-ci Layer E3/E5) failed with error[E0432] unresolved import (Zid is gated behind routing-peer). Reverted zid_hex to direct per-byte hex formatting -- byte-identical output, no coupling to the peer-only type. The per-atom demo gate built only routing-peer + default, never routing-router alone, so the break reached the pre-push full run-ci. Build errors are absolute priority.
changes_bullets: runner.rs zid_hex (the face-log hex helper, cfg(any(routing-router, routing-peer))): removed the `use wz::runtime_tokio::linkstate_forward::Zid` import + the Zid::Display delegation that sr added as an SSOT, and restored the direct per-byte `bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()` formatting. The bug: linkstate_forward (which re-exports Zid) is gated behind `routing-peer`, but zid_hex compiles under routing-router OR routing-peer -- so the routing-ROUTER-only demo build (run-ci Layer E3 / E5) could not resolve the import and failed to compile. zid_hex is a router/peer face-log display helper; it must not couple to the routing-peer-only Zid type. Output is byte-identical (the same wire-order lowercase hex Zid::Display produces), just formatted in place.

Gate gap that let it through: the sr per-atom demo gate built only `--features routing-peer` (where linkstate_forward exists) + default (where zid_hex is cfg'd out entirely), never routing-router ALONE -- so sr's break reached the pre-push full run-ci undetected.
verification_bullets: wz-ap-demo builds clean on ALL 4 routing feature axes now: routing-router (the axis that broke -- E3/E5), routing-routes, routing-peer (E6), and default. Previously only routing-peer + default were gated per-atom, which is exactly how sr's zid_hex break slipped past to the pre-push gate.

Root-cause provenance: the pre-push full run-ci reported Layer E3 FAIL + E5 FAIL, both `error[E0432]: unresolved import wz::runtime_tokio::linkstate_forward` at runner.rs:1108 (zid_hex), with the compiler note `the item is gated behind the routing-peer feature`. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: Session::query + Session::query_aliased signature flipped to `Result<ReplyHandle, QueryAliasError>`. The `#[cfg(not(feature = "query-get"))]` arm returns `Err(QueryAliasError::FeatureDisabled)` (was R311s stub-form `return ReplyHandle::sentinel();`); the `#[cfg(feature = "query-get")]` arm tail wraps the registered handle in `Ok(handle)`. The R311s doc-comment claims about "stub-form fall-through to a sentinel ReplyHandle(0) to avoid ~22-callsite churn" + "future round may promote to Result-form" rewritten to record the R311t realisation of that promotion and the honest-signal rationale (silent rid=0 fall-through was an anti-pattern matching the doc-around-hack memory anchor — callers that did not check the rid would silently misfile replies into a non-registration).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: Session::query_aliased_auto inner delegate cleaned — the `#[cfg(feature = "query-get")]` arm previously wrapped `Ok(self.query_aliased(...))` because query_aliased returned ReplyHandle; with query_aliased now returning `Result<ReplyHandle, QueryAliasError>` the inner call propagates directly as the function-tail expression (no double-wrap). doc-comment updated to record the R311t propagation contract.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: Querier::get signature flipped to `Result<ReplyHandle, QueryAliasError>`; body unchanged (still delegates to `self.session.query(...)` which now propagates the Result directly). QuerierAliased::get unchanged (already returned `Result<_, QueryAliasError>` for the R242 UnknownMapping signal). Both impl doc-comments updated to record the R311t FeatureDisabled-OFF-arm propagation contract.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: QueryAliasError struct doc-comment rewritten — the R311s claims "Currently unused by the type-ungated declare/query paths" + "those use the stub-form fall-through to a sentinel ReplyHandle(0)" + "variant exists for the future round that may switch Session::query and Querier::get to Result-form" all retracted. New text records the R311t realisation: FeatureDisabled is active across all five entry points (Session::query, query_aliased, query_aliased_auto, Querier::get, QuerierAliased::get) and callers branch uniformly on the same enum across consumer-feature subsets.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: declare_querier + declare_querier_aliased doc-comments updated — the R311s notes describing the ".get path hits the stub-form fall-through to a sentinel ReplyHandle(0)" rewritten to record the R311t Result-form transition ("returns Err(QueryAliasError::FeatureDisabled) via Session::query/query_aliased_auto's OFF arm — no wire frame, no callback registration").

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: Querier struct doc-comment + the line-75 wz_runtime_core::TimeSource import comment + the line-113 crate::reply imports doc-block all reworded to describe ReplyHandle as the "inner success value" of Session::query's Result return rather than the previous "direct return value flowing through the stub-form sentinel" framing.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/reply.rs: ReplyHandle::sentinel() crate-private constructor removed (the cfg-gated `pub(crate) fn sentinel() -> Self { ReplyHandle(0) }` block + its multi-line doc-comment about the rid=0 out-of-band signal). With R311t Session::query's OFF arm returning `Err(FeatureDisabled)` the constructor has no caller and dead-code lint would have flagged it; removing it eliminates the rid=0 sentinel pattern entirely.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs: 22 internal test callsites of Session::query (17) + Session::query_aliased (5) now suffixed with `.expect("query-get feature is ON in this test build")`. The 1 querier.get(&clock, |_| {}, |_| {}); single-line call inside querier_get_threads_target_option_into_wire was split to multi-line + `.expect()`. The 5 `let h0 = ... query(...)` / `let h1 = ... query(...)` / `let h0 = querier.get(...)` / `let h1 = querier.get(...)` / `let q1 = querier.clone().get(...)` / `let q2 = clone.get(...)` bindings were split to multi-line method-chain form `.expect(...)` so the subsequent `.rid()` calls stay typed as ReplyHandle. The expectation message is uniform across all sites — the test target builds with default features which forces `query-get` ON, so the OFF arm is unreachable from those test bodies.
verification_bullets: cargo check 7-lane clean: default-features build OK; --no-default-features OK; --no-default-features --features=query-get OK; --no-default-features --features=query-queryable OK; --no-default-features --features=liveliness-token OK; --no-default-features --features=liveliness-subscriber OK; --no-default-features --features=declare-queryable OK; --no-default-features --features=declare-subscriber OK. The query-get OFF lane is the load-bearing one for the R311t change — it confirms that `Err(QueryAliasError::FeatureDisabled)` compiles cleanly through Session::query, Session::query_aliased, Session::query_aliased_auto, Querier::get, and QuerierAliased::get without any cfg-cascade gap.

    )
    .expect("...");` — the auto-reformat is the canonical Rust idiom and matches the R311s/R311q/R311r style for cfg-elided method chains.

Round 311v.decision_summary: R311v QueryEvent.attachment extraction. Inbound Query extension chain (ext_id 0x05, ExtZbuf) decoded to Option<&[u8]> view threaded through fire_matching_queryables; R311r carry closed.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: new module-private free function `fn extract_query_attachment(query: &Query) -> Option<&[u8]>` walks `query.extensions.as_ref()` and matches each `ExtEntry` against the zenoh-pico query-attachment wire shape (`ext_id == 0x05` low-nibble of header + `body == ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf`). First matching entry's `zbuf.value.as_slice()` is returned; absent extensions vec or no-attachment chain yields `None`. The mandatory bit (`_Z_MSG_EXT_FLAG_M = 0x10`) is intentionally NOT required to match because zenoh-pico's `_z_query_decode_extensions` falls into the `default` arm silently when M is clear (no `_z_msg_ext_unknown_error`), which is the encode-side behaviour we mirror at decode-side.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: `fire_matching_queryables` body augmented — the existing `let parameters_view = query.parameters.as_deref();` line is followed by `let attachment_view = extract_query_attachment(query);` so the view is computed ONCE per inbound query (the chain walk is O(n) on ext count which the zenoh wire format caps at 8 per `Query::decode` line 109). The `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: None, ... }` literal inside the matched-queryable loop body becomes `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: attachment_view, ... }`. The closure body's R311r doc-comment carry note ("attachment extraction from the extensions chain is a future round") rewritten to record the R311v closure ("the attachment view is extracted from the inbound extensions chain at R311v").

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: imports gain `use wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntryVariant;` (the helper pattern-matches on the variant; the `ExtEntry` struct itself reaches the helper transitively through `Query.extensions: Option<Vec<ExtEntry>>` so it does not need a separate import at the module-prologue level — only the variant constants need direct reference). No new cfg-gates introduced; the helper compiles in every consumer-feature subset because `wz_codecs::ext_entry` is unconditionally part of the wz-codecs surface.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests module gains 2 new tests + 1 helper. `request_query_with_attachment(rid, suffix, attachment)` constructs a `Request` whose body is a `Query` carrying a single `ExtEntry` shaped per the zenoh-pico encode path (`ext.set_ext_id(0x05); ext.set_enc(2); ext.body = ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf(ExtZbuf { value_len: attachment.len() as u64, value: attachment.to_vec() })`), plus `query.header |= 0x80` so a hypothetical round-trip through `Query::decode` would re-surface the chain. `dispatch_threads_attachment_into_query_event_callback` registers a queryable on `home/temp`, dispatches an attachment-bearing Query, and asserts the captured `event.attachment.map(<[u8]>::to_vec)` equals `b"hello-att"[..]`. `dispatch_query_without_extensions_threads_none_attachment` initialises the capture slot non-None (`Some(b"dirty".to_vec())`) so an accidental skipped-write would surface as a false positive, then dispatches a no-extensions Query and asserts the slot is None.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests-module imports expanded — `std::sync::Mutex` joins the existing `std::sync::Arc` import (the new tests' capture pattern needs interior mutability across the move-closure boundary). `wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntry` + `wz_codecs::ext_zbuf::ExtZbuf` are imported for the helper's construction path (the variant import `ExtEntryVariant` reaches the helper through the `use super::*` at the test module head).
verification_bullets: cargo check 7-lane clean: default + --no-default-features + 6 single-feature lanes (query-get / query-queryable / liveliness-token / liveliness-subscriber / declare-queryable / declare-subscriber). All lanes finish without warnings; the new helper compiles unconditionally because wz-codecs ext_entry / ext_zbuf are not feature-gated.

cargo test --workspace: 763 passed / 0 failed (R311t baseline 761 + R311v's 2 attachment tests — dispatch_threads_attachment_into_query_event_callback + dispatch_query_without_extensions_threads_none_attachment).

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean after one struct-init rewrite (the initial `let mut query = Query::default(); query.extensions = Some(vec![ext]);` pattern tripped `field_reassign_with_default`; rewrote as `let query = Query { header: Query::default().header | 0x80, extensions: Some(vec![ext]), ..Query::default() }` per the clippy suggestion).
cargo fmt --all --check: clean (no auto-reformat pass needed for the new code; the helper + tests landed already in canonical rustfmt shape).

Layer E 30-trial × 3 flake-0: wz_queryable_round_trip 30/30 (load-bearing for R311v — the attachment-extraction path now fires on the queryable wire path), wz_publisher_to_zsub 30/30, wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip 30/30. Total 90/90 trials — the new extraction logic did not regress the wire round-trip paths.
carry_forward_bullets: ReplyEmitter PhantomData arm awkward (R311r design trade-off, low priority) — compile-time scaffolding only, never reached at runtime. Rework worth considering once Session<R,T> reparam pivot is on the table since the reparameterisation may surface a cleaner shape.

Session<R,T> reparam pivot (R267 architectural carry; ratifiable once all atomic feature elide is confirmed clean across the type-ungated surface — R311o through R311t took the surface to the point where the pivot is on the critical path again, and R311v leaves that observation undisturbed).
Phase W lwIP runtime crate (long-standing architectural carry; multi-round work, no R311 series interaction).

R311n measurement re-run for the post-R311t/v cumulative catalog truthfulness gate: scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh against the codec-frame / codec-declare / codec-request / codec-response / minus-all-codecs / handshake-only lanes. R311t/v added no new wire-codec footprint so the measurement is opt-in confirmation, not a blocking gate.

Attachment SourceInfo + Payload ext mirror — R311v extracts only the 0x05 attachment ext from the Query body. Query body also carries 0x01 (SourceInfo) and 0x03 (Payload) ext shapes per zenoh-pico `_z_query_encode_ext` lines 430-449. The wz consumer surface currently exposes neither through QueryEvent; future round adds those when the wz keyexpr v1 spec surfaces application-level needs.

Reply / Push attachment parity — the attachment ext on Reply (0x05) and Push body (0x03) wire shape is symmetric to the Query-side extraction landed here. The Reply / Push side currently surfaces attachment through Sample.attachment for Push (R232) but the Reply side's InboundReply.attachment is the next analogue to wire up. publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: new module-private free function `fn extract_query_attachment(query: &Query) -> Option<&[u8]>` walks `query.extensions.as_ref()` and matches each `ExtEntry` against the zenoh-pico query-attachment wire shape (`ext_id == 0x05` low-nibble of header + `body == ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf`). First matching entry's `zbuf.value.as_slice()` is returned; absent extensions vec or no-attachment chain yields `None`. The mandatory bit (`_Z_MSG_EXT_FLAG_M = 0x10`) is intentionally NOT required to match because zenoh-pico's `_z_query_decode_extensions` falls into the `default` arm silently when M is clear (no `_z_msg_ext_unknown_error`), which is the encode-side behaviour we mirror at decode-side.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: `fire_matching_queryables` body augmented — the existing `let parameters_view = query.parameters.as_deref();` line is followed by `let attachment_view = extract_query_attachment(query);` so the view is computed ONCE per inbound query (the chain walk is O(n) on ext count which the zenoh wire format caps at 8 per `Query::decode` line 109). The `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: None, ... }` literal inside the matched-queryable loop body becomes `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: attachment_view, ... }`. The closure body's R311r doc-comment carry note ("attachment extraction from the extensions chain is a future round") rewritten to record the R311v closure ("the attachment view is extracted from the inbound extensions chain at R311v").

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: imports gain `use wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntryVariant;` (the helper pattern-matches on the variant; the `ExtEntry` struct itself reaches the helper transitively through `Query.extensions: Option<Vec<ExtEntry>>` so it does not need a separate import at the module-prologue level — only the variant constants need direct reference). No new cfg-gates introduced; the helper compiles in every consumer-feature subset because `wz_codecs::ext_entry` is unconditionally part of the wz-codecs surface.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests module gains 2 new tests + 1 helper. `request_query_with_attachment(rid, suffix, attachment)` constructs a `Request` whose body is a `Query` carrying a single `ExtEntry` shaped per the zenoh-pico encode path (`ext.set_ext_id(0x05); ext.set_enc(2); ext.body = ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf(ExtZbuf { value_len: attachment.len() as u64, value: attachment.to_vec() })`), plus `query.header |= 0x80` so a hypothetical round-trip through `Query::decode` would re-surface the chain. `dispatch_threads_attachment_into_query_event_callback` registers a queryable on `home/temp`, dispatches an attachment-bearing Query, and asserts the captured `event.attachment.map(<[u8]>::to_vec)` equals `b"hello-att"[..]`. `dispatch_query_without_extensions_threads_none_attachment` initialises the capture slot non-None (`Some(b"dirty".to_vec())`) so an accidental skipped-write would surface as a false positive, then dispatches a no-extensions Query and asserts the slot is None.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests-module imports expanded — `std::sync::Mutex` joins the existing `std::sync::Arc` import (the new tests' capture pattern needs interior mutability across the move-closure boundary). `wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntry` + `wz_codecs::ext_zbuf::ExtZbuf` are imported for the helper's construction path (the variant import `ExtEntryVariant` reaches the helper through the `use super::*` at the test module head).

SCE codegen template bug workaround in build.rs post-process: SCE emits `#![doc = "SCE-MAP: stem:line"]` as a file-leading inner attribute. When wz includes the file inside `pub mod X { include!(...); }`, rust rejects (E0658 / inner-attribute-not-permitted at item position). SCE's own `cargo test -p sce-forge-runtime --features alloc` hits the same wall — verified R40. changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_fsm_coverage.rs (~250 lines): single mega-test r61_full_coverage_sequential walks 11 scenarios covering every transition edge in session_fsm_unicast.scxml outside the R59 happy path — listener path (Init→AwaitingInitSyn→SentInitAck→SentOpenAck→Established), all 4 close-reason setters (Generic / Invalid / Expired / Unresponsive), all 5 close-from-state edges (LinkOpening / Opening.SentInitSyn / Opening / Established / Accepting), all 3 direct-to-Closed edges (link.lost from LinkOpening, peer.close from Established, link.lost from Accepting).

fresh_engine() helper isolates each scenario via rebind_session_actions_for_test (R60 feature-gated path); a fresh Driver + Actions triple resets every counter to zero between scenarios while INSTALLED OnceLock stays at its first-install pointer.

Single mega-test on purpose: cargo's thread-parallel runner races concurrent rebind_session_actions_for_test calls against the process-global Lua-engine global function namespace. Sequential dispatch in one test fn is the only race-safe shape until R60 carry on session-scoped Lua binding lands. Initially split into 11 #[test] fns and observed 9/11 races; consolidated to one fn after diagnosis.

Each scenario asserts (a) Engine::get_current_state matches the SCXML target state, (b) trace.close_reason discriminator matches the set_close_reason_* action the transition runs, (c) send_close_frame_with_reason counter increments only on Closing-routed paths (not on direct-to-Closed via link.lost / peer.close).

Round 70.decision_summary: Crypto safety hardening — SigningKey newtype + Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> drop-wipe + RFC 4231 HMAC-SHA256 test vectors. Closes the 3rd-review #4 crypto-secret-in-plain-memory defect.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: zeroize = '1' with zeroize_derive feature added. RustCrypto-ecosystem standard for cryptographic secret lifecycle.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: new SigningKey struct wrapping Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>; SigningKey::new(bytes) validates >= 32 bytes at construct (RFC §5.M) and returns Err(SigningKeyTooShort) instead of panicking at HMAC site. Drop wipes the heap allocation — cookie key bytes no longer linger in core dumps / heap-leak windows / panic backtraces.

Manual Debug impl on SigningKey: shows length + literal '<redacted>' for bytes. Prevents log / panic stack-trace leakage; a regression to #[derive(Debug)] would surface in `signing_key_debug_redacts_bytes` test.
SessionInitParams::cookie_signing_key field type Vec<u8> → SigningKey. for_test fixture + integration test fixture_params both construct via SigningKey::new.

generate_cookie_hmac_sha256 split: pure compute_hmac_sha256_full(key, data) -> [u8; 32] primitive separate from the 16-byte wire truncation. The split lets RFC 4231 test vectors cross-check the underlying HMAC without entangling the cookie-truncation slice.
2 new RFC 4231 test cases (TC1 + TC2) cross-check against the canonical HMAC-SHA256 vectors. If RustCrypto's hmac/sha2 ever regresses on us the assertion fires loud.
Removed signing_key_short_panics test; replaced with signing_key_short_returns_err matching the new typed-error path.

Round 82.decision_summary: R74 Frame.payload application-layer dispatch — parse_frame_payload + NetworkMessage{Request, Unknown}; DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload replaces the silent payload-drop in poll_and_dispatch_one's Frame arm.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: NetworkMessage enum (Request(Box<wz_codecs::request::Request>) / Unknown { mid, body }) + parse_frame_payload(bytes) -> Result<Vec<NetworkMessage>, CodecError> helper that loops over the Frame.payload batch, dispatching N_MID_REQUEST (0x1C) to wz_codecs::request::Request::decode and absorbing other MIDs as Unknown { mid, body } that terminates the batch loop (no length-aware decoder for unknown bodies means cursor cannot safely advance past them).

DriverLoopOutcome gains FramePayload { reliable, sn, messages, has_ext, extensions } variant; SideEffectOnly is now KeepAlive-only. The prior #[derive(Debug)] is replaced by manual Debug impls on both DriverLoopOutcome and NetworkMessage because wz-codecs structs (Request / ExtEntry) only derive Default per sce-codegen output — the manual impl prints variant kind + ext_count + body_len without recursing into codec fields so existing {outcome:?} test assertions keep working.

poll_and_dispatch_one Frame arm rewired: previously bucketed under None -> DriverLoopOutcome::SideEffectOnly (payload silently dropped). Now matches InboundFrame::Frame fields, runs parse_frame_payload, surfaces FramePayload on Ok or ParseError(InboundParseError::Codec) + Engine::process_event(E::FramingError) on Err. Application-layer parse failure is conservatively treated as a transport-FSM framing.error so the session moves to Closing on malformed batch payload (revisitable per carry).

inbound_to_fsm_event docstring extended: Frame None branch now documents 'application-layer dispatch via parse_frame_payload' instead of 'drop'. KeepAlive None branch unchanged. The function itself still returns None for both — the dispatch fan-out lives in poll_and_dispatch_one.

wire_const::N_MID_REQUEST (0x1C) constant added. The other 6 network MIDs (PUSH 0x1D, RESPONSE 0x1B, DECLARE 0x1E, OAM 0x1F, RESPONSE_FINAL 0x1A, INTEREST 0x19 per zenoh-pico network.h:33-39) are documented in NetworkMessage rustdoc but not declared as constants until their decoders land — YAGNI per the existing wire_const philosophy where every named constant has at least one match-arm consumer.

Tests added — 4 parse_frame_payload unit tests in session_fsm_inbound_dispatch.rs: empty payload returns empty Vec; Unknown MID (0x1D) absorbs remainder; Request envelope MID 0x1C dispatches to Request::decode (first record is Request); truncated Request body returns CodecError. 3 r74_* poll_and_dispatch_one integration scenarios in session_fsm_driver_loop.rs: empty-payload Frame surfaces FramePayload{messages=[]}, Unknown-MID payload surfaces FramePayload{messages=[Unknown{mid:0x1D, body}]}, malformed Request payload surfaces ParseError + FSM transitions SentInitSyn -> Closing.

Closes R73 + R76 carry 'Application-layer Frame payload dispatch (R74-tier) — DriverLoopOutcome::SideEffectOnly variant on Frame currently drops the payload; downstream consumer needs the msg_put/del/query/response codec dispatch'. The dispatch wiring is now in place; envelope codec coverage remains REQUEST-only until SCE Push/Response/Declare/OAM/Interest SCXMLs land.

wz_codecs::request encode/decode byte-count discrepancy discovered empirically: Request::default() with header=0x1C encodes N bytes that Request::decode consumes M < N. The R74 batch loop absorbs the residual as Unknown rather than misinterpreting it. The unit test parse_frame_payload_dispatches_request_mid_to_request_decoder asserts 'first record is Request' (parsed[0]) instead of strict parsed.len()==1; the discrepancy is documented in carry forward as a wz-codecs/sce-codegen issue out of R74 scope.

carry_forward_bullets: wz_codecs::request encode/decode roundtrip discrepancy — Request::default() with header=0x1C produces bytes where Request::decode consumes a different (smaller) byte count, leaving residual bytes that the R74 batch loop absorbs as Unknown. The contract should be 'encode then decode consumes exactly the encoded bytes' regardless of state. Likely root cause: Wireexpr default-state encode/decode mismatch OR RequestVariant Default-arm tag round-trip. A focused round on the wz-codecs codegen or Wireexpr default state would close this; without it, real production Request payloads (where header is set and inner body is meaningful) may roundtrip cleanly, but the codec contract is currently soft on default state.

Network-envelope codec coverage — wz_codecs::request is the only authored envelope. The other 6 network MIDs (PUSH 0x1D, RESPONSE 0x1B, DECLARE 0x1E, OAM 0x1F, RESPONSE_FINAL 0x1A, INTEREST 0x19) decode as Unknown until their SCE codec SCXMLs land. PUSH is the highest-priority next target (pub/sub data path = put/del without request-reply correlation); RESPONSE follows for request-reply parity. Each new envelope codec round bumps a wire_const::N_MID_* constant and adds a parse_frame_payload match arm.

Application-layer parse error -> transport FramingError mapping conservative — R74 treats any CodecError inside parse_frame_payload as a transport FramingError that closes the session. Stricter wire-spec reading might preserve the session and only log application-layer batch failures (the Frame transport envelope itself parsed OK). Revisit if production deploys need batch resilience or if integration testing surfaces sessions closing on transient app-layer noise.

FramePayload outcome not yet consumed by drive_session_until_terminal — R81's loop discards the per-iteration DriverLoopOutcome (matches all variants with `=> {}`). A future round (composing on R81 carry #4 'per-iteration observer callback') wires FramePayload.messages to a consumer registry — pub/sub topic dispatcher / Lua bridge / Rust callback. Without that wiring, R74 surfaces the payload at the API boundary but no one reads it yet.

carry_forward_bullets: Established.onexit does NOT clear established_at — if the FSM reaches Closed and a fresh handshake is attempted on the same SessionLinkActions instance (uncommon but theoretically possible), the stale established_at would skew the lease window. Current architecture assumes one SessionLinkActions per session lifetime (the SCE upstream-fixed singleton retirement landed in R79), so this is not a hot defect — but a future session-reuse scenario would need an onexit clear. Defer until session reuse is on the roadmap.

Lease comparator semantic question — session-fsm §2.5 reads as 'lease resets on KeepAlive', which matches max(established_at, keepalive). But strict zenoh-pico parity may want 'last KeepAlive only OR established_at as fallback' (NOT max — treat them as fallback chain). The semantic difference shows up when KeepAlive is OLDER than established_at (unusual but possible if KeepAlive arrived before handshake completed somehow). R84 ships max() which is the most defensive (latest stamp wins); revisit if upstream wire-spec discussions surface a stricter contract.

Multi-instance test isolation now safe — the R79 per-instance ScriptEngine DI migration means each fresh_setup() gets its own Lua engine, so record_established_at's `*established_at.lock() = Some(Instant::now())` body doesn't race across parallel tests. This was a real risk pre-R79 (the singleton INSTALLED OnceLock would have caused cross-test interference); R79's foresight pays off here.

Outbound-half observer (R83 carry #4) still open — R83 wires inbound poll + lease observer, R84 closes the established_at gap, but the outbound TX path (record_established_at is technically state-internal not TX, so it's in scope; but send_init_syn / send_open_ack etc. have no symmetric observer) remains unobservable from the application layer. A symmetric outbound observer round would close the full telemetry surface.

carry_forward_bullets: Cookie verification on inbound OpenSyn — R86 closes the OUTBOUND cookie binding (Accepting side mints HMAC-bound cookie on InitAck). The INBOUND side (Accepting-side OpenSyn cookie verification) still trusts the peer's echoed cookie blindly (R57's guard_fns just returns true for cookie_valid). RFC §5.M requires the Accepting side to re-HMAC peer_zid with the same cookie_signing_key on OpenSyn arrival and compare against body.cookie. A follow-up round wires that verification through the cookie_valid guard.

inbound_peer_zid stale across handshake retries — R86's slot is populated once on InitSyn arrival but never cleared. A retry scenario where the FSM goes back to AwaitingInitSyn (currently NOT a wire-spec edge, but theoretically possible if a future round adds inbound.restart) would see stale peer_zid. Defensive: clear the slot on AwaitingInitSyn entry. Defer until the retry edge is on the roadmap.

Cookie ext-chain extension — R86 produces the 16-byte HMAC cookie in body.cookie. RFC §5.M also allows the cookie to carry additional MAC material via the ext chain (HMAC ext entry, deploy-specific anti-amplification token). The ext_chain_for(ExtChainRole::InitAck) slot is already wired (R68b); composing the HMAC into the ext chain is a separate extension point not covered by R86.

Initiator-side cookie verification — the Initiator (sending InitSyn) receives the Accepting side's InitAck cookie via inbound_cookie capture (R62). The Initiator echoes that cookie verbatim in OpenSyn (R57 caller-owned cookie field). Both sides should ideally re-derive the cookie locally and compare — but the Initiator doesn't know the cookie_signing_key (only the Accepting side does). So echo-only is the correct contract on the Initiator side; R86 only addresses the Accepting-side mint path.

Round 87.decision_summary: R87 debt repayment — R82's "first record is Request" workaround replaced with exact-byte-count round-trip Request construction; assertions strengthened to parsed.len()==1, and the previously-removed Request+Unknown chain test restored.
changes_bullets: Root cause identified for the R82 codec discrepancy: `RequestVariant::default()` returns `CodecZenohMsgPut(MsgPut::default())` per sce-codegen's 'pick first variant' rule, but `MsgPut::default().header = 0` (low-5 MID = 0) causes Request::decode's inner-MID dispatch (line 102 of generated request.rs: `match (peek >> 0) & 0x1F { 1=>MsgPut, 2=>MsgDel, 3=>Query, other=>Default{tag:other, body:Query} }`) to route to the Default arm with Query::decode. Encode wrote MsgPut bytes; decode read Query bytes. The discrepancy is a sce-codegen Default-arm self-inconsistency on the codec output, NOT a real wire-spec bug — production callers construct Request with explicit body, not Default.

The fix is a test-side construction discipline: build Request with `body: RequestVariant::Default { tag: 0, body: Query::default() }` so encode and decode use the same arm (Default arm) and the same inner codec (Query::default round-trips in 1 byte; Wireexpr::default round-trips in 1 byte). Total round-trip-safe wire: header(1) + rid_vle(1) + wireexpr(1) + query_default(1) = 4 bytes exact.

Rustdoc inside the test documents the codegen-Default corner so the construction discipline is preserved when future codecs are added.

This test was REMOVED from the original R82 commit because the default-state mismatch produced unpredictable residual bytes that polluted the chain assertion. With the R87 construction, the chain test asserts `parsed.len() == 2` (Request envelope + Unknown absorbing tail) and validates the Unknown.body byte equality.

The discovered codegen corner (Default impl picks first variant + MsgPut::default.header == 0 ≠ msg_put MID 1) is documented as a separate SCE upstream concern; wz-side tests now bypass it by explicit body construction. No wz-codecs change needed for production correctness.

End-to-end RFC §5.M cookie binding closure: (1) InitSyn arrives -> handle_inbound captures peer_zid (R86); (2) SentInitAck.onentry -> send_init_ack_with_cookie computes HMAC(key, peer_zid)[..16] and embeds in InitAck wire (R86); (3) Initiator echoes cookie back in OpenSyn (Initiator-side R62 chain); (4) OpenSyn arrives -> handle_inbound captures echoed cookie (R89); (5) cookie_valid() re-HMACs and compares (R89); (6) match -> FSM advances to SentOpenAck, mismatch -> stuck at SentInitAck.
carry_forward_bullets: Constant-time comparison — R89 uses standard byte-equality (==) for the HMAC compare. For a single-peer test fixture this is fine; production hardening against timing oracles would swap to subtle::ConstantTimeEq. Defer until a security review surfaces a timing-side-channel concern in the deploy.yaml scope (mostly an issue for multi-tenant routers, less so for embedded AP pairings).

Slot lifetime / replay defense — R89 captures the inbound_opensyn_cookie slot once on each OpenSyn arrival and overwrites on subsequent arrivals. A replay attack (peer re-sends a stale OpenSyn) is possible if the FSM ever revisits SentInitAck. Current session-fsm doesn't have a SentInitAck re-entry edge so this is theoretical; a defensive clear-on-exit hook (similar to R84's established_at carry #1) would close it preemptively.

Cookie ext-chain MAC material — RFC §5.M allows additional MAC carriers in the cookie ext-chain. R89 verifies the base 16-byte HMAC only. The ext-chain extension point lives in `ext_chain_for(ExtChainRole::InitAck)` (R68b slot) but isn't HMAC-composed yet. Out of R89 scope.

half_open_cap_available + accept_rate_token guards still R57 placeholders (bind_bool true). bind_guard infrastructure from R89 now exists, so retiring those placeholders is a 2-line change once cap-quota / token-bucket implementations land. Defer until DoS-mitigation rounds.

Initiator-side cookie verification absent — R89 is Accepting-side. The Initiator receives the Accepting side's cookie via InitAck and echoes it verbatim on OpenSyn. The Initiator cannot verify the cookie itself (only the Accepting side holds cookie_signing_key); echo-only is the correct contract per RFC §5.M. No carry needed — explicitly NOT a gap.

Round 98.decision_summary: R98 lands the application-layer subscriber registry — closes R90 carry #4, AP MVP critical-path unblock; deliberate pivot away from the next codec round (DECLARE 0x1E) because pub/sub demo value-add exceeds 7/7 MID catalog vanity, and DECLARE's 9-sub-codec chain is a multi-round project on the scale of RESPONSE chain (R95-R97).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs new — `SubscriberRegistry` with register / unregister / dispatch / len / is_empty / Default. Callbacks are `Box<dyn FnMut(&Push) + Send + 'static>`; subscription handles are opaque `SubscriptionId(u64)` so callers can hold a stable removal key without depending on keyexpr equality (duplicate keyexpr literals are explicitly allowed). Registry is `!Sync` by design — cross-task sharing is the caller's responsibility via `Arc<Mutex<…>>` to keep the hot dispatch path mutex-free in single-owner cases.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs declares `pub mod pubsub` after session_glue.

Dispatch scope (R98): Push only, literal keyexpr matching on `Push.keyexpr.suffix` when `Push.keyexpr.id == 0`. Non-Push variants and mapping-id pushes (`id != 0`) are filtered out at dispatch time. Module + struct + each method carry doc comments explaining the scope limits and the DECLARE-table dependency that future rounds will close.

6 inline unit tests cover the dispatch matrix: (1) matching keyexpr fires callback, (2) non-matching keyexpr skips, (3) multiple matching subscribers fire in registration order, (4) non-zero mapping id is filtered out (deferred DECLARE), (5) non-Push variants (ResponseFinal here) are no-ops, (6) unregister is idempotent and returns false on missing id.

Test helper `push_with_keyexpr` constructs a Push whose Wireexpr embed has id=0 + inline suffix — mirrors the on-wire shape of a router-less pub/sub setup where the publisher has not yet performed a DECLARE handshake (the dominant AP MVP demo configuration).
